The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sector-Wide Approach (SWAp) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include Project Management Office (PMO) to provide oversight for the Digital Transformation Project of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA). data.title: Hiring of a Project Manager for PIU
data.project_name: Support for Preparation of the Modernizing Ethiopia’s Statistical System Project
data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (EOI)

Individual Consultant Selection (INDV)

Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS)

Project:-Modernizing Ethiopia’s Statistical System Project (MESSP) – Preparation Grant for Modernizing Ethiopia’s Statistical System Project 

Project ID:-P516394 Grant No. E6970-ET 

Assignment Title:- Hiring of a Project Manager for PIU

Reference No.ET-ESS-574077-CS-INDV

1. Background

The Ethiopian Statistical Service (ESS) has received financing from the World Bank and intends to apply part of the proceeds to recruit an individual consultant under the Individual Consultant Selection (INDV) method.

The project aims to improve the availability, quality, timeliness, and use of official statistics for evidence-based policymaking in Ethiopia. ESS will establish a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) responsible for day-to-day implementation, including coordination, procurement, financial management, monitoring and evaluation, environmental and social risk management, reporting, annual work planning and budgeting, procurement planning, and liaison with the World Bank and key stakeholders.

 2. Assignment Objective

The Project Manager will provide overall leadership and management of the PIU to ensure effective, efficient, and compliant implementation of project activities in accordance with the Financing Agreement, Project Implementation Manual, annual work plans, procurement plans, fiduciary requirements, environmental and social commitments, and World Bank procedures.

3. Scope of Services / Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager shall, among other duties:

- Provide overall strategic leadership, direction, and management of the project. 

- Coordinate the preparation and implementation of annual work plans, procurement plans, training plans, ICT modernization plans, and project budgets. 

- Ensure timely implementation of project activities in accordance with approved project documents, financing agreements, and implementation schedules. 

- Lead and coordinate digital transformation and ICT modernization initiatives under the project, aligned with ESS strategic priorities and national digital transformation agendas. 

- Coordinate technical, fiduciary, safeguards, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), ICT, and administrative functions of the PIU. 

- Serve as the primary liaison between ESS and key institutions including the Ministry of Finance (MoF), Ministry of Planning and Development (MoPD), sector ministries, development partners, and the World Bank. 

- Ensure compliance with World Bank procurement, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, digital governance, cyber security, and reporting requirements. 

- Supervise consultants, specialists, and support staff recruited under the project, including ICT and digital transformation specialists. 

- Facilitate coordination with sector institutions to strengthen data integration, interoperability, and administrative data systems. 

- Lead the preparation and submission of quarterly, semi-annual, and annual project progress reports. 

- Organize and coordinate Steering Committee and Technical Committee meetings. 

- Monitor project implementation progress and recommend corrective actions where necessary. 

- Identify project risks (including ICT-related risks) and oversee mitigation measures. 

- Ensure stakeholder engagement, communication, and change management activities. 

- Perform any other related duties assigned by ESS management.

4. Duration and Duty Station

Duration:-18 months, full-time, subject to satisfactory performance and project requirements. 

-Duty Station:-ESS Headquarters, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

The project preparation phase will be up to eighteen (18) months from the date of hiring. Implementation is expected to commence upon Project Effectiveness and continue for approximately five (5) years, with possible overlap between preparation and implementation phases.)

5. Minimum Qualifications and Experience

Education:-

- Master’s degree or above in Statistics, Economics, Information Systems, Computer Science, Public Administration, Project Management, Development Studies, ICT for Development, or related field.

Professional Experience:

- Minimum ten (10) years of relevant professional experience, including at least five (5) years in project coordination/management/program management roles. 

- Demonstrated experience managing large-scale, multi-stakeholder, donor-funded development projects. 

- Proven experience coordinating and implementing World Bank-financed projects is mandatory (experience with other multilateral/bilateral donors is an added advantage). 

- Demonstrated experience in ICT modernization, digital transformation, e-government, statistical modernization, or data system strengthening initiatives. 

- Strong understanding of digital technologies, data ecosystems, information systems, administrative data integration, interoperability frameworks, and digital governance principles. 

- Proven experience working with PIU and managing multidisciplinary teams (procurement, financial management, safeguards, ICT, and M&E). 

- Strong knowledge of World Bank operational policies and procedures including procurement, financial management, safeguards, M&E, and reporting requirements. 

- Experience with national statistical systems and public sector institutions is highly desirable.

6. Selection Method

The consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers – Selection of Individual Consultants (INDV) method.

7. Submission of Expression of Interest

Interested candidates shall submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) and an updated CV including relevant qualifications and experience, electronically no later than:

Deadline: November 13, 2026 at 5:30 PM (Ethiopia Time)

Project ID: P508698

Credit/Financing No: IDA 79300-TZ

Grant/Trust Fund No.:  TFC9664

Procurement Plan Reference No.: TZ-MOW-545525-CS-QCBS

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Aquifer Mapping in Five Water Basins, and the Design, Development, and Implementation of a National Groundwater Information System and an Online Groundwater Licensing and Permitting Portal.

1. The Government of the United Republic of Tanzania has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program (SRWSSP, Phase II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include Consultancy Services for Aquifer Mapping in Five Water Basins, and the Design, Development, and Implementation of a National Groundwater Information System and an Online Groundwater Licensing and Permitting Portal. The objective of the assignment is to strengthen groundwater resources management in Tanzania through completion of aquifer mapping in five target Basin Water Boards, enhancement of groundwater monitoring systems, upgrading of the national groundwater information system, and modernization of groundwater licensing and permitting processes. The Consultant shall undertake technical, institutional, and digital systems interventions to support sustainable groundwater management in the five target Basin Water Boards. The assignment will be undertaken within a period of twelve (12) months.

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website:

(https://www.maji.go.tz/announcements/consultancy-services-for-aquifer-mapping-in-five-b).

4. The Ministry of Water invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Design, Development, and Implementation of a National Groundwater Information System, Online Groundwater Licensing and Permitting Portal
  • Conducted national or basin-scale aquifer mapping and groundwater resource assessment;
  • Groundwater quality assessment, hydrochemistry, and environmental risk mapping;
  • Hydrogeological investigations in complex geological terrains, including fractured basement, sedimentary, volcanic, and alluvial aquifer systems
  • The firm shall demonstrate at least ten (10) years of proven experience in undertaking assignments of varying nature and complexity, with at least three (3) successfully completed assignments, each valued at not less than TZS 2 billion. For each referenced assignment, the Consultant should provide the assignment title, client’s name and contact details, country, contract dates, contract value, consultant’s contractual role, proportion undertaken where the assignment was performed in association, brief description of services, and evidence of successful completion or substantial completion.
  • The Consultant shall demonstrate adequate technical and managerial capability to undertake a multi-disciplinary, multi-basin assignment, including its organizational structure, relevant permanent professional capacity, quality-assurance arrangements and experience coordinating multidisciplinary and multi-location consulting teams. Individual experts and their CVs will not be evaluated at this stage

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 7th-Edition-Sep-2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. data.notice_text:
Employer:

Blantyre Water Board

Project:

Malawi Water and Sanitation Project-1

Assignment title:

Consultancy Service for Contract Management Specialist

Country:

Malawi

Loan No. /Credit No. / Grant No:

IDA E159-MW

Reference No:

MW-BWB-578558-CS-INDV

Issued on:

31st  October 2026

 

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM), through Blantyre Water Board (BWB) and Blantyre City Council (BCC) has secured financial support from the International Development Agency (IDA) of the World Bank (WB) towards the cost of the Malawi Water and Sanitation Project-1 (MWSP-1) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

Blantyre Water Board (BWB), which is the main implementing agency, intends to apply part of these proceeds from the grant to recruit an individual consultant to take up assignment of Contract Management Specialist to be positioned in the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) for the Malawi Water and Sanitation Project (MWSP-1) in adherence to the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

  1. Scope of the Services

The Contract Management Specialist shall assist and be answerable to the PIU Manager and will play a crucial role to support the project on contract compliance and risk management by spearheading the planning, design /review implementation, monitoring and management (supervision) of all contracts under the Project according to the World Bank Procurement regulations and work according to principles of good practice in contract management, and bear responsibility for performance management and cost effectiveness of contracts. The specialist will be expected to work very closely with the other members of the PIU and technical officers from the implementing agencies such as BWB, BCC, Ministry responsible for water development, and Ministry responsible for sanitation and hygiene, in the management and supervision of all contracts under the project. Specifically, the Contract Management Specialist will perform the following duties:

  1. Work hand in hand with the procurement team to prepare contract documents covering specifically guarantee requirements, price-adjustment provisions and indices, commencement and effectiveness conditions, sectional and substantial completion arrangements, and other potential claims risks.
  2. Provide support on contract administration and management with focus on proper contract compliance and performance oversight management for example appropriate determination of time and cost entitlements, variations to ensure technical necessity, accuracy as well as consistent value-for-money pricing; IPC reviews, contract price adjustment calculations, contingency utilization assessments and contract performance assessments;
  3. Undertake regular contract progress reports reviews and preparation of a synthesis report of key findings and recommended actions;
  4. Undertake proper project closure by ensuring preparation and issuance of completion certificates, management of the defects liability period, including decommissioning, final inspections, supervision requirements, outstanding payment obligations, completion documentation etc.,
  5. Manage works supervision contracts (both lumpsum and time-based consultancy contracts) by tracking deliverables, timesheets and associated payments;
  6. Maintain contract management tracking for all the contracts under implementation and coordinate any variation required, well in time as per contract.
  7. Monitoring and analyzing contracts performance under the projects against agreed benchmarks and advise Contract Managers in monitoring agreed contract-management key performance indicators, identifying potential bottlenecks and recommended remedial actions (close-out, extension or renewal of contracts) according to the FIDIC Conditions of Contract;
  8. Assist in resolving any unforeseen technical difficulties, complaints and other problems that may arise in the process of implementation
  9. Communicate regularly with the management on the status of various contracts, and ensure proper guidance and approvals are acquired before any contract amendments or cancellation / termination as per contract provisions.
  10. Assist the project in preparing realistic work plans and budgets for execution of contracts and tracking progress including undertaking period updating of contract management module in STEP.
  11. In liaison with the Contracts Managers (Engineers and implementing team), conduct progress review meetings and field supervisory visits to project sites to assess technical, administrative, and financial processes and implementation progress of the contracts.
  12. Ensure all formal and informal meetings and discussions with the service providers and implementing sectors are documented and records adequately filed.
  13. Review financial data submitted by the contractor and service providers in support of the Finance Unit and ensure timely payment of certificates and invoices.
  14. Address all matters associated with delivery of goods/services e.g. taxation, duties, clearance etc. in consultation with the Financial Management specialist.
  15. Contribute to the formulation of any contract amendments and any changes in accordance with the Bank Procedures i.e. ensuring that prior review documents are sent to the Bank for relevant approvals.
  16. Support the preparation quarterly, semi-annual, and annual progress reports for the project including completion reports for subprojects
  17. Document learnings and best practices from the implementation of the contract under the project, and preparation of performance assessment reports for completed contracts.
  18. Attend and participate in World Bank Missions including monthly progress review meetings and support the preparation of appropriate technical briefs as required.

 

2. Professional Qualifications and Experience

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

  1. Post-graduate Degree in Management Discipline such as Contract Management, Project Management, Procurement, Civil Engineering or Construction Management from a recognized institution and those with procurement qualifications such as CIPS, or FIDIC training in contract management or adjudication, will have added advantage;
  2. At least 8 years of post-qualification experience in contract management or procurement under projects financed by International Financing Institutions including practical engineering experience in design, field supervision, or both, for high-value infrastructure Water Supply and Sanitation works.
  3. Demonstrated experience (at least 3 years) applying standard international conditions of contract, particularly the FIDIC Red Book and thorough understanding of contract management tools and project fiduciary procedures including Interim Financial Reports (IFR) and World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers;
  4. Demonstrated proficiency with project management software /tracking tools and project fiduciary procedures;
  5. Demonstrated experience managing contracts works and services, and experience in the public sector will be considered an asset;
  6. Demonstrated experience in the development and use of contract management and tracking tools and/or platforms
  7. Willingness to work under pressure and with minimum supervision; and
  8. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  9. Highly motivated with excellent planning, analytical, communications and   interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  10. Upholding of anti-corruption and anti-bribery ethics.

3.  Duration of the Assignment

The Contract Management Specialist shall be recruited for a period of two (2) years, but the contract shall be renewable annually subject to satisfactory performance, need and availability of funding.

4. Facilities to be provided by the Client

The following shall be provided by the client: office space, furniture, and office equipment, communication, and internet facilities. For all field related assignments, the Project shall provide transport and costs and other expenses (per Diems etc.) related to the field work.

5. Location of Employment and Obligations of the Consultant

The Contract Management Specialist will be based at the Chileka PIU Offices in Blantyre but would be required to travel regularly to various locations within the Blantyre City and surrounding areas, where BWB/BCC shall be implementing the project activities.

6.  The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

8. Mode of Application

Interested Individuals meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail or by e-mail) by 13th November 2026 at or before 16.00 hours, local time.

The Chairperson, Internal Procurement and Disposal Committee (IPDC)

Blantyre Water Board,

Off-Makata Road,

P.O. Box 30369,

Blantyre,

Malawi

Phone: +265 (0) 1 872 200

Physical submission: Blantyre Water Board Head Office Main Reception

Attention: PIU Manager

REQUEST FOR EXPRESS OF INTEREST
CONSULTANT TO PREPARE A LOCAL ROADS NETWORK FINANCING STRATEGY
REFERENCE NO. CRRCIP-IC-016

The Government of Lao Peoples Democratic Republic (GoL) has received financing support from the World Bank’s (WB) International Development Association (IDA) to implement the Lao PDR Climate Resilient Road Connectivity Improvement Project (CRRCIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The proposed of Climate Resilient Road Connectivity Improvement Project (CRRCIP) seeks to build about 300 km of District Roads and Rural Roads in the poor districts of Khammouan, Savannakhet, and Saravan provinces. The MPWT in consultation with the DPWT of these three provinces had identified a long list of proposed roads. About 100 km of roads in each of the provinces will be selected from the roads in this longlist through a prioritization exercise based on aspects which include: (i) passing through a poor district – based on poverty headcount, (ii) criticality of the link for climate resiliency of the network, (iii) connectivity to agricultural areas, (iv) population served by the road, (v) traffic level, (vi) not passing through environmentally sensitive areas, and (vii) no resettlement of more than 200 people (or 40 households) and/or more than 40 households severely affected with 10 percent of productive assets owned by individual household lost in all three target provinces. The proposed project provides connectivity to National Roads and access to the east-west economic corridor between Vietnam and Thailand thus increasing market linkages and contributing towards greater economic gains to the local communities.

The CRRCIP now intends to engage a part-time, suitably qualified and experienced individual Consultant to Prepare a Local Roads Network Financing Strategy. Specifically, the consultant is required to prepare a local road network financing strategy which will include (i) Road Sector Overview and Expenditure Needs, (ii) Review of current Road Sector Financing, (iii) Fiscal and Macro-economic context, (iv) exploring Financing Options and Reform Scenarios, (v) prepare the Road Sector Financing Strategy and Action Plan. This will be a part-time assignment and the Consultant will work intermittently in Lao PDR and home-based. During visits to Lao PDR, the consultant will be based in Vientiane Capital, MPWT. In the course of entire assignment, the Consultant will cooperate with MPWT and in particular with the Department of Roads (DoR) and the Department of Finance (DPF) as described in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The full ToR for the assignment can be found at the following website : https://ppmd.mof.gov.la/opportunities/com or it can be provided to interested candidates upon written request to the email address below.

This will be an output-based contract with part-time inputs, expected to start by February 2027. The Consultant is required to work in Vientiane for at least 50% of the finally agreed time input in person-days. The work plan shall be agreed during contract negotiations.

The CRRCIP now invites eligible individual consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant should provide information (CV, Expression of Interest, other supporting information, if any) demonstrating that s/he has the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. In order to qualify for this position, the candidates shall meet the following experience and competence requirements :

    At least a Master’s degree in transport economy, civil engineering, road/transport contract management, or related fields. 
    A minimum of 15 years of working experience in Road Sector institutional reforms and Road Sector financing. 
    Preparation / implementation / completion of at least 3 similar projects, including roads’ long-term operation & maintenance (O&M) funding & implementation frameworks and/or strategies.
    A minimum of 6 years of experience working with development partners funding the road sector, including WB, ADB or other international institutions. 
    Experience in Lao PDR or in other countries in South/ Southeast Asia region is an advantage. 
    Familiarity with the GoL road improvement projects and GoL’s administrative and other procedures is an advantage.
    Excellent speaking and writing English.
    Excellent communication skills.
    Ability to work independently.

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 4th edition of November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) on or before 13 November 2026, 17:00 o’clock Lao time (submissions via email are also acceptable). Only the shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Project Name

Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project

Project Number

https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P502591

Activity and Reference Number (STEP)

Project Country Coordinator - Samoa FJ-PIFS-577402-CS-INDV

Implementing Agency Names

Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat

Country

FIJI

 

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) and seven Pacific Island member countries (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) have received financing (grants and credits) from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) towards the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project (the Project) and will apply part of these proceeds to the contract below for Consulting Services.

PIFS is seeking a qualified and experienced Project Country Coordinator (CC) - Samoa to provide in-country coordination support for the implementation of the Project in Samoa. The Coordinator will assist with the management and delivery of country-specific project activities, working closely with the Ministry of Finance's designated Country Focal Point (CFP), the Project Management Unit (PMU) in Suva, and other stakeholders.

This is a part-time individual consultant assignment for up to 144 days per year (maximum 20 days per month), initially contracted for two years with performance-based extensions every two years thereafter until 2030. The consultant must have the legal right to live and work in Samoa.

 

Scope of Services

Under the overall direction of the PMU Project Coordinator, the Country Coordinator shall undertake the following activities:

  1. Lead and coordinate day-to-day implementation of project activities in Samoa.
  2. Liaise with the Ministry of Finance's CFP and the Central Bank of Samoa on project activities, including follow-up on Project Steering Committee (PSC) meetings and preparation of minutes.
  3. Support the CFP in developing annual country-specific work plans and budgets for submission to PIFS/PMU.
  4. Monitor procurement, financial management, and reporting activities to ensure timely delivery and compliance with World Bank procedures.
  5. Identify and resolve implementation issues in coordination with the CFP and PMU.
  6. Review consultant outputs, prepare documentation for payments, and support reporting obligations.
  7. Prepare annual reports on country-specific activities for submission to the Ministry of Finance and PIFS.
  8. Undertake any other tasks requested by the CFP or PMU Project Coordinator.

 

Mandatory Criteria

Education

The CC’s services shall be subject to an annual performance evaluation based on performance indicators specified in the Terms of Reference below. Performance evaluation shall be the basis for the extension or termination of the services. The selected CC is expected to work in his/her home country

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges, and foster collaboration and cooperation in the pursuit of shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.  The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

Participating Countries

The Pacific Island Countries (PICs) participating in the regional project comprise Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu

Overall Project Objective

The Project development Objective is to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries

Project Length

August 2024 to September 30 2030

 

2. Project Background

The Pacific Island Forum Secretariat (PIFS) is expecting to receive financing from the World Bank (WB) Group’s International Development Association (IDA) for a proposed project to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in Pacific Island Countries (PICs).  The PICs covered by the proposed regional project (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) include diverse island economies facing similar correspondent banking relationship challenges.

PICs range in size and topography – from small island states such as Samoa, with two principal inhabited volcanic islands, to large archipelagos such as the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), with 29 atolls spread over 2 million km2 of ocean. Population sizes vary from 11,300 people in Tuvalu to 930,000 people in Fiji.

The economic landscape of PICs is equally diverse, marked by different growth drivers, poverty rates, and growth trajectories. The average GDP growth across PICs decelerated to 3.5 percent in 2023 after a historically high of 7.9 percent in 2022, in a rebound from the COVID-19 crisis. However, medium-term growth prospects have worsened, with output growth expected to be significantly below the pre-pandemic trend of 4.7 percent between 2014 & 2019. Given low growth and limited employment opportunities in the island economies, labor migration to neighboring countries and the resulting remittances are critical drivers of living standards.

The United States, New Zealand, and Australia account for 94 percent of the Pacific diaspora. Trade and tourism are vital for many PICs, providing revenue and employment opportunities. Remittances, equivalent to more than 40 percent of GDP in some PICs, are a buffer against income shocks and an important source of finance for essential household consumption and human capital investment.

Financial systems in PICs are characterized by low levels of financial access and an uneven development of national payment systems. Both domestically owned and multinational commercial banks dominate the financial sector in all PICs.  In several PICs, much of the population lacks access to basic transaction accounts, limiting households and businesses’ ability to send and receive payments, save, invest, and respond to climatic and economic shocks. The financial market infrastructure is underdeveloped, in part due to limited competition and the lack of economies of scale. The level of national payment system development is uneven across PICs, and regional efforts to improve the efficiency of cross-border payments are limited in scale and scope.

PICs are uniquely vulnerable to the withdrawal of the correspondent banking relationships (CBR) that underpin international trade, tourism, remittances, and humanitarian financial flows. Correspondent banking is an arrangement under which one bank (correspondent) holds deposits owned by other banks (respondents) and provides payment and other services to those respondent banks. CBRs are an essential feature of the global payment system – they enable individuals, businesses, and governments to make and receive cross-border payment services related to remittances, e-commerce, trade, and official sector flows. The cross-border transactions enabled in PICs are in various currencies, primarily the US dollar, Euro, and Australian dollar.

The withdrawal of CBRs, a well-documented global phenomenon affecting many emerging markets and developing economies, has adverse consequences and negative externalities for Pacific Islanders, including seasonal laborers, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and vulnerable populations. Based on publicly available data, the number of active correspondents for Pacific banks has declined significantly since 2011 to levels that put the Pacific financial system overall at risk.

In order to mitigate the issues identified above, the WB will provide funding to the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) to implement the proposed “Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project”.  The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges and foster collaboration and cooperation in pursuing shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources, and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members' shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance, and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.    The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions, and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

The project will have two components: (1) Temporary correspondent banking services and (2) Enabling environment and regulatory harmonization.  The proposed project will be implemented by a Project Management Unit (PMU) within the PIFS with strategic project oversight provided by a Project Steering Committee (PSC) comprised of representatives of participating Pacific Finance Ministers. While the PMU will be responsible for day-to-day project activities, it will need to ensure close collaboration and coordination with participating Ministries of Finance, which will oversee project activities and approve work plans through the PSC.

Comprising of Secretaries of Finance or other officials from the participating PICs finance ministries and the PIFS Director (Programs and Initiative), the PSC will meet on a quarterly basis and be responsible for the approval of key project activities as needed. The PSC will report to Pacific Finance Ministers annually at the Forum Economic Minister Meeting (FEMM) to ensure that strategic guidance and orientation are provided over the project activities. At the technical level, each participating PIC will be required to nominate a competent   government official as a Country Focal Point (CFP) responsible for project coordination at the national level, who will be designated as the point of contact with the PMU and the WB team.

The competent government official in each PIC will be complemented by a country coordinator (CC) based in-country, recruited through the PMU, and responsible for coordinating service delivery at the individual country level.

The PIFS is now seeking qualified and competent national consultants from each member country to be the country coordinator (CC) for the PMU and based in the respective participating Pacific Island countries (PICs).  The required positions are expected to be selected by the PIFS in accordance with the WB’s ‘Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers’ (Procurement Regulations), fifth edition, September 2023, and as amended over time.

 

3. Objective of the Position

The main objective of the CC would be to manage and coordinate the full range of project, country specific activities during the project cycle from effectiveness through implementation to completion.  The CC will be funded by the project (through the PMU) and report to the PIFS/ PMU Coordinator.  In addition, he/she will work closely with the specific Country Focal Point (CFP), a government official appointed by the MOF of that particular PIC.

 

4. Scope of Services

The CC will be required to adopt a flexible approach to coordinate and facilitate the required country specific project activities and report on tangible outcomes in terms of project implementation progress. The CC will be required to work in a pro-active manner, and to help ensure effective implementation of activities and delivery of outputs in a timely manner.

  1. The selected CC will lead and coordinate the day-to-day implementation of the project activities, including the following:
  2. Liaising with PICs Ministry of Finance’s CFP and Central Bank on country specific project related activities, including follow up on the Project Steering Committee (PSC) meetings and preparing meeting minutes as required;
  3. Work in close coordination with the CFP in developing the annual country specific activities, budgets to be submitted to the PIFS/PMU;
  4. Follow up closely on all country specific procurement activities to ensure that there are no delays in the selection process;
  5. In coordination with the CFP, identifying problems/impediments promptly as they arise during project implementation and take timely remedial actions;
  6. Monitoring, with assistance of the PMU M&E specialist, the progress of the country specific project activities and its results indicators;
  7. Follow up closely on all country specific financial management activities to ensure that there are no delays in the payment process;
  8. Follow up closely on the country specific activities and report to the CFP and the PMU Project Coordinator;
  9. Work closely with the CFP and review reports/outputs prepared by selected consultants and provide inputs to the CFP as required;
  10. Prepare the required documentation for the payment of outputs prepared by the selected consultants, obtain CFP approval and submit documents to the PMU for payment;
  11. Work closely with the CFP in preparing annual reports on country specific activities to be submitted to the MOF and PIFS; and
  12. Any other activities as requested by the CFP or the PMU Project Coordinator.

 

5. Reporting Obligations

The CC will work closely with the Country Focal Person (CFP) and report to the PMU Project Coordinator.

 

6. Institutional Arrangements

This is a part-time work assignment, with the Consultant expected to be based in in their home country. The Consultant will be supported by the PIFS PMU based in Suva, Fiji but will work closely with and report to the country focal person in the first instance. The CC is expected to show flexibility in working arrangements as time inputs will fluctuate based on country requirements. The work will be part-time averaging approximately 12  days per month for the next six years. A contract will initially be signed for two years with a performance based extension every two years thereafter. Performance evaluation shall be the basis for the extension or termination of the services. Facilities such as office space, intercom telephone facilities, personal computers, printing facilities, Internet access and stationery will be provided.

 

7. Performance Indicators

The following performance indicators shall be used for performance assessment:

  1. Positive progress and good performance of the entrusted project activities, as per the TOR;
  2. Ensuring that WB processes and procedures are complied with in all activities and in accordance with the POM;
  3. Provide and maintain strategic engagement, networking and collaboration with key stakeholders;
  4. Ensure the utilization and management of project funds are in compliance with the Financing Agreement;
  5. Ensure the collection of all data required to track project progress;
  6. Ensure the project monitoring and reporting timeline is adhered to;
  7. Prepare and compile periodic semi-annual and annual reports on project activities
  8. Compile proposed annual workplan for the following year with budget and procurement plan;
  9. Positive evaluation of performance by the PIFS and the WB team;
  10. Effective management of other experts engaged by the PMU; and
  11. Support in implementing any capacity building agendas related to the Project as required.

 

8. Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

The CC undertakes to comply with PIF’s and WB’s policies and rules with regard to anti-corruption and prevention of fraudulent practices, conflict of interest and confidentiality. The CC shall maintain confidentiality on all sensitive information obtained during the assignment and shall not publish wholly or in part the findings or such information, without prior written consent by the PIF. Any draft reports and other documents produced by the consultant will be discussed and cleared with the PIF and the WB before their final issue. A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) will be signed between the PIFS and the selected candidate to be attached to the contract.

RE-ADVERTISEMENT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

 

Country:  Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Employer: Ministry of Revenues (MOR)

Project: Governance Modernization for Efficient Service Delivery Project

Credit No.: 7619 ET

Assignment Title: Selection of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS)

Reference No.: ET-MOR-577821-CS-INDV

Issued on: October 24, 2026

 

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Governance Modernization for Efficient Service Delivery Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) aim to engage a highly qualified Technical Lead / Chief Architect to provide independent technical leadership for the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS). The role will focus on strengthening enterprise architecture, governing system design, ensuring compliance with approved standards, and overseeing vendor performance in alignment with program objectives and governance frameworks.

 

The Ministry of Revenues requires two (2) individual consultants for the role of Technical Lead/ Chief Architect for ITAS. This notice is for Reference No.: ET-MOR-577821-CS-INDV. A similar notice has been published for the second position under Reference No.: ET-MOR-578032-CS-INDV. Interested candidates are required to submit a separate Expression of Interest for each specific reference number they wish to be considered for.

 

The Ministry of Revenue invites qualified professionals to apply for the role of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the ITAS initiative. The selected candidate will be responsible for reviewing and updating enterprise architecture, defining and maintaining solution architecture, establishing governance standards, and ensuring integration across ITAS, DW/BI, e-Invoicing, and other Ministry systems. The role also includes oversight of vendor activities, management of technical risks, and ensuring compliance with security, scalability, and performance requirements. Given the scale, complexity, and national importance of this program, the Ministry seeks an experienced Chief Architect with a proven track record in large-scale IT system implementations within multi-stakeholder environments.

 

The Ministry of Revenue invites qualified individual consultants to apply for the role of Technical Lead / Chief Architect for the ITAS initiative. Applicants must hold a Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, with a minimum of 12 years’ experience (10 years with a Master’s). Required expertise includes mission-critical system integration, distributed systems, multi-vendor environments, architecture governance, and advisory roles. Strong competencies in enterprise IT system design, data and security architecture, infrastructure, API-based integration, and high-availability systems are essential; experience with containerized architectures (e.g., Kubernetes) is an advantage. Prior work in public sector or large government systems is required, with preference for tax administration or revenue/financial systems. Interested consultants should submit CVs and documentation demonstrating qualifications and relevant experience.

                    

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.13 and 3.14 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulation for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”).

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 12:30 hours and 13:30 to 17:00 hours Ethiopian Time.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) on or before 17:00 hours Ethiopian Time on November 13, 2026.

Ministry of Revenue, Head Office

Street Address: Megenagna 24 (40/60 Condominium), near Addis Ababa Water and Sewerage Authority

Floor/ Room number: Building Block-B, 2nd Floor, Room number 201

Governance Modernization to Enable Efficient Service Delivery Project;

Mr. Dawit Tesfaye – Procurement Expert (World Bank - Project Implementation Unit, MoR dawittmor@gmail.com, or DawitTT@mor.gov.et,  Tel. No. +251956201120

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.15, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixth Edition March 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

data.title: International short-term consultant on International good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education)
data.project_name: Project Preparation Assistance: Enhancing Access to Tertiary Education through Student Loan Mechanis
data.institution: Ministry of Economy and Finance of the Republic of Uzbekistan
data.notice_text:
TERMS OF REFERENCE

 For International short-term consultant on International good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education)

Grant facility for project preparation (GFPP) – Uzbekistan Student Loan Program

I. Background

The Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at expanding equitable access to higher education and strengthening the effectiveness, sustainability, and inclusiveness of student financing mechanisms. As higher education participation continues to increase, ensuring adequate, equitable, and effective financing has become a key priority to support equal educational opportunities and long-term sector development.

To support these reforms, the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) represents a strategic investment of US$2 million, financed by the World Bank, to support the preparation and implementation readiness of the Student Loan Program in Uzbekistan. The GFPP finances analytical studies, institutional capacity building, implementation support, and policy development to establish a sustainable and efficient student financing system. The facility supports comprehensive analytical work to assess the current student financing landscape, conduct stakeholder consultations, evaluate international good practices, and develop evidence-based policy recommendations. It also strengthens implementation capacity through the recruitment of specialized Project Implementation Unit (PIU) staff and fiduciary experts, while supporting national and international training programs for representatives of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), the Ministry of Education and Science (MoES), and other relevant stakeholders.

These reforms take place in a context of rapid expansion. Gross enrolment in higher education rose from 9 percent to 21 percent between 2016 and 2022, the number of HEIs grew from 70 to 194, and the Government aims to reach 50 percent enrolment by 2030. Admission is still largely managed through centrally set quotas of places, which are increased every year.2 Public spending on tertiary education has risen more than fivefold in five years to about 0.89 percent of GDP, close to the OECD average. However, the financing model continues to rely heavily on households: around 68 percent of public higher education institutions’ (HEIs’) revenues come from tuition fees; free (state-funded) places, held by about 17 percent of students, are allocated on admission test scores and benefit mostly students from middle- and higher-income families; and government funding to HEIs is based on enrolment alone, so it does not reward labour market outcomes, curricular innovation or industry links.1 The regional “dual-track” model of budget-funded and fee-paying places, combined with centralised quotas that may not correspond to demand for specific programmes, has been found to create an incentive for institutions to retain fee-paying students at the expense of academic standards.2 World Bank analysis has pointed to a package of system-level financing reforms, including a transparent funding formula that combines enrolment with performance on strategic indicators, competitive grants, diversification of institutional revenues and reform of student financial aid. These reforms depend on greater institutional financial and academic autonomy and on reliable data on graduate outcomes.1

The Government recognizes the importance of evidence-based analysis to inform future reforms of the financing of tertiary education, covering both technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and higher education (HE). It also places high value on learning from good practice in relevant and comparable international cases, so that design choices for Uzbekistan are informed by what other systems have done, what results they achieved, and under which conditions.

II. International good practice and strategic choices in tertiary education (TVET and HE) financing

Financing systems are not neutral. How public and private resources are allocated to institutions and students – for example through negotiated or input-based budgets, enrolment-based or formula funding, performance-based funding, competitive and grant-based funding, or cost-sharing with students and employers – and the legal and institutional framework that governs these flows shape what is incentivised in the system. Over time, these choices influence which models of TVET and HE emerge (for example, broad mass access versus a more differentiated system with centres of excellence; demand-led versus centrally steered provision; the balance and pathways between TVET and HE), and which outcomes the system tends to produce in terms of access and equity, completion, quality, labour market relevance, research, and the sustainability and predictability of public spending.

International experience shows that similar arrangements can lead to very different results depending on their design, on how they are combined, and on the institutional context in which they operate (e.g., system governance, institutional autonomy, quality assurance and data systems). A related question for Uzbekistan is how to manage the number and distribution of places. Several countries have moved away from centrally set quotas for students entering TVET and HE, and the experience of these transitions, including the financial incentives and changes in funding allocation that made them possible, is directly relevant. A structured review of selected international cases will help the Government consider which options, or combination of options, best fit Uzbekistan’s strategic intentions for the sector, and what adaptations would be required.

III. Objectives

The objective of this consultancy is to support the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the PIU, in coordination with the MoES and other relevant stakeholders, by carrying out research on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and HE). Specifically, the consultant will:

  1. review and analyse the general design of TVET and HE financing systems in a selection of relevant and comparable countries, including their institutional and legal frameworks;
  2. show how different financing arrangements link to different strategic visions for the sector, what they incentivise, and what impact they have had on the sector, including their benefits and risks;
  3. review countries’ experiences with admission quotas for students entering TVET and HE, and the steps governments took to phase them out, with particular attention to the finance-related aspects of this transition (e.g., use of financial incentives, or changes in how funds are allocated and managed in the sector); and
  4. assess the extent to which these arrangements are a good fit for, or would need to be adapted to, the Uzbek context and the Government’s strategic intentions.

IV. Scope of Work and Deliverables

Working with the MEF and the PIU, the consultant will carry out the following tasks:

  1. Review of the current financing system in Uzbekistan. Carry out an initial review of how TVET and HE are currently financed in Uzbekistan, including the main sources and flows of funds, the allocation of state-funded and fee-paying places, and the related legal and institutional framework. The review will draw on available documents and data and on discussions with the MEF, the PIU, the MoES and other relevant stakeholders, and will provide the baseline against which international experience is assessed.
  2. Methodology and analytical approach. Define the overall methodology of the research, including the approach to case selection, desk research, data analysis and interviews, and an initial framework for comparing financing systems. The framework will be kept broad at the outset and refined as the exploratory research and the review of the Uzbek system identify the most relevant dimensions and questions.
  3. Long-list of cases. Through desk research, identify and briefly profile a long-list of countries with relevant experience, based on criteria agreed with the MEF and the PIU (e.g., comparability with Uzbekistan, recent reform of the financing system, experience in phasing out admission quotas, strength of the TVET system).
  4. Selection of cases. Present the long-list to the MEF, the PIU, the MoES and other relevant stakeholders and agree on a short-list of cases (indicatively 6–7) for in-depth review.
  5. National consultations. Subject to confirmation, undertake a mission to Tashkent in mid-November 2026 to consult and interview national stakeholders (e.g., MEF, MoES, PIU, TVET and HE institutions), in order to deepen the understanding of the current financing system and the quota system and to discuss reform priorities.
  6. In-depth review and interviews. Carry out further research on the selected cases and lead in-depth interviews, with the support of the research assistant, with stakeholders and staff of the relevant ministries, agencies, funding bodies and/or institutions, to verify and complement information collected online.
  7. Analysis of admission quotas. Review the experience of selected countries in setting and phasing out quotas for students entering TVET and HE, including the sequencing of reforms and the role of financing instruments and fund-management arrangements in the transition.
  8. Analysis and recommendations. For each case and across cases, analyse design, legal and institutional arrangements, implementation, costs, impact on the sector, benefits and risks, and preconditions. Assess the fit of each option with the Uzbek context and identify the adaptations, sequencing and preconditions that a transition would require.
  9. Coordination of research. Coordinate and quality-assure the research process, including guiding and supervising a research assistant: allocating research tasks, specifying the data to be collected from available databases and the analyses to be run, developing common templates for case profiles and interview notes, managing sources, and collating and synthesising the evidence collected into an evidence matrix that underpins the report.
  10. Reporting and dissemination. Prepare the deliverables below, incorporate comments from the MEF, the PIU and other relevant stakeholders, and present findings as agreed with the MEF and the PIU.

Deliverables: (1) Inception note with an initial overview of the current financing system in Uzbekistan, the methodology and initial analytical framework, work plan and long-list of cases; (2) Preliminary draft report; (3) Revised draft report, including an executive summary and a summary presentation (PPT). The report will be in English, of approximately 40-50 pages plus annexes with case profiles.

The indicative timetable is as follows:

Intermediary steps (e.g., structure of the report, interview guide and list of interviewees) and the related timeline will be agreed with the MEF and the PIU.

V. Timeline, estimated efforts, and reporting arrangement

The consultancy will run from 16 November 2026 to 31 December 2026, for an estimated 30 working days, or 35 working days if the mission to Tashkent takes place. The consultancy is financed under the GFPP.

The consultant will report to the social department  at the MEF and work closely with the PIU, the MoES and other relevant stakeholders. The consultant will be supported by a research assistant, who will work under the consultant’s guidance.

VI. Qualifications Required

  • Graduate degree (PhD preferred) in education policy, economics, public policy, social science or other relevant field
  • At least 12 years of relevant professional experience in education policy and reform, including in tertiary education and TVET
  • Excellent knowledge and understanding of international tertiary education policy and governance, including the legal and institutional frameworks of TVET and HE, and a good understanding of system-level financing arrangements and their links with governance
  • Proven experience of comparative and international policy analysis, including institutional and governance analysis, case study research and stakeholder interviews
  • Experience of coordinating research and supervising research staff
  • Experience of working with government counterparts and international organisations on education sector reform
  • Knowledge of tertiary education in Central Asia, including Uzbekistan, and in other transition economies
  • Strong communication skills and excellent written and oral English
  • Motivated, proactive, and committed personality
  • Good IT skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form in English or Russian languages to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by November 13, 2026.

Uzbekistan, 100017, Tashkent, Niyozbek yo'li, 1

Tel:(+99897) 447-86-11

E-mail: gfppp181956@gmail.com

Web site: https://www.imv.uz/

Abdurashid Abdurakhmanov

2 Ambasz, D., D. Nikolaev, S. Malinovskiy, A. Olszak-Olszewski, P. Zavalina, and J. Botero Álvarez (2023). Towards Higher Education Excellence in Central Asia: A Roadmap for Improving the Quality of Education and Research through Regional Integration. Washington, DC: World Bank.

TERMS OF REFERENCE

 For research assistant on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and Higher education)

Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) – Uzbekistan Student Loan Program:

I. Background

The Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at expanding equitable access to higher education and strengthening the effectiveness, sustainability, and inclusiveness of student financing mechanisms. As higher education participation continues to increase, ensuring adequate, equitable, and effective financing has become a key priority to support equal educational opportunities and long-term sector development.

To support these reforms, the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) represents a strategic investment of US$2 million, financed by the World Bank, to support the preparation and implementation readiness of the Student Loan Program in Uzbekistan. The GFPP finances analytical studies, institutional capacity building, implementation support, and policy development to establish a sustainable and efficient student financing system. The facility supports comprehensive analytical work to assess the current student financing landscape, conduct stakeholder consultations, evaluate international good practices, and develop evidence-based policy recommendations. It also strengthens implementation capacity through the recruitment of specialized Project Implementation Unit (PIU) staff and fiduciary experts, while supporting national and international training programs for representatives of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF), the Ministry of Education and Science (MoES), and other relevant stakeholders.

These reforms take place in a context of rapid expansion. Gross enrolment in higher education rose from 9 percent to 21 percent between 2016 and 2022, the number of HEIs grew from 70 to 194, and the Government aims to reach 50 percent enrolment by 2030. Admission is still largely managed through centrally set quotas of places, which are increased every year.2 Public spending on tertiary education has risen more than fivefold in five years to about 0.89 percent of GDP, close to the OECD average. However, the financing model continues to rely heavily on households: around 68 percent of public higher education institutions’ (HEIs’) revenues come from tuition fees; free (state-funded) places, held by about 17 percent of students, are allocated on admission test scores and benefit mostly students from middle- and higher-income families; and government funding to HEIs is based on enrolment alone, so it does not reward labour market outcomes, curricular innovation or industry links.1 The regional “dual-track” model of budget-funded and fee-paying places, combined with centralised quotas that may not correspond to demand for specific programmes, has been found to create an incentive for institutions to retain fee-paying students at the expense of academic standards.2 World Bank analysis has pointed to a package of system-level financing reforms, including a transparent funding formula that combines enrolment with performance on strategic indicators, competitive grants, diversification of institutional revenues and reform of student financial aid. These reforms depend on greater institutional financial and academic autonomy and on reliable data on graduate outcomes.1

The Government recognizes the importance of evidence-based analysis to inform future reforms of the financing of tertiary education, covering both technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and higher education (HE). It also places high value on learning from good practice in relevant and comparable international cases, so that design choices for Uzbekistan are informed by what other systems have done, what results they achieved, and under which conditions.

II. The assignment

To inform these reforms, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the PIU have engaged an international consultant to carry out research on international good practice in the financing of tertiary education (TVET and HE). The research covers the general design of TVET and HE financing systems in a selection of relevant and comparable countries, including their institutional and legal frameworks, the incentives they create and their impact on the sector; and countries’ experiences in phasing out admission quotas for students entering TVET and HE, including the finance-related aspects of this transition. It will assess how far these arrangements fit, or would need to be adapted to, the Uzbek context. The work runs from October to December 2026. It starts with an initial review of how TVET and HE are currently financed in Uzbekistan and exploratory desk research on international experience, through which the analytical framework will be refined. It then includes a selection of country cases with national counterparts, in-depth interviews with stakeholders in the selected countries and, subject to confirmation, a mission to Tashkent in mid-November 2026.

III. Objective

The objective of this assignment is to provide research support to the international consultant throughout the study, by collecting, organising, analysing and synthesising evidence and data on the financing of TVET and HE in Uzbekistan and in the selected countries, and by supporting interviews, the mission to Tashkent and the preparation of the report.

IV. Scope of Work and Deliverables

Under the guidance and supervision of the international consultant, who defines the overall methodology of the research, the research assistant will carry out the following tasks:

  1. Review of the current system in Uzbekistan. Collect and organise documents and data on the current financing of TVET and HE in Uzbekistan (e.g., laws and regulations, budget and enrolment data, admission quota decisions, available studies), in coordination with the PIU, and prepare summary tables and notes as requested by the consultant.
  2. Exploratory and in-depth desk research. Identify, collect and review relevant documents on the financing of TVET and HE and on admission quotas in other countries (laws and regulations, policy documents, funding rules, evaluations, academic and grey literature), first to help identify countries for the long-list and then in more depth for the selected cases.
  3. Data collection and analysis. Where necessary, extract data from available national and international databases (e.g., UNESCO UIS, OECD, Eurostat, World Bank and national statistics) and run specific analyses as requested by the consultant, such as comparisons of funding levels, enrolment and outcomes across countries.
  4. Case profiles. Draft short country profiles using common templates developed by the consultant, which will be refined as the research progresses.
  5. Evidence management. Set up and maintain a library of sources and references and an evidence matrix that brings together the information collected across countries, flagging gaps and inconsistencies to be checked in interviews.
  6. Support to interviews. Support the consultant, who will lead the interviews, by helping to prepare interview guides; identify and contact potential interviewees and schedule interviews; take notes and prepare written summaries of interviews.
  7. Support to the mission to Tashkent. Subject to confirmation, travel to Uzbekistan on the same dates as the consultant; support the preparation of meetings in coordination with the PIU; collect documents and data shared by national counterparts; take notes and prepare summary notes of meetings and consultations.
  8. Support to reporting. Prepare tables, figures and annexes; check facts and references; and proofread and format drafts of the inception note and report.

Deliverables: (1) Collection of documents and data on the current financing system in Uzbekistan, with summary tables; library of sources; and first draft case profiles of long-listed countries; (2) Summary notes of meetings held during the mission to Tashkent (if it takes place); (3) Interview notes, completed case profiles for the selected countries, evidence matrix, and datasets and outputs of the data analyses carried out; (4) Tables, annexes and reference list for the final report.

The indicative timetable is as follows:

V. Timeline, estimated efforts, and reporting arrangement

The assignment will run from 16rd November to 31 December 2026, for an estimated 20 working days. It may involve travel to Uzbekistan on the same dates as the international consultant (indicatively -November 2026, dates to be confirmed). The assignment is financed under the GFPP.

The research assistant will work under the day-to-day guidance and supervision of the international consultant and will report to Zulfiya Mamadalieva (mamadaliyeva.zulfiya@mail.ru) at the MEF. Deliverables will be approved by the MEF and the PIU on the advice of the international consultant.

VI. Qualifications Required

  • Master’s degree in economics, education, public policy, social science or other relevant field
  • At least 5 years of experience in policy research or analysis, preferably in education, TVET or public finance
  • Familiarity with tertiary education policy and financing; knowledge of international comparative work is an advantage
  • Strong desk research skills, including working with legal and policy documents
  • Good quantitative skills and experience of working with international and national statistical databases; knowledge of statistical software (e.g., Stata, R or SPSS) is an advantage
  • Excellent organisational skills and ability to manage sources and evidence systematically
  • Excellent written and oral English; knowledge of Russian and/or Uzbek is an advantage
  • Ability to work independently and to meet deadlines
  • Good IT skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and reference management tools

Abdurashid Abdurakhmanov

 

References

2 Ambasz, D., D. Nikolaev, S. Malinovskiy, A. Olszak-Olszewski, P. Zavalina, and J. Botero Álvarez (2023). Towards Higher Education Excellence in Central Asia: A Roadmap for Improving the Quality of Education and Research through Regional Integration. Washington, DC: World Bank.

data.title: Study on Financing and Commercial Components for the ASEAN Submarine Power Cable Framework
data.project_name: Accelerating Sustainable Energy Transition Program
data.notice_text:
The ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Clean Energy and Power Trade Development in Southeast Asia Project as Phase 1 of the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach Accelerating Sustainable Energy Transition/MPA ASET (P181555) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Firm to develop a Study on Financing and Commercial Components for the ASEAN Submarine Power Cable Framework.
The consulting services (“the Services”) include assessing electricity demand and potential anchor off-takers along priority submarine power cable corridors; developing minimum investment-readiness and bankability criteria; evaluating financing strategies, risk allocation, and investor protection mechanisms; developing ownership, cost allocation, and operational governance options; establishing harmonised commercial and settlement principles for cross-border electricity trading; and developing and applying an investment readiness maturity assessment tool to identify gaps, prioritise submarine interconnection projects, and support project preparation and potential financing.
The assignment is expected to run for over a period of ten (10) months commencing from tentatively in January 2027. Actual commencement date will be communicated with the consulting firm that is successfully selected from the procurement process.
ACE now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.
Interested Consultants must submit detailed documentary evidence indicating credentials to perform the services including company profiles, core business description, description of similar assignments and experience in similar conditions, qualifications relevant to this field, brochures (if available) and other relevant information. The shortlisting criteria are:
A.    Qualifying Criteria (Eligibility Requirement) – Pass/Fail:
1.    The consulting firm must demonstrate relevant professional experience in providing consulting or advisory services in the energy sector, power infrastructure, infrastructure financing, or related fields.
2.    The consulting firm must demonstrate experience in at least two (2) completed or substantially completed assignments involving power transmission infrastructure, electricity interconnection, cross-border electricity trade, regional power cooperation, or large-scale energy infrastructure development and financing.
Only consulting firms meeting all qualifying criteria (Pass) will proceed to the ranking assessment. Firms failing any of the qualifying criteria will not be considered further.
 
B.    Criteria for Ranking:
1.    Power Transmission and Interconnection Infrastructure
Experience in submarine power cables, subsea transmission, cross-border power transmission, electricity interconnection, regional electricity trade, power system planning, demand forecasting, and renewable energy integration.
2.    Infrastructure Financing and Commercial Structuring
Experience in infrastructure project financing, financial modelling, bankability assessments, investment structuring, PPP, joint ventures, blended finance, guarantees, tariff methodologies, cost allocation, revenue models, and commercial arrangements.
3.    Energy Sector Regulatory, Legal, and Institutional Frameworks
Experience in developing energy sector legal, regulatory, and institutional frameworks, including cross-border permitting, licensing, concession arrangements, grid access, investor protection, risk allocation, and dispute resolution.
4.    Regional Experience and Stakeholder Engagement
Experience in ASEAN or comparable regional/multi-country energy cooperation, stakeholder engagement with governments, regulators, utilities, TSOs, investors, and development partners, and MDB/IFI-financed assignments.
Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. Hence, CVs are not required at this stage.
The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest or can be found at the following website: https://aseanenergy.org/opportunities.
The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised in sixth edition dated February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The Consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultants Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method. The Full Technical Proposal (FTP) format will be applied in evaluating the proposals as specified in procedures set out in the last updated version of World Bank guidelines.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 09:00 to 17:00 Jakarta Time (GMT+7).
Expressions of interest must be submitted in a written form as one (1) single consolidated PDF document, including all relevant attachments or annexes, by e-mail at the latest by 13 November 2026, 23:59 Jakarta Time (GMT+7) to:

ASEAN CENTRE FOR ENERGY Attn: MPA ASET PMU
E-mail: asetprocurement@aseanenergy.org
Subject: [EOI Submission] Study on Financing and Commercial Components for the ASEAN Submarine Power Cable Framework (ID-ACE-578697-CS-CQS) – [Insert Name of Firm]

Os serviços de consultoria (“os Serviços”) incluem: A empresa de fiscalização deverá garantir a conformidade das obras de construção de cada escola com a documentação técnica e dentro dos orçamentos estipulados no contrato do empreiteiro fazendo registos comprovativos sob a forma de relatórios das acções desenvolvidas durante o período do contrato. Os especialistas-chave não serão avaliados para fase de pré-seleção (lista curta).

 

Os Consultores deverão ter em especial atenção a Secção III, parágrafos 3.13, 3.15 e 3.16 dos Regulamentos de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Operações de Financiamento de Projetos de Investimento (o “Regulamento de Aquisições”), datadas de Setembro de 2025, que estabelecem as políticas do Banco Mundial relativas a conflito de interesse.

O consultor será selecionado com base no método de Seleção Baseada no Menor Custo (LCS) de acordo com o “Regulamento de Aquisição para Mutuários de IPF” do Banco, Setembro de 2025 (“Regulamento de Aquisição”).
