Objective of the Assignment

The general objective of the assignment is to prepare a complete, technically sound and procurement-ready Terms of Reference and functional and technical requirements package for the RVS digital data-collection solution — comprising a mobile field application and a web-based administration and data-management portal (Section 3.4) and related data collection workflow, in accordance with the RVS methodology described in GD 334 of 05-06-2025, the Project implementation framework and the Quality Assurance Plan applicable to Subcomponent 3.1. The package shall be methodologically driven by seismic risk and RVS requirements, while being sufficiently clear and structured for subsequent application development procurement and implementation.

The specific objective is to define, in a clear and verifiable manner, what the future mobile application must do from the perspective of RVS field screening and seismic risk data collection: what building data it must collect, how evaluators shall record observations, how vulnerability and exposure indicators shall be structured, how data shall be validated, stored, exported and documented, and how the application shall be tested and accepted before field use. The Consultant shall ensure that the resulting specification is suitable for subsequent application development procurement and implementation, while remaining primarily aligned with the seismic risk, building screening, GIS/data and institutional requirements of the Project.

Specific objectives

In addition to the general objective stated above, the Consultant shall achieve, in particular, the following specific objectives:

  • Translate the RVS methodology established by GD 334/2025 into a structured set of building-level data fields, controlled vocabularies, vulnerability and exposure indicators, validation rules and scoring logic suitable for digital field data collection;
  • Document the mapping of the GD 334/2025 scoring and classification parameters to the predominant Moldovan building typologies and to the seismic zoning of the national territory (using Activity 1a outputs as they become available), identify the parameters that will require future calibration, and define the data fields, metadata and procedure needed to make such calibration possible once screening datasets exist (calibration-readiness, Section 3.1);
  • Prepare a complete data model and data dictionary for the RVS solution, including field IDs, data types, mandatory/optional status, allowed values, units, validation rules, dependencies, export attributes and GIS relevance;
  • Define the field-screening workflow, user roles (field evaluator, supervisor, data validator, GIS/data manager, administrator, MIRD/OEAPM/PIU reviewer) and the corresponding access permissions, workflow states and audit-trail requirements;
  • Define the functional requirements for the mobile application and the web-based administration and data-management portal, including form-driven data entry, photo and GPS capture, offline operation, synchronization, supervisor review, correction workflow, user and role management, workflow supervision, data validation and quality control, reporting, export and reporting functions;
  • Define the technical requirements and minimum architectural constraints in an implementation-neutral manner, sufficient for objective procurement and acceptance testing, but without locking the future Client into a specific technology stack unless explicitly justified;
  • Validate the draft data-collection form and field workflow through a limited form walkthrough and tabletop simulation (Section 3.11), and incorporate the documented lessons learned into the final specification
  • Prepare the QA/QC, testing and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) framework, including test scenarios, defect severity levels, acceptance conditions and Test/UAT register templates;
  • Prepare a procurement-ready Terms of Reference and technical specification for the subsequent acquisition of application-development services, fully consistent with World Bank Procurement Regulations;
  • Define the minimum content of user and administrator documentation to be produced by the future application-development service provider, in support of training, field deployment and post-collection validation;
  • Define the data-governance, privacy, security, hosting, source-code ownership and maintenance requirements applicable to the future solution (Section 3.10);
  • Ensure full requirements traceability through a Requirements Traceability Matrix linking each requirement to a methodological source, data field, test scenario and acceptance criterion;

Document all decisions, assumptions, comments and revisions through controlled Version Log, Comment Log, Data Register and, where applicable, Change Log and NC/CAPA Register, in line with the QAP.Scope of Services

The Consultant shall provide all services necessary for the preparation of a complete requirements and technical specification package for the RVS digital data-collection solution and data collection workflow. The core services shall cover methodological translation of RVS requirements, assessment of field screening workflow, definition of functional requirements, preparation of the data model and validation rules, definition of GIS/export and metadata requirements, preparation of the QA/UAT framework, a limited form walkthrough and tabletop simulation, definition of data-governance and security requirements, cross-ToR coordination under the Common Data Standard,  and preparation of the procurement-ready ToR and technical specification for the subsequent application development services contract.

Review of the RVS methodology, GD 334 and QAP requirements

The Consultant shall review the RVS methodology described in GD 334 of 05-06-2025 and all available project documents relevant to Activity 1b, including the QAP, implementation chart, existing RVS forms/guidelines, risk map methodology requirements, data/GIS requirements and any other documentation made available by the Client.

The review shall identify the minimum data that must be collected through the mobile application, the logic of the RVS scoring/assessment process, the building typologies and vulnerability indicators to be recorded, the relationship between hazard, exposure and vulnerability data, and the quality control rules needed to make the collected dataset usable for subsequent analysis.

As part of this review, the Consultant shall map the scoring and classification parameters of GD 334/2025 against: (i) the predominant Moldovan building typologies (including precast large-panel, masonry, reinforced-concrete frame and mixed systems of the relevant construction periods); and (ii) the seismic zoning of the territory, using the administrative-unit hazard values produced under Activity 1a as they become available. The Consultant shall identify and document the parameters that would require future calibration, the evidence needed for such calibration, the applicable limitations, and the data fields and metadata that the future solution must capture so that calibration can be performed once the first screening datasets and the Activity 1a/1c outputs exist. The Consultant shall not modify the scoring rules established by GD 334/2025.

The Consultant shall prepare a Requirements Source Matrix showing the origin of each requirement.

Assessment of the RVS field workflow and user requirements

The Consultant shall analyse the practical workflow for field screening and data collection. This shall include the identification of user groups, field roles, data collection steps, review/validation steps, synchronization needs, supervisor functions and institutional review requirements.

At minimum, the analysis shall consider the following user groups: field evaluator, field team leader/supervisor, data validator, GIS/data manager, application administrator, OEAPM/PIU reviewer and MIRD reviewer. The Consultant shall describe the expected rights, responsibilities and access permissions for each user group.

The Consultant shall prepare workflow diagrams and/or process descriptions covering the full chain from assignment of buildings/areas, field visit, data entry, photo/geolocation capture, completeness checks, synchronization, supervisor review, correction/rejection, data export and final handover for further QC and integration.

Definition of functional requirements for the mobile application

The Consultant shall define the functional requirements for the future solution. The requirements shall be precise enough to be used in subsequent application development procurement and later testing. Each requirement shall have an identifier, description, priority, acceptance criterion and, where applicable, a reference to the RVS methodology or QAP requirement.

As a minimum, the functional requirements shall address the following components:

  • creation, assignment and management of field screening tasks and investigated areas;
  • RVS data collection form structured according to GD 334 of 05-06-2025 and the approved RVS methodology;
  • building identification and location capture, including address, administrative unit, coordinates and, where available, cadastral/building reference fields;
  • recording of building use, occupancy, structural typology, approximate age, number of storeys, structural and non-structural vulnerability indicators, visible deficiencies, exposure information and other required RVS fields;
  • photo capture and attachment to building records, with metadata such as date, time, user and coordinates where technically feasible;
  • automatic and manual validation rules, including mandatory fields, controlled lists, ranges, cross-field consistency checks and duplicate detection;
  • RVS scoring or classification logic, if required by the approved methodology, with transparent formulas/logic and traceable outputs;
  • offline-first field operation and subsequent synchronization when internet access is available;
  • record status workflow: draft, submitted, returned for correction, validated, exported and archived;
  • supervisor review, comments and correction workflow;
  • web-based administration and data-management functions: user and role management, task assignment and monitoring, workflow supervision, data validation and quality-control queues, dashboards and progress reporting, configuration of controlled lists where permitted, and system administration;
  • export of datasets in reusable formats for GIS and tabular processing;
  • generation of basic record summaries, field reports or export packages, where required;
  • audit trail for creation, modification, validation and export actions.

The Consultant shall distinguish mandatory, recommended and optional requirements. Optional features shall not obscure the minimum functional core required for field data collection and data quality control.

Definition of technical requirements and system architecture constraints

The Consultant shall define the minimum technical requirements for the future application in a way that is clear for application development service providers, but not unnecessarily restrictive with regard to implementation technology unless required by the Client. The technical requirements shall remain implementation-neutral and shall be derived from the RVS field workflow, data quality, security/access, interoperability and acceptance needs.

The Consultant shall not be required to design the full software architecture, write code, select a specific programming language or deliver a working application under this assignment. The expected technical specification shall describe the required functions, data structures, validation logic, export formats, user roles, testing evidence and acceptance conditions, so that a future application development service provider can develop the application competitively and objectively.

The future solution shall comprise, at minimum: (i) a mobile application for offline-first field data collection; and (ii) a web-based administration and data-management portal accessible from standard desktop environments (including Windows), supporting user and role management, task assignment, workflow supervision, data validation and quality control, reporting, export functions and system administration. Both components shall operate on a single controlled backend database with a common data model, access-control scheme and audit trail.

The technical requirements shall cover, as a minimum: mobile device compatibility, offline operation, synchronization, database structure, administrator functions, data storage, backup, performance, stability, security, access control, logging, interoperability, data export, deployment, maintenance and handover requirements.

The requirements shall specify that the application must support field use on common mobile devices used by field evaluators. At minimum, Android compatibility shall be addressed; iOS or cross-platform compatibility may be included where justified by the Client’s needs and budget. The Consultant shall propose clear minimum device and operating system requirements, taking into account field usability, camera/GPS availability and expected deployment conditions.

In particular (responding to reviewer questions on the backend), the technical specification shall explicitly define, in implementation-neutral terms: (i) where and how field-collected data shall be stored, including the hosting options analysed in Section 3.10; (ii) the minimum backend database requirements (controlled data model, referential integrity, unique identifiers, spatial attributes, transaction logging); (iii) how records shall be validated upon synchronization (server-side re-validation, conflict handling, duplicate detection, rejection/return workflow); (iv) how access shall be controlled (role-based access, authentication, session management, least-privilege administration); and (v) how data shall be backed up and restored (backup frequency, retention, recovery testing, responsibility).

The Consultant shall define requirements for a sustainable and maintainable solution, including documentation, configuration, administrator access, avoidance of vendor lock-in where possible, use of open/reusable export formats, and transfer of ownership of deliverables, source files, documentation and configuration materials as required by the Client, in accordance with the data-governance requirements of Section 3.10.

 

Development of the data model, data dictionary and validation rules

The Consultant shall prepare a complete data model and data dictionary for the RVS solution. The data dictionary shall translate the RVS methodology into a structured set of application fields, controlled vocabularies, field types, validation rules and export attributes.

For each field, the data dictionary shall include at least: field ID, field name, description, data type, mandatory/optional status, allowed values or domain, units where applicable, source or rationale, validation rule, dependency on other fields, export name, GIS relevance and notes/limitations.

The data model shall apply the Common Data Standard of Subcomponent 3.1 (Section 3.12): stable unique building identifiers, administrative-unit coding based on CUATM, the agreed coordinate reference system(s), and controlled building-typology vocabularies compatible with the exposure model of the seismic risk map methodology (Activity 1c). The data model shall also include the calibration-readiness fields defined under Section 3.1.

The Consultant shall define validation and consistency checks for field data. As a minimum, these shall include mandatory field checks, coordinate validity, duplicate building detection logic, consistency between number of storeys and building type, valid domains for structural typologies, photo completeness checks, date/time/user checks and logical checks required by the RVS methodology.

The Consultant shall also define the required export formats and attribute structure. At minimum, the future application shall be capable of exporting clean datasets in CSV/XLSX and GIS-compatible formats such as GeoPackage and/or GeoJSON, with stable unique identifiers and complete metadata. Where API or database export is required, the Consultant shall define the minimum expected structure and documentation.

Definition of QA/QC, testing, UAT and acceptance framework

The Consultant shall prepare the QA/QC and testing framework to be used during future application development and acceptance. The framework shall follow the QAP logic for application/IT deliverables and shall include the minimum evidence required for the application to be accepted before field use.

The Consultant shall define test scenarios covering at least: installation/login, role-based access, creation of tasks, offline data entry, photo/geolocation capture, validation rules, synchronization, correction workflow, supervisor validation, export, import/opening of exported files in GIS/table tools, audit trail and administrative functions, including the functions of the web-based administration portal, backup/restore evidence and server-side re-validation upon synchronization.

The Consultant shall prepare a draft Test/UAT Register template, including test ID, scenario, precondition, steps, expected result, actual result, pass/fail status, defects, severity, retest status, UAT decision and approval/confirmation fields. The framework shall also define defect severity levels and conditions under which the application can be accepted, accepted with conditions or rejected.

The acceptance framework shall define a two-stage acceptance for the future solution: Stage 1 — functional UAT in a controlled environment against the test scenarios; Stage 2 — a supervised field pilot on a limited building sample, performed with Client-designated certified evaluators, verifying the complete chain (task assignment → field collection → synchronization → validation → export) under real conditions before final acceptance. The obligations of the future application-development service provider in the field pilot shall be defined in the procurement-ready specification (Section 3.7).

The Consultant shall specify that final acceptance of the future solution will require an accepted UAT decision for the exact release/version, a test report, defect register, release notes, installation/export package, user/admin documentation and confirmation that the fields, functions and exports are correct and usable for RVS data collection and further processing, together with the accepted field-pilot report under Stage 2.

Preparation of the procurement-ready ToR and technical specification for subsequent application development services

The Consultant shall prepare a procurement-ready Terms of Reference and technical specification for the subsequent acquisition of application development services for the digital data-collection solution. This document shall be sufficiently detailed to allow qualified software developers or application development service providers to understand the scope, submit comparable offers and deliver a product that can be objectively tested and accepted.

The procurement-ready technical specification shall include, at minimum: background and objective, scope of subsequent application development services, required application modules, functional requirements, minimum technical requirements, data model, export requirements, security and access requirements, testing and UAT requirements, field-pilot obligations (Stage 2 acceptance), hosting and deployment options with their implications, data-governance obligations (data ownership, source-code and IP transfer, documentation and build/deployment instructions), warranty and post-acceptance support requirements (indicatively a minimum 12-month warranty and defect-correction period), deliverables, implementation timeline, support/warranty requirements, documentation requirements, handover requirements, acceptance criteria and evaluation inputs for procurement, if requested by the Client.

The specification shall be written in a way that reduces ambiguity and procurement risk. Requirements shall be measurable, testable and traceable. The Consultant shall avoid vague formulations such as “user-friendly” without defining the expected functionality, usability condition or acceptance evidence.

Inputs for training, field data collection and post-collection validation

Although the actual user training, building screening and data validation are subsequent activities, the Consultant shall prepare the application requirements in a manner that supports these activities. The requirements shall specify the minimum documentation and support materials that the application development service provider shall deliver for user training and field deployment.

The Consultant shall define the minimum content of user and administrator documentation, including quick-start guidance for field evaluators, administrator manual, data export procedure, troubleshooting notes, synchronization rules and basic data quality instructions, as well as training-of-trainers materials enabling MIRD/OEAPM-PIU and designated institutions to train future evaluators without dependence on the developer.

The Consultant shall additionally deliver, as part of the final package, a concise Specification Reading Guide (indicatively 10–15 pages) explaining to MIRD/OEAPM-PIU how the requirements package is structured, how to use it during the procurement and acceptance of the application-development services, and how to manage changes through the Change Request mechanism, and shall present it in a dedicated handover session

The Consultant shall also define how the future application shall support post-collection validation, cleaning, checking and consistency analysis. This shall include export of record status, validator comments, modification history, mandatory metadata and quality flags needed for the future building inventory database in the investigated area.

Data governance, privacy and security requirements

The Consultant shall prepare a dedicated data-governance chapter of the requirements package, covering at minimum the following, in implementation-neutral terms:

  • Data ownership: all data collected through the future solution, the configured system, its documentation and derived datasets shall be the property of the Government of the Republic of Moldova, administered by MIRD or a designated subordinate institution;
  • Hosting: an options analysis with indicative cost and responsibility implications for at least two hosting arrangements — (i) the MCloud government cloud platform / e-Government infrastructure, and (ii) dedicated infrastructure administered by MIRD or a designated institution — without prescribing the final choice, which is institutional;
  • Personal-data protection (Law No. 133/2011): purpose limitation and data minimization (no personal data of residents/owners beyond what GD 334/2025 strictly requires); field guidance for photo capture so that identifiable persons, vehicle plates and private interiors are avoided where practicable; access restriction to personal-data fields; retention and anonymization/aggregation rules for publication-oriented outputs; and identification of the need for a data-protection impact assessment as an institutional responsibility;
  • The technical specification shall include appropriate safeguards for future field data collection, including respectful interaction with building occupants, protection of personal information, and clear information on available Project GRM channels for submitting feedback or complaints
  • Security: role-based authentication and least-privilege administration, encryption of data in transit and of the central data store, audit logging, separation of test and production environments, and basic vulnerability-management and incident-handling obligations for the developer;
  • Backup and continuity: minimum backup frequency, retention, restoration testing and assignment of responsibility between the operator and the developer during warranty;
  • Source code and intellectual property: full transfer to the Client of source code, build and deployment instructions, configuration and documentation upon acceptance (or an equivalent escrow arrangement where a justified exception is accepted by the Client);
  • Maintenance and sustainability: a maintenance and support skeleton (warranty period, defect severity response categories, update responsibilities) and identification of the institutional operator, required capacity and indicative recurrent resources for operating the solution beyond project completion

Limited field validation — form walkthrough and tabletop simulation

Before finalizing the specification, the Consultant shall validate the draft data-collection form and field workflow through a limited, low-cost exercise that does not require any software development: a structured form walkthrough and tabletop simulation using the draft data dictionary in paper form and/or configured in a generic, freely available survey tool used solely as a mock-up.

  • Scope: indicatively 5–15 buildings in at least two localities (one urban, one rural), covering the predominant building typologies;
  • Participants: Key Expert 2 (and Key Expert 4 for workflow/usability observations), together with Client-designated future evaluators where feasible;
  • Focus: completeness and clarity of fields, controlled lists and evaluator instructions; realistic time per building; photo and GPS practicality; ambiguity and friction points; supervisor/validation steps simulated on the collected sample;
  • Output: a Field Walkthrough and Tabletop Simulation Report (Deliverable D3a) documenting findings and the resulting changes to the data dictionary, forms, workflow and functional requirements, each traceable in the Requirements Traceability Matrix.

For clarity, this exercise is a specification-validation instrument. It is not a statistical screening pilot and does not replace the supervised field pilot of the developed application, which is defined as Stage 2 of acceptance under Section 3.6 and in the subsequent-stage schedule of Section 5.1.

Cross-ToR coordination and Common Data Standard

The Consultant shall participate in the cross-ToR coordination mechanism of Subcomponent 3.1: (i) a joint inception workshop with the consultants of ToRs 1a, 1c and 1d (as mobilized), organized by OEAPM/PIU; (ii) the adoption, within the first 8 weeks, of a common data protocol implementing the Common Data Standard below; and (iii) review gates at Deliverables D3 and D5, to which the consultants of ToRs 1a and 1c shall be invited as reviewers of interoperability aspects.

Common Data Standard (defaults, shared with ToR 1a): coordinate reference system MOLDREF99 (EPSG:4026) for national datasets, with geographic coordinates (WGS84) for GPS capture and conversion rules documented; administrative-unit coding based on CUATM with stable unique building identifiers; controlled building-typology vocabulary compatible with the Activity 1c exposure model; file formats GeoPackage/GeoJSON for spatial data and CSV/XLSX for tabular data; metadata per ISO 19115; and a data-privacy line under Law No. 133/2011 for any building-level data containing personal or sensitive attributes.

Quality Assurance and Technical Requirements

The Consultant shall implement a structured Quality Assurance and Quality Control process for all deliverables prepared under this assignment. The purpose of this process is to ensure that the functional requirements, technical requirements, data model, UAT framework and procurement-ready specification are complete, technically correct, traceable, internally consistent and suitable for review, validation and later use in subsequent application development procurement.

Compatibility with RVS methodology, GD 334 and related Subcomponent 3.1 outputs

The Consultant shall demonstrate that the requirements package is compatible with the RVS methodology described in GD 334 of 05-06-2025 and with the QAP requirements applicable to the RVS mobile application, RVS pilot/field launch and data/GIS deliverables. The requirements shall also be coherent with the future use of RVS data for exposure and vulnerability components of seismic risk analysis.

The Consultant shall prepare a Compatibility Matrix showing the link between the RVS methodology, application functions, data fields, validation rules, export outputs and testing/UAT evidence, including compliance with the Common Data Standard (Section 3.12). This matrix shall be used to confirm that the future application covers all necessary functions and does not create gaps between methodology, field collection and later data processing.

Requirements traceability and data model control

Each requirement shall be traceable from source to specification and from specification to acceptance evidence. The Consultant shall maintain a Requirements Traceability Matrix showing, at minimum: requirement ID, source/rationale, requirement text, priority, related data field or function, test scenario, acceptance criterion and status.

The data model shall be controlled as a formal project output. Any change to field names, data types, domains, mandatory status, validation rules or export structure shall be recorded in the Version Log and, where it affects scope or interpretation, in the Change Log / Change Request.

Internal QA/QC

The Consultant shall carry out internal QA/QC before each official submission. No draft, revised or final deliverable shall be submitted to the Client without prior internal verification by the Consultant.

Internal QA/QC shall cover, at minimum: completeness of the deliverable, consistency of terminology, consistency between requirements and data dictionary, completeness of acceptance criteria, clarity of test scenarios, consistency of user roles and workflow, absence of contradictions between functional and technical requirements, version control and inclusion of all annexes and registers.

The Consultant shall submit an Internal QA/QC Checklist with each major deliverable package. The checklist shall indicate, for each verification item, whether it was checked, by whom, on what date, what issue was identified and how it was resolved.

Peer-review and domain validation

If the Client requires peer-review, the Consultant shall provide all editable requirements documents, matrices, data dictionary, workflow diagrams and test/UAT templates necessary for verification. The Consultant shall address peer-review comments through the Comment Log.

Version Log, Comment Log, Data Register, Test/UAT and NC/CAPA records

The Consultant shall maintain a Version Log for all official submissions. Each submitted version shall have a unique code, version number, date and status. The minimum versioning structure shall include Draft v0.1, Revised/Consolidated v0.2 or higher and Final v1.0.

The Consultant shall maintain a Comment Log for all comments received from MIRD, OEAPM/PIU, the World Bank or other designated reviewers. Comments classified as major shall be closed before the deliverable is proposed as final, unless the Client explicitly agrees otherwise.

The Consultant shall maintain a Data Register / Data Dictionary Register for all datasets, forms, fields and export structures defined by the assignment. The Consultant shall also prepare Test/UAT Register templates and an NC/CAPA Register template for future use during application development and acceptance.

Acceptance of deliverables by the Beneficiary

A deliverable shall be eligible for acceptance only if it meets the scope requirements, is complete, technically clear, traceable, internally consistent and delivered in the required format. For this assignment, acceptance shall require at least the following: main report/specification in DOCX and PDF; Requirements Traceability Matrix; functional requirements; technical requirements; data dictionary; workflow diagrams; QA/UAT framework; test scenarios; acceptance criteria; Version Log; Comment Log; internal QA/QC checklist; and, where applicable, peer-review/domain validation evidence.

A submission shall be considered incomplete if it does not include the supporting annexes, matrices, data dictionary, acceptance criteria, QA records or editable files required for review. Major non-conformities shall block final acceptance. Minor non-conformities may allow “accepted with conditions” only if the condition, responsible party and deadline for closure are recorded in the Comment Log or NC/CAPA Register.

Final acceptance shall be confirmed only in writing by the Client or Beneficiary, through e-mail, minute, handover note or acceptance form, and shall explicitly indicate the accepted version number and date. Submission of a deliverable alone shall not be considered acceptance.

Deliverables and Timeline

The Consultant shall prepare and submit the deliverables listed below. The indicative deadlines are calculated from the contract signing date

 

 

No.

Deliverable

Indicative deadline

D1

Inception Report and Detailed Work Plan (incl. joint inception workshop and common data protocol inputs)

within 4 weeks from contract signing

D2

RVS Methodology, QAP and Field Workflow Review Report (incl. Requirements Source Matrix and the GD 334 typology/seismicity mapping and calibration-readiness framework)

within 7 weeks from contract signing

D3

Draft Functional and Technical Requirements, Data Model and UAT Framework (incl. administration portal, backend, data-governance and security requirements)

within 13 weeks from contract signing

D3a

Field Walkthrough and Tabletop Simulation Report (Section 3.11)

within 15 weeks from contract signing

D4

Draft Procurement-Ready ToR and Technical Specification for Application Development Services

within 17 weeks from contract signing

D5

Final Requirements Package, Procurement-Ready ToR, Data Dictionary, QA/UAT Package and Handover Package (incl. Specification Reading Guide and handover session)

within 20 weeks from contract signing

Note: The review periods of the Client/Beneficiary (indicatively 10 working days for short deliverables and 15 working days for major deliverables, per Section 8.4) are not counted within the Consultant's execution weeks; deadlines above are therefore net of review time. One consolidation round per deliverable (review → revision → resubmission) is included in the timeline; if the Client requires a second full review iteration for a deliverable, the corresponding time shall be added through the Change Request mechanism without penalty to the Consultant.

 

D1. Inception Report and Detailed Work Plan

The Inception Report shall confirm the Consultant’s understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology, work plan, team organization, consultation approach, key risks and proposed structure of the final requirements package. It shall also include a detailed schedule showing all steps from document review to final delivery within the relative timeline above (final package within 20 weeks from contract start), together with the Consultant's inputs to the common data protocol (Section 3.12).

D2. RVS Methodology, QAP and Field Workflow Review Report

This deliverable shall include the review of GD 334 of 05-06-2025, QAP requirements, existing RVS forms/guidelines, expected field workflow, user roles, data quality needs and dependencies with subsequent project activities. It shall include the initial Requirements Source Matrix and a draft list of application modules and data groups, together with the GD 334 typology/seismicity mapping and the calibration-readiness framework (Section 3.1).

D3. Draft Functional and Technical Requirements, Data Model and UAT Framework

This deliverable shall include the first complete draft of functional requirements, technical requirements, user roles, workflow diagrams, data model, data dictionary, validation rules, export requirements, QA/QC logic, test scenarios and UAT acceptance framework, , explicitly covering the administration portal functions, data storage and hosting options, backend database requirements, synchronization re-validation, access control and backup/recovery (Sections 3.4 and 3.10).

D3a. Field Walkthrough and Tabletop Simulation Report

This deliverable shall document the exercise defined in Section 3.11: sample and localities, participants, findings on form completeness, clarity, timing, photo/GPS practicality and workflow friction points, and the resulting traceable changes to the data dictionary, forms and requirements.

D4. Draft Procurement-Ready ToR and Technical Specification for Application Development Services

This deliverable shall include a procurement-ready draft ToR and technical specification for the subsequent acquisition of application development services for the digital data-collection solution. It shall include scope, application modules, required deliverables, implementation timeline, testing/UAT requirements, field-pilot obligations, hosting options and data-governance obligations, handover requirements and acceptance criteria for the application development service provider and shall incorporate the findings of D3a.

D5. Final Requirements Package, Procurement-Ready ToR, Data Dictionary, QA/UAT Package and Handover Package

This deliverable shall include the final consolidated package after Client and Beneficiary comments. The final package shall include the functional and technical requirements, procurement-ready ToR/technical specification, Requirements Traceability Matrix, data dictionary, validation rules, workflow diagrams, Test/UAT Register template, QA/QC checklist, Version Log, Comment Log, Change Log/NC-CAPA templates, the Specification Reading Guide, editable files and PDF versionsIndicative dependency timeline for subsequent Activity 1b stages

 

The Consultant shall take into account the subsequent implementation stages shown in the Activity 1b implementation chart. These stages are not part of the Consultant’s core deliverables under this assignment, but the requirements package must be suitable to support them. The periods below are indicative, are owned by the Client, derive from the Week-0, and have been resequenced so that each stage follows the outputs it depends on.

Subsequent stage

Responsible

Reporting and Format of Deliverables

Language of deliverables, reporting process and final submission package

Deliverables shall be prepared in English. In addition, the following shall be delivered in Romanian: the procurement-ready ToR and technical specification (main document), the data dictionary controlled vocabularies and all evaluator-facing/user-facing texts, the Specification Reading Guide, and executive summaries of D2 and D3. .

Each deliverable shall be submitted in three stages, where applicable: Draft, Revised/Consolidated and Final. Each submitted version shall include a clear document title, deliverable code, version number, date of issue, author/organization and status.

Each official submission shall be accompanied by a short transmittal note listing all files included in the package and identifying the main document to be reviewed. The Consultant shall maintain an updated Version Log and Comment Log throughout the assignment.

Required formats

The final submission package shall include, as applicable:

  • main report / requirements specification in DOCX and PDF;
  • procurement-ready ToR and technical specification for application development services in DOCX and PDF;
  • Requirements Traceability Matrix in XLSX and/or DOCX;
  • Data Dictionary / Data Model in XLSX and/or DOCX;
  • Workflow diagrams in editable format and PDF/PNG;
  • Field Walkthrough and Tabletop Simulation Report (D3a) in DOCX and PDF;
  • Test/UAT Register template and test scenarios in XLSX and/or DOCX;
  • QA/QC checklist, Version Log, Comment Log, Change Log and NC/CAPA templates;
  • README file explaining the folder structure, file purpose, version and use restrictions, if any.

Where GIS export requirements are defined, sample attribute structures, field lists and metadata templates shall be provided in reusable tabular format, aligned with the Common Data Standard (Section 3.12). No final GIS production dataset is expected under this preparatory assignment unless explicitly requested by the Client.

Key Qualification Requirements

The Consultant shall propose a team capable of combining seismic/RVS methodology knowledge, building screening and vulnerability assessment, GIS/spatial data modelling, data quality control and QA/UAT design , together with IT business analysis for digital data-collection systems. The proposed team shall include at least four Key Experts. The Key Experts shall reflect the main technical risk of the assignment: correct definition of RVS field data, vulnerability/exposure indicators, validation logic and data structures for seismic risk analysis - and the correct translation of these into a feasible, consistent and implementable IT specification.

Although the assignment does not include software development or coding, its main output is a procurement-ready specification for a future IT application; the preparation of functional and technical requirements, system workflows, data models, testing procedures and acceptance criteria therefore requires dedicated, evaluated IT expertise within the core team. Additional IT input (e.g. UX/UI, cybersecurity/data protection, database design) may still be mobilized as non-key or short-term support. The methodological weight of the evaluation remains with the seismic/RVS and GIS/data experts (Section 9)..

Key Expert 1 — Team Leader / RVS Methodology and Seismic Risk Specialist

The Team Leader shall be responsible for the overall technical direction of the assignment, methodological coherence, coordination with MIRD/OEAPM/PIU, quality of deliverables and final integration of requirements. Minimum requirements:

  • demonstrated knowledge of building typologies, vulnerability indicators, seismic risk concepts and field assessment/screening methods is a must;
  • degree in civil engineering, structural engineering, earthquake engineering, disaster risk management or a related field;
  • at least 7 years of relevant professional experience in structural/seismic engineering, seismic risk assessment, vulnerability assessment, RVS or technical methodologies for buildings;
  • experience in preparing or coordinating technical methodologies, guidelines, Terms of Reference, technical specifications or institutional reports;
  • ability to translate methodological requirements into practical field data collection requirements and acceptance criteria.
  • attestation as certified technical expert in constructions in the Republic of Moldova, or a designer certificate in the relevant field, shall be considered an advantage.

Key Expert 2 — Building Screening / Seismic Vulnerability Assessment Specialist

The Building Screening / Seismic Vulnerability Assessment Specialist shall be responsible for translating the RVS methodology into practical field screening requirements, building data fields, vulnerability and exposure indicators, evaluator instructions, validation logic and acceptance criteria, and shall lead the form walkthrough and tabletop simulation (Section 3.11). Minimum requirements:

  • degree in civil engineering, structural engineering, earthquake engineering, architecture, disaster risk management or a related field;
  • at least 5 years of professional experience in building assessment, structural/seismic vulnerability assessment, building typology assessment or disaster risk reduction related to buildings;
  • demonstrated knowledge of building typologies, structural systems, visible vulnerability indicators, non-structural risk-relevant observations, occupancy/exposure information and practical field screening constraints;
  • ability to convert methodology provisions into field forms, data collection instructions, controlled answer options, validation rules, quality flags and evaluator guidance;
  • experience with RVS methodologies, building inventory surveys, GIS-linked field data collection, technical guidelines or methodological reports shall be considered an advantage.
  • attestation as certified technical expert in constructions in the Republic of Moldova, or a designer certificate in the relevant field, shall be considered an advantage

Key Expert 3 — GIS, Spatial Data and Data Management Specialist

The GIS, Spatial Data and Data Management Specialist shall be responsible for the data model, spatial attributes, export requirements, metadata, identifiers, data quality controls and interoperability with GIS/seismic risk analysis workflows, including compliance with the Common Data Standard (Section 3.12). Minimum requirements:

  • degree in GIS, geoinformatics, geography, civil engineering, data science, computer science or a related field;
  • at least 5 years of professional experience in GIS, spatial data management, database design, geospatial datasets or field data collection systems;
  • demonstrated experience with data dictionaries, metadata, coordinate reference systems, GIS-compatible formats such as GeoPackage/GeoJSON and tabular exports such as XLSX/CSV;
  • ability to define validation rules, unique identifiers, attribute structures and export packages suitable for quality control and later integration into risk analysis;
  • experience with building inventory, infrastructure datasets or disaster risk data shall be considered an advantage.

Key Expert 4 — IT Business Analyst / Digital Data Collection Specialist

The IT Business Analyst / Digital Data Collection Specialist shall be responsible for the feasibility, consistency and implementability of the specification as an IT product: structuring the functional and technical requirements, system workflows, backend/portal requirements, testability of acceptance criteria and coherence between the data model and the future implementation. Minimum requirements:

  • degree in computer science, software engineering, information systems, business informatics or a related field;
  • at least 5 years of professional experience in business analysis or requirements engineering for software systems, digital data-collection solutions or information systems for public or institutional clients;
  • demonstrated experience in preparing functional and technical specifications, data models, workflow definitions, test/UAT frameworks or acceptance criteria for software procurement or development;
  • experience with mobile/offline field data-collection platforms or survey/inventory systems shall be considered an advantage;
  • experience with IT procurement under World Bank or other IFI/public-sector procurement frameworks shall be considered an advantage.

Non-Key Experts / Optional Specialists

The Consultant may propose non-key experts as needed, including a UX/UI specialist, cybersecurity/data protection specialist, database developer, mobile application developer,, QA/UAT specialist, procurement/ToR drafting specialist, training specialist or field data collection specialist. These experts may support specific parts of the assignment, particularly the formulation of implementation-neutral technical requirements, test scenarios, user roles, data security, deployment assumptions and handover requirements. They shall not be considered Key Experts for evaluation purposes, but their involvement may be assessed as part of the Consultant’s organization, methodology and ability to deliver a complete and implementable package.

The Consultant may also demonstrate that members of the proposed technical team have practical experience with digital survey tools, mobile data collection, GIS-linked forms or database exports. This is acceptable, provided that the final requirements package remains clear enough for a future application developer to implement and for MIRD/OEAPM/PIU to test and accept.

Client’s Inputs and Institutional Coordination

Available documents

The Client shall provide, to the extent available, the relevant project documents and inputs necessary for the assignment, including: QAP for Subcomponent 3.1, implementation chart for Activity 1b, RVS methodology described in GD 334 of 05-06-2025, existing RVS forms or guidelines, relevant seismic risk map methodology inputs, data/GIS requirements, institutional comments and any other documents needed for preparing the requirements package, as well as the preliminary administrative-unit hazard values from Activity 1a as they become available (handoff H1, Section 3.12).

Coordination with MIRD and OEAPM/PIU

OEAPM/PIU shall act as the main operational and contractual coordination point. MIRD shall act as the main Beneficiary for technical review, institutional validation and acceptance. The Consultant shall coordinate all official submissions through the channels indicated by OEAPM/PIU.

Access to stakeholders and users

The Client shall facilitate, where feasible, consultations with future users or institutional stakeholders, including potential field evaluators, data validators, GIS users and MIRD/OEAPM/PIU reviewers and shall facilitate access to the localities and building samples for the form walkthrough under Section 3.11. The Consultant shall prepare the materials for these consultations and record decisions, comments and follow-up actions.

Comments on deliverables

Comments shall be transmitted in writing, preferably in consolidated form, within the review period agreed in the work plan. For planning purposes, the ToR may assume 10 working days for review of short deliverables and 15 working days for review of major deliverables, unless otherwise agreed. These review periods are subject to the clock-stop rule in Section 5.

The Consultant shall respond to all comments through the Comment Log. Comments classified as major shall be closed before the deliverable is submitted as final, unless the Client explicitly agrees otherwise. If comments require changes to scope, requirements logic, data model, deadlines or procurement assumptions, the issue shall be recorded as a Change Request, where applicable.

Technical meetings and consultations

As a minimum, the assignment should include: one inception meeting (combined with the joint inception workshop under Section 3.12 where practicable), one RVS methodology and workflow review meeting, one requirements/data model review meeting, one draft technical specification review meeting and one final validation/presentation meeting (combined with the handover session under Section 3.8). Additional meetings may be organized if required by the complexity of comments or by the need to resolve technical issues.

After each meeting, the Consultant shall record the main conclusions, decisions, actions, responsible parties and deadlines. These records shall support the traceability of decisions and revisions made during the assignment.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Individual Selection)

Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor

Country

Ethiopia

Project

Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project

Project ID

P179040

Assignment Title

Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor

Reference No.

ET-NIDP-573612-CS-INDV

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. The National ID Program (NIDP), the ultimate project implementer, intends to apply part of the proceeds to select an individual consultant.

The National ID Program is looking for a Senior Personal Data Protection Existing and Emerging Technologies – Technical Advisor located at the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) to support the implementation of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project with respect to providing high-level technical expertise in translating the requirements of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation into practical and technically implementable standards, safeguards, and supervisory mechanisms, among others.

The primary objective of the assignment is to provide high-level technical expertise to support ECA in translating the requirements of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation into practical and technically implementable standards, safeguards, and supervisory mechanisms. The Advisor will bridge technology, cybersecurity, data governance and privacy, enabling ECA to assess risks associated with existing and emerging technologies, strengthen technical compliance audits and DPIA assessments, develop appropriate standards and assessment tools, advise on data localization and cross-border data transfers, support breach-response mechanisms, and enhance the Authority’s oversight of digital platforms and data markets.

Scope of Service and specific tasks

     Scope of Services

The Technical Advisor shall provide specialized technical advisory, assessment, regulatory development, capacity-building, and supervisory support to the Authority in the implementation and enforcement of the Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 and other applicable legal and regulatory instruments.

The scope of services shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

  • Technology Foresight and Advisory: Advise ECA on the privacy, cybersecurity, and regulatory implications of existing and emerging technologies.
  • Technical Standards Development: Develop technical standards, guidelines, and security baselines for secure personal data processing, storage, and transfer.
  • Technical Risk Assessments: Conduct system reviews, security assessments, and DPIAs for high-risk personal data processing activities.
  • Technical Compliance and Supervision: Develop audit tools and support ECA's inspections and technical compliance assessments of data controllers and processors.
  • Breach and Incident Response: Develop incident-response procedures and support technical investigations, root-cause analysis, and remediation monitoring.
  • Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement: Develop training materials and deliver technical training and workshops for ECA staff and relevant stakeholders.
  • Technical Coordination and Other Duties: Collaborate with relevant ECA departments and stakeholders and undertake related assignments directed by ECA leadership within the scope of the assignment.

   Specific Tasks

Based on the above Scope of Service, the Technical Advisor shall perform the following specific tasks:

  • Technology Foresight and Strategic Technical Advisory
  • Development of Technical Standards and Security Baselines
  • Technical Assessments, System Reviews, and DPIAs
  • Technical Compliance Audits and Supervisory Support
  • Personal Data Breach and Security Incident Management
  • Technical Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement
  • Reporting, Knowledge Management, and Additional Assignments

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

The candidate is required to have the following minimum Qualifications and Experience:

  • A Master's degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Telecommunications/Communications Engineering or a related field;
  • At least seven (7) years of relevant professional experience in cyber security, technology strategy, digital transformation, data architecture, emerging technologies, technology governance or a related field;
  • Strong knowledge and demonstrated practical understanding of AI, biometrics, digital identity, cloud computing, privacy-enhancing technologies, data technologies and other emerging technologies;
  • Good understanding of personal data protection, privacy by design and by default, and technology-related regulatory requirements;
  • Experience working with digital public infrastructure, telecommunications, financial services or other complex technology environments is an advantage;
  • Experience or knowledge in RegTech and technology-enabled regulatory solutions is desirable;
  • Strong analytical, research, communication and report-writing skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues to legal, policy and regulatory audiences;
  • Relevant professional certifications in data protection, privacy, cybersecurity, information technology or related fields are an advantage; and
  • Excellent command of written and spoken English and Amharic.

Duration and Location

The consultant will be engaged on a full-time basis for an initial period of twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget. The position will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopian Communication Authority (ECA)

The Technical Advisor shall report to the Director General or the designated Deputy Director General/Director responsible for personal data protection, or another designated ECA supervisor. The Advisor shall work in close coordination with the Personal Data Protection Directorate and other relevant ECA departments.

The Advisor shall submit deliverables in editable electronic format, together with supporting technical documentation, assessment tools, and presentation materials where applicable. Reports containing sensitive information shall be handled in accordance with ECA's applicable confidentiality, information-security, and records-management requirements.

Selection Method

The selection method is based on paragraphs 7.36 and 7.37 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations. The attention of interested individuals is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” July 2016, as revised, including February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An individual will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultant (Section V) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Submission of Expression of Interest

National ID Program, Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Expression of Interest should include a CV, formal application/cover letter, and documentary evidence supporting the stated qualifications and experience, including descriptions of relevant assignments and experience in similar conditions.

Expressions of interest must be submitted by e-mail on or before November 16, 2026.

Further information may be obtained by e-mail during office hours from 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM Addis Ababa time.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Individual Selection)

Senior Personal Data Protection Compliance & Audit Advisor

Country

Ethiopia

Project

Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project

Project ID

P179040

Assignment Title

Senior Personal Data Protection Compliance & Audit Advisor

Reference No.

ET-NIDP-573615-CS-INDV

Required No.

1 (one)

Organization

Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA)

Duty Station

Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA), Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Employment Type

Contract

Duration

12 months, with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Finance (MoF), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Ethiopia Digital ID for Inclusion and Services Project. The National ID Program (NIDP), the ultimate project implementer, intends to apply part of the proceeds for selecting an individual consultant.

The National ID Program is seeking a Senior Personal Data Protection Compliance & Audit Advisor to support the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) in strengthening ECA’s personal data protection compliance, audit, inspection, risk assessment, and regulatory supervision functions under Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 and applicable subsidiary legislation, directives, standards, and guidelines.

1. Background

The Government of Ethiopia has established a comprehensive legal framework for the protection of personal data through Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024. The Proclamation designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) as the national authority responsible for regulating and enforcing personal data protection.

ECA’s mandate includes, among others, registration and supervision of data controllers and processors, compliance monitoring, investigation of violations and complaints, development of regulatory instruments, and enforcement of personal data protection requirements. The Proclamation establishes obligations concerning lawful and fair processing, purpose limitation, storage limitation, security and confidentiality, data-subject rights, registration of controllers and processors, Data Protection Officers, technical and organizational measures, breach notification, Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), and privacy by design.

The implementation of these requirements requires ECA to develop a risk-based, systematic and evidence-based compliance and audit capability capable of assessing whether public and private sector organizations are effectively complying with the Proclamation and applicable subsidiary legislation, directives, standards and guidelines. This is further reinforced by Digital Ethiopia 2030, which assigns ECA an expanded role in implementing personal data protection and exercising proactive oversight of digital platforms and data markets.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The overall purpose of the assignment is to provide senior-level professional expertise to strengthen ECA’s personal data protection compliance, audit, inspection and supervisory functions. The Advisor will support ECA in developing and implementing a risk-based compliance and audit framework for data controllers and processors; conducting compliance assessments and audits; identifying systemic and sector-specific privacy risks; assessing technical and organizational measures; supporting DPIA and high-risk processing assessments; developing audit tools and methodologies; monitoring corrective actions; and providing evidence-based recommendations for regulatory intervention and enforcement.

The Advisor shall also support ECA in translating the personal data protection objectives of Digital Ethiopia 2030 into practical supervisory mechanisms for digital platforms, data-driven businesses, emerging technologies and data markets.

3. Scope of Services / Key Responsibilities

The Advisor will:

  • Establish risk-based frameworks, indicators, maturity models, and annual plans for supervisory inspections, audits, desk reviews, and regulatory follow-ups.
  • Plan and lead audits to assess compliance with Proclamation No. 1321/2024 and other applicable laws and directives, evaluating entities’ governance structures, DPO arrangements, policy enforcement, registration accuracy, and data-subject rights implementation.
  • Evaluate the adequacy of technical controls, including access management, encryption, logging, backup, physical security, data localization, cloud arrangements, and cross-border transfer safeguards.
  • Review Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) and assess risks linked to high-risk processing, digital platforms, data monetization, and emerging technologies, including AI, biometrics, digital ID, cloud, IoT and fintech.
  • Assess breach preparedness, investigate root causes and control failures in reported incidents, review notification compliance, and oversee remedial action plans.
  • Provide technical evidence, risk ratings, and recommendations to support ECA’s regulatory inquiries, enforcement actions, corrective orders, and administrative sanctions.
  • Formulate standardized supervisory toolkits, including audit manuals, inspection checklists, sector guidelines, DPIA/breach assessment templates, and compliance dashboards.
  • Deliver technical training, develop audit materials, mentor ECA inspection teams, and facilitate awareness workshops with controllers, processors, and peer data protection authorities.
  • Execute any additional assignments directed by ECA leadership to support ECA’s mandate.

4. Minimum Qualifications and Professional Experience

The candidate should have:

  • A minimum of a Master’s degree in Information Technology; Computer Science; Cybersecurity; Information Security; Information Systems; Data Science/Data Engineering; Computer Engineering; Telecommunications Engineering; Digital Transformation; Privacy/Data Protection; Risk Management; or another closely related discipline.
  • At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in personal data protection, privacy compliance, information security, technology risk, IT audit, cybersecurity, data governance, regulatory compliance, or related fields.
  • Of which at least five (5) years shall involve substantial experience in personal data protection/privacy compliance, IT audit, information-security auditing, regulatory supervision, or data-governance assessment.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting compliance audits, IT audits, privacy assessments, security assessments or regulatory inspections.
  • Demonstrated experience developing compliance frameworks, audit methodologies, risk assessment tools and supervisory mechanisms.
  • Experience assessing cloud environments, data centers, digital platforms, data-sharing arrangements and third-party processors.
  • Experience in data breach assessment and incident-response compliance.
  • Experience working in a multi-stakeholder regulatory environment.
  • Good communication skills in both English and Amharic.

5. Duration and Location

The consultant will be engaged on a full-time basis for an initial period of twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and availability of budget. The position will be based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA).

The Advisor shall report to the Deputy Director General responsible for Personal Data Protection at ECA, or another designated ECA supervisor, and shall work in close coordination with the Personal Data Protection Directorate and other relevant ECA departments.

6. Selection Method

data.notice_text:
ADDENDUM No 1

 TO THE REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

The Republic of Azerbaijan

Project Preparation in relation to: Competitive and Resilient Agriculture and Irrigation Services (CRAIS) Project

Loan/Grant No.: TF0D1739

Assignment Title: Review and Updating of Feasibility Studies, Technical Assessments and Detailed Engineering Design for Irrigation Schemes

Reference No.: CRAIS-P515925-CS-CQS/1

CLARIFICATION RESPONSES REGARDING THE TERMS OF REFERENCE

The following clarifications are provided to ensure a common understanding among all prospective consultants of the scope of the assignment.

As set out in the Terms of Reference (TOR), the assignment is structured in three phases:

  • Phase 1 covers review of existing studies, feasibility studies, technical-economic assessments, conceptual designs, hydraulic data, operational records, and intensive technical consultations with ASWRA, irrigation institutions, local stakeholders, and relevant government entities regarding rehabilitation and modernization priorities for the irrigation schemes under Component 1 validating the viability and readiness of the irrigation schemes for World Bank financing, and identifying the needs and scope for updating existing documentation.
  • Phase 2 covers the preparation or updating of the necessary technical and economic assessments and feasibility studies for all viable sub-projects identified under Phase 1. The selected priority sub-project will be addressed as a priority to inform the subsequent detailed design work. The feasibility-level work for the remaining viable schemes should provide the necessary inputs for CRAIS project appraisal.
  • Phase 3 is limited to the selected priority sub-project and covers the detailed engineering design and preparation or updating of the technical documentation required to bring that sub-project to full procurement and implementation readiness.

Accordingly, the clarifications below should be read together with the TOR and do not amend the scope of the assignment.

No.

Question / Issue Raised

Clarification

1.1

Is it intended to assess the existing technical documentation for all four projects against the requirements of the World Bank and identify any gaps?

Yes. Under Phase 1, the Consultant is required to review the existing feasibility studies, technical-economic assessments, conceptual designs, expert review reports, hydraulic analyses, preliminary technical studies, as-built drawings and operational records for the irrigation schemes under Component 1. Based on this review and consultations, the Consultant shall prepare a readiness assessment for each scheme covering, among other matters, data completeness, technical adequacy of the existing studies, key gaps, the estimated effort required for updating, and a preliminary ranking of readiness for financing. The purpose is to validate the viability and readiness of the proposed schemes for World Bank financing and identify the needs and scope for further work.

1.2

Will the analysis for the other three non-priority projects be conducted only at the feasibility study level, or will corrections and updates also be made to their existing project documentation?

Please refer to Section 3. Scope of Work of the disclosed TOR. Under Phase 2, the Consultant is required to prepare or update the necessary technical and economic assessments and feasibility studies for all viable sub-projects identified under Phase 1 to inform the CRAIS project appraisal. Section 3.2 of the disclosed TOR clearly states that Phase 2 is not limited to the selected priority/readiest scheme; all FSs for the viable schemes need to be updated as much as possible, as needed to complete the project appraisal. The level and extent of such updates should be consistent with the requirements of the TOR, including the essential inputs needed for project appraisal. Upon completion of works under Phase 2, the Consultants are required to deliver an Updated Feasibility Study Report for all viable sub-projects, including preferred options, preliminary technical solutions, indicative quantities and costs, economic/financial analyses, climate-resilience and SCADA recommendations, dam-safety findings, and indicative implementation schedules.

1.3

Which technical, economic, environmental and social criteria are expected to be taken as a basis when selecting the priority canal?

Please refer to Section 3. Scope of Work of the disclosed TOR. In accordance with the TOR, the recommendation of the priority/readiest sub-project shall be based on technical completeness of existing documentation, data availability, economic justification, climate-resilience benefits, dam-safety considerations, implementation readiness, and overall contribution to the objectives of Component 1. The Consultant's Phase 1 review and readiness assessment should provide the basis for this recommendation.

2.1

What is the technical and functional connection between the works envisaged for the Yengija Reservoir and the objectives and irrigation systems of the CRAIS Project?

The reference to Yengija in the TOR should be understood in the context of the Project Dam Dependency Note, which has a project-wide scope and covers all three CRAIS components. The TOR requires the Consultant to review dam dependency for dams on which the Project relies for water resources or whose failure could affect Project facilities. Yengija, which is under construction, is specifically mentioned as an example to be considered in relation to the Water Users Association/irrigation pilot under Component 2 in the Gabala district. Its inclusion in this context does not imply a technical or hydrological connection with the Component 1 irrigation schemes supplied through the Araz River and Bahramtapa Hydrojunction.

2.2

Which technical or project documents justify the inclusion of the works on the Yengija Reservoir within the scope of this consultancy service?

The Consultant's responsibility in relation to Yengija arises from the TOR requirement to prepare a Project Dam Dependency Note covering all three CRAIS components. The relevant task is to identify dams, including dams under construction, on which the Project relies for water resources or whose failure could affect Project facilities, and to assess the consequences of dam failure as required under the TOR. The reference to Yengija does not require detailed feasibility, engineering design or other works for the reservoir itself under this consultancy assignment.

2.3

Is the inclusion of the relevant paragraph in the TOR a technical error, a provision left over from a previous project, or related to an expansion of the project's scope?

The primary scope of this consultancy assignment is focused on the key irrigation schemes fed by the Araz River via the Bahramtapa Hydrojunction (including the Bash Mughan canal network). It reflects the broader scope of the Project Dam Dependency Note, which, as specified in the TOR, covers all three components of the CRAIS Project.

NATIONAL OFFICE FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECTS (NOIEP)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants)

(Call for local consultants only)

Procurement consultant (specialist)

Date: November 02, 2026

REPUBLIC OF MOLDOVA

GEF/WB  Project: Restoring ecosystems for marine pollution prevention” (ReMaP) (P505546) and upcoming “Expanding Sustainable Land and Biodiversity Management” TerraMoldova (P514338) 

Assignment Title: Procurement consultant

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MD-NOIEP-573625-CS-INDV

Moldova “Restoring Ecosystems for Marine Pollution Prevention” (REMAP) Project, financed by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and supported by the World Bank, is implemented through the National Office for the Implementation of Environmental Projects (NOIEP) under the Ministry of Environment (MoE). REMAP is a flagship national initiative promoting Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to restore ecosystems and reduce land-based pollution in the Dniester River Basin. The project aligns with Moldova’s priorities under the EU approximation agenda, the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and the Paris Agreement, demonstrating that healthy, community-supported ecosystems underpin climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods.

TerraMoldova’s development objective is to reverse ecological decline in Moldova's landscapes by scaling SLM practices and NbS-based restoration across priority ecosystems. The project is structured around three components: (i) strengthening knowledge, capacity, and environmental governance for EU alignment, including modernizing biodiversity monitoring systems and establishing a national ecological knowledge platform; (ii) revitalizing biodiversity and SLM through field-based NbS interventions across wetlands and riparian corridors (at least 250 ha), degraded forest landscapes (at least 500 ha), and agroecosystems including vineyard mosaics (at least 500 ha); and (iii) project coordination, M&E, and knowledge management. Site selection is guided by the NNRP and the ReMaP project assessment, targeting ecological corridors, buffer zones, fragmented forest blocks, erosion-prone slopes, and priority catchments. The project is expected to generate indirect ecological benefits across an additional 2,500–3,750 ha beyond its direct intervention areas.

TerraMoldova is designed to complement REMAP: while REMAP addresses the broader institutional and administrative framework for land management, TerraMoldova delivers targeted field-level NbS and ecological restoration within that framework, focusing on high-value ecological zones and biodiversity conservation. The two projects share a common vision of sustainable land management and climate resilience, and their activities are coordinated to maximize synergies — including through shared site prioritization informed by the ReMaP assessment — while remaining technically and operationally independent. Both projects are implemented through NOEPI, which operates under the MoE and serves as the fiduciary agency.

The procurement consultant will play a crucial role in assisting the Project Coordinator and Project team with the effective implementation of the operational procurement system. This will be done in full compliance with the financing agreement, project operational manual for both RE-MAP TerraMoldova in one document (updated accordingly including TerraMoldova Project), and the procurement regulations set forth by the World Bank (WB). The Procurement Specialist’s primary responsibility is to ensure smooth, transparent, and efficient procurement processes throughout the life cycle of the project.

The minimum qualifications and experience for this position are:

  • University degree/master’s degree in economics, law, public administration or related fields.
  • Demonstrated practical experience and in-depth knowledge of procurement rules and procedures of the World Bank and/or international organizations or agencies as international donors.
  • At least 5 years of working experience as a procurement specialist (consultant) in projects financed by the IFI and/or similar international organizations/agencies.
  • Knowledge and practical experience working with the World Bank’s procurement systems, including experience in the Bank’s STEP will be an asset and will be given significant weight in the evaluation.
  • Advanced knowledge of Romanian and English (spoken and written).
  • Excellent knowledge of computer applications (MS Office suite, etc.).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Individual Consultants will be selected in accordance with the „Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants” method set out in the above-mentioned “Procurement Regulations”. Expressions of interest namely “Procurement consultant” must include updated CV reflecting consultant's qualification and experience, recommendation letters, if any and must be submitted by email to the address below by November 16, 2026, cob.
