REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-IC-NIO-13-R – Infrastructure Manager)

Market Approach - Open, National

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant No. TF0C5794

 

Assignment Title: Infrastructure Manager

Reference No. LEARN-IC-NIO-13-R

 

Ukraine has signed agreements with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter – the World Bank) for the "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine" Program (hereinafter – LEARN, or the Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, in line with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine through 2027.

The Operation focuses on supporting priorities "1. Early Childhood and Pre-school Education" and "2. New Ukrainian School Reform," as set out in the Strategic Plan. The objectives of the Operation are: (i) improving teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthening the management capacity of the education system.

The objective of the Consultant's assignment is to provide coordination and expert-analytical support to the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in updating the regulatory-legal framework and technical regulations relating to the construction, reconstruction, major repair, and fit-out of general secondary education institutions (school infrastructure), including with due regard to the principles of inclusiveness, barrier-free access, and universal design.

The Infrastructure Manager will be responsible for coordinating and providing analytical and expert support for processes related to updating the regulatory-legal and regulatory-technical documentation (a set of documents — technical regulations, standards, norms, and technical specifications — defining requirements for products, production processes, technical means, and manufacturing methods); will ensure analysis of current standards and approaches to shaping the educational space; will participate in preparing proposals for their improvement; and will coordinate engagement with stakeholders on the development of modern, safe, inclusive, and accessible education infrastructure in line with the principles of the "New Ukrainian School" reform and the development of the "Building Back Better Physical Learning Environments" (BFB PLEs) strategy.

 

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

REPUBLIC OF MOZAMBIQUE

MINISTRY OF PUBLIC WORKS, HOUSING AND WATER RESOURCES

WATER SUPPLY AND SANITATION INVESTMENT AND ASSETS FUND – FIPAAS

 

URBAN WATER SECURITY PROGRAM – P509890

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST Nº. FIPAAS/UWSP/CON-02/26

 

CONSULTING SERVICES FOR DETAILED ENGINEERING DESIGN, SUPERVISION AND ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL INSTRUMENTS FOR WATER SUPPLY AND SANITATION INFRASTRUCTURE FOR VILANKULO, PAMBARRA AND MAPINHANE

 

1.     The Government of Mozambique, through the Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources (MOPHRH), has received financing from the World Bank under the Urban Water Security Program (P509890), to be implemented in the Greater Maputo Metropolitan Area and the Southern Region, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract FIPAG/UWSP/CON-02/26 – Consulting Services for Detailed Engineering Design, Supervision and Environmental And Social Instruments for Water Supply and Sanitation Infrastructure for Vilankulo, Pambarra and Mapinhane.

 

2 .     The services include: (i) review of the 2021 studies and detailed engineering design of the water supply infrastructure, the Faecal Sludge Treatment Plant and public sanitation blocks in Vilankulo, Mapinhane and Pambarra; (ii) preparation of the environmental and social instruments and tender documents; and (iii) construction supervision. The expected duration is 10 months for the detailed design (Lump-Sum) and 28 months for construction supervision, including a 12-month Defects Liability Period.

3.       The Water Supply and Sanitation Investment and Assets Fund (FIPAAS) invites eligible firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants must provide valid information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, etc.).

 

4.      Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, 7th Edition, September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

5.     The firms are also drawn to paragraph 3.32, of the Section III, related to prohibited practices (fraud, corruption, collusion, coercion, and obstruction) and the Consultants found to have engaged in such practices will be declared ineligible for World Bankfinanced contracts.

 

6.     Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a subconsultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

7.      The Consultant shall be a Civil Engineering consulting firm with: (i) - A minimum of 15 (fifteen) years of general experience in the water and sanitation sector; (ii) - At least 10 (ten) years of specific experience in Sub-Saharan Africa; (iii) - have successfully executed at least three (3) projects of hydraulic infrastructure, with similar nature, which may include, but are not limited to: (a) Water supply systems; (b) Sanitation infrastructure; (c) Hydraulic infrastructure for water resources management; (d) Irrigation and (e) productive water use schemes, (iv) - demonstrate experience in assignments implemented under FIDIC Conditions of Contract and/or projects financed by international financing institutions or other internationally financed development programmes, (v) - demonstrate experience with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), (vi) - World Bank procurement requirements, or equivalent environmental, social and procurement frameworks applied by other international financing institutions, (vii) – have at least six (6) water supply system projects in Sub-Saharan Africa, each including: (a) Surface water abstraction and intake works; (b) Conventional water treatment plants; (c) Reinforced concrete reservoirs with a minimum storage capacity of ≥ 5,000 m³;  (d) Distribution networks with pipe diameters of ≥ 500 mm and (viii) – have at least three (3) detailed engineering designs of sanitation infrastructure, including faecal sludge treatment plants (FSTPs) and associated facilities.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Georgia

Anaklia Rail Hinterland Connectivity Project

Assignment Title: Supervision of Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port

Reference No. GE-GR-577262-CS-QCBS

The Government of Georgia intends to apply for financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Project, and JSC Georgian Railway intends to utilize part of the proceeds towards payments under the contract for “Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port”, as well as for consulting services (the Services).

 

The Services include “Supervision of Design and Build of a Railway and Related Infrastructure Connecting to the Anaklia Deep-Sea Port”. The Project envisages design and construction of a railway line with its supporting infrastructure, electrification, construction of overpasses and underpasses, drainage channels and pipes, construction of a new railway station “Anaklia”, construction of Khamiskuri junction, reconstruction of existing railway station “Khobi” and construction of service facilities. The Project territory is located between the village Khamiskuri and the Black Sea from East to West direction. From North it is bordered by the rivers Jumi and Enguri, from South – by the villages of Khobi municipality: Tsvane, Mogiri and Torsa. Eastern (about 4km) and Western (about 9km) parts of the territory are uninhabited. Its middle part (about 4km) is populated (the villages: Ergeta, Didi Nedzi and Orulu). The railway line starts at Khamiskuri and ends near the Port area in Anaklia. The total length of the line is approximately 17.74km.

 

The primary objectives of the Consulting Services are as follows: (i) review the Contractor’s detailed design and verify its compliance with the Employer’s Requirements; (ii) function as the Engineer in administering the works contract and execution of all rights and responsibilities of the Engineer in accordance with the “Conditions of Contract for Plant & Design-Build for Electrical & Mechanical Plant & for Building & Engineering Works Designed by the Contractor (“Yellow book”) Second edition 2017, reprinted 2022 with amendments”; (iii) comprehensive supervision of design activities and works carried out by the Contractor to ensure compliance with the drawings, technical specifications and various stipulations contained in the contract documents, with high standards of quality assurance in supervision and in the execution of works; (iv) advise the Client on all matters concerning the contract management and support the Client to have the works completed within the stipulated time for completion and budget.

 

The Consultant is expected to provide 369 person-months (full-time field presence) of consulting services. The Services will be provided over a period of 48 months (including 30 months of design and construction supervision and 18 months of Defects Notification Period).

 

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the link below:

https://georgianrailway-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/gr_conference_railway_ge/IgAru-htvbxaQbpIIYH0Di0iARskrIr3sxsRaN3outlrMgE?e=el2SiM

 

JSC Georgian Railway now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. 

 

The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

  • General experience in railway infrastructure projects;
  • Similar experience in supervision of railway construction assignments within the last 10 years (i.e., since January 2017).

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. GR reserves the right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

 

The shortlist will consist of five (5) to eight (8) eligible firms.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025, seventh edition (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The consultant shall not receive any payment in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. data.institution: Ministry of  Economic Development and Youth Economy
data.notice_text:
GOVERNMENT OF SAINT LUCIA

MINISTRY OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND YOUTH ECONOMY

 

Request for Expressions of Interest

Consulting Services — Firms Selection

Project: OECS Data for Decision Making Project — Saint Lucia Component
Project ID: P174986
Credit / Financing No.: 71120
Procurement Reference No.: SLU-DDM-TECADVISR-CSO-QCBS-26


Notice Date: October 28, 2026

Assignment: Consultancy to Provide Technical Assistance to the CSO to Upgrade the Statistical Business Register IT Infrastructure and Improve the Coverage and Quality of Business Statistics

The Government of Saint Lucia has received World Bank financing for the OECS Data for Decision Making Project and intends to use part of this financing for the consulting services described below. The Ministry of Economic Development and Youth Economy, through its Project Implementation Unit, invites eligible consulting firms to submit expressions of interest.

Assignment scope

The firm will support the Central Statistics Office (CSO) in improving the completeness, coverage, content and functionality of its Statistical Business Register (SBR), upgrading its IT environment and strengthening the production and use of quality business statistics. The services comprise:

  • Assessment and improvement planning: Review legislation, protocols and practices used by custodians of economic administrative records; assess the maturity of the CSO’s SBR; and prepare recommendations and an SBR Improvement Plan aligned with relevant international standards and frameworks.
  • SBR systems upgrade and data integration: Implement approved improvements to the existing SQL-based client-server relational database system; update features and functionality; and use Enterprise Census and economic administrative data to improve coverage, content and business survey sampling frames.
  • Classification consistency and migration: Promote consistent use of the International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC), concepts and definitions across the CSO and custodians of economic administrative data; review guidance for ISIC Revision 5; and prepare an ISIC 5 migration plan.
  • Business statistics and quality assurance: Strengthen statistical business processes and protocols for producing structural and business demography statistics, developing metadata and assuring quality, with reference to the System of National Accounts 2008/2025, UN statistical business register guidelines and the UN National Quality Assurance Framework 2019.
  • Deployment, documentation and knowledge transfer: Test and deploy the upgraded SBR; address defects and incorporate CSO feedback; prepare systems documentation, a Service Level Agreement, a maintenance manual and a user guide; and facilitate at least two consultation, training and sensitisation workshops for the CSO and custodians of economic administrative records.

 

Principal outputs include an inception report and work plan; a Situational Analysis Report incorporating the SBR Improvement Plan, ISIC Improvement and Migration Plan, and proposed uses of SBR data; a functioning and tested SBR; a deployed “go live” SBR with approved features, systems documentation, Service Level Agreement, maintenance manual and user guide; and a Final Summary Report covering the work performed and consultancy deliverables.

Duration: Six (6) months from contract signing. Tentative commencement: January 2027. Most work will be home-based, with occasional travel to Saint Lucia according to a mutually agreed timetable. The firm will report to the CSO Director of Statistics and liaise closely with the Deputy Project Coordinator and the Permanent Secretary, Department of Economic Development. The detailed TOR accompanies this notice.

Firm qualifications and shortlisting criteria

Interested firms should provide evidence of their relevant experience and capacity to field the multidisciplinary team specified in the TOR. Shortlisting will consider:

  • Experience developing or upgrading statistical business registers, administrative register systems or relational databases, and implementing IT systems that use administrative records.
  • Technical capacity in database management systems, including SQL Server, MySQL or PostgreSQL, and in the design, implementation, testing, deployment and maintenance of register systems.
  • Experience applying international standards and frameworks for statistical business registers, including the UN Guidelines for Statistical Business Registers and the UN Maturity Model for Statistical Business Registers.
  • Experience applying ISIC and the Central Product Classification, supporting classification revisions or migration, and promoting consistent statistical concepts and definitions across institutions.
  • Experience analysing official business statistics and producing technical reports or policy briefs on structural and business demography statistics, using relevant international frameworks and quality assurance standards.
  • Experience consulting with diverse stakeholders and delivering training, sensitisation workshops, technical guidance and knowledge transfer.
  • Capacity to mobilise and manage a team covering SBR systems development, statistical classifications, and structural and business demography statistics, as specified in the TOR.

Shortlisting will assess the firm’s qualifications, relevant experience and organisational capacity. Individual Key Experts will be assessed at the proposal stage rather than during shortlisting. The TOR identifies a Lead Expert / Statistical Business Register Expert, an ISIC Expert, and a Structural and Business Demography Statistics Expert; their detailed education, experience and skills requirements are set out in the TOR.

Information to submit

Submit a signed expression of interest in English, a firm profile describing its core business and years of operation, and details of relevant completed assignments. For each assignment, identify the client, country, dates, scope, services performed, completion status and a reference contact. Describe the firm’s technical, managerial and training capacity and provide supporting evidence. Identify any proposed association and the responsibilities of its members. A financial proposal is not requested at this stage.

Selection and conflict of interest

Selection will use Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS), in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers applicable to the Project. Interested firms must observe the conflict-of-interest provisions in Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of those Regulations.

Associations may take the form of a joint venture or sub-consultancy and must be identified in the submission. If selected, joint venture members will share joint and several liability for performance of the contract.

Submission and enquiries

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 08:00–16:30 Atlantic Standard Time (AST, UTC−04:00).

Expressions of interest must be received by November 18 at 9.30 am Eastern Caribbean Time (ECT)   AST (UTC−04:00) through the Government of Saint Lucia Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) System: https://in-tendhost.co.uk/goslprocurement/.

Submissions shall include a cover page displaying the consulting firm’s name and address and shall be clearly marked “EOI — Statistical Business Register Upgrade and Business Statistics — [insert approved procurement reference]”.

 

Further information and the TOR may be requested from:
Project Implementation Unit

Address: 2nd Floor Financial Administrative Centre, Pointe Seraphine, Castries, Saint Lucia
Email: oecsddmproject@gmail.com

(CONSULTING SERVICES -INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

The AmharaNationalRegional State Bureau of Labour and Skillinvites qualified and eligible applicants for the position of Youth Employment Specialist under the Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project (UPSNJP) financed by the World Bank.

Youth Employment Specialist for the following city

City

Required No.

Procurement Reference Number

Debre Brehan

1

ET-AMHARA UDIB-561136-CS-INDV

 

The Consulting Service (The Services) include the Youth Employment Specialist will lead, coordinate, and provide technical expertise for all youth-focused activities at the city level.

Duties and responsibilities:

A. Planning and Strategy

  • Develop a city-level annual work plan and budget for youth employment activities.
  • Identify and map potential host employers (private companies, NGOs, and public institutions) for the Apprenticeship Program.
  • Design outreach strategies to recruit eligible vulnerable youth according to project guidelines.

B. Implementation of the Apprenticeship Program

  • Facilitate the matching process between youth interests/skills and employer needs.
  • Draft and manage Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) between the project, host employers, and apprentices.
  • Organize and deliver pre-apprenticeship orientation and soft skills training (e.g., work ethics, communication, Life skill).
  • Ensure the timely payment of stipends or subsidies to participants.

C. Stakeholder Engagement

  • Establish and maintain a City Youth Employment Taskforce or Committee.
  • Liaise with Vocational Training Centers (TVETs) to align training with market demand.
  • Advocate for the permanent hiring of apprentices by host employers upon program completion.

D. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL)

  • Conduct regular site visits to monitor the quality of mentorship and safety at host workplaces.
  • Maintain an accurate database of all program participants and their employment status.
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual progress reports highlighting achievements, challenges, and lessons learned.

The duration of assignment will be for one-year contract, with a possibility of extension upon satisfactory performance of the consultant.

 Required Competencies

The Youth Employment Specialistshould have the following required experience and qualification to properly carryout the assignment:

  • Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Management, Sociology, Development Studies, Business administration, Public administration, Business management, or a related field.
  • Experience: * Minimum of 5 or 3 years of professional experience in youth development, employment services, or labor market programs.
    • Proven experience in managing apprenticeship or internship schemes.
    • Familiarity with the urban poverty context and social protection programs (experience with World Bank-funded projects is a plus).
  • Skills: * Strong networking and negotiation skills with private sector actors.
    • Excellent report writing and data management capabilities.
    • Fluency in the local language and the official working language.

 

The Bureau now invites eligible individual consultants/Specialists to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Academic Qualification and Experience as youth employment specialist,
  • Technical Expertise: Proven track record in designing and managing Apprenticeship Programs or large-scale internship schemes,
  • Stakeholder Engagement: Demonstrated ability to negotiate with private sector employers and coordinate with government offices,
  • Reporting & MIS: Experience in data collection, using MIS tools for project tracking, and high-quality technical report writingand
  • Relevant training:Life skill, Job searching,digital skill, Peer meeting facilitation, Training of trainers  and Entrepreneurship.

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III paragraph 3.16 and 3.17 of The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Procurement In Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (recent Edition) (“Procurement Regulation”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance to Section VII para 7.34 to 7.39 of The World Bank Procurement Regulation based on qualification and relevant experience of the applicants to the assignment.

data.notice_text:
NATIONAL INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AUTHORITY – UGANDA (NITA-U)

 

 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET)

PROJECT ID: P171305

LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/26-27/00027

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The consultant will have the overall responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capability and experience is:

 

The shortlisting criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are:

  1. A minimum of eight (8) years of core business experience in ICT digital skills training, capacity building and skills development consultancy.
  2. Demonstrated successful completion of at least five (5) assignments in atleast two or more assignments involving: digital-skills training, digital literacy upskilling, ICT competency development, education technology, or large-scale capacity-building programmes within the past seven (7) years.  Evidence should indicate the client, scope, duration, and status/completion of each assignment.
  3. Presence of appropriate skills among staff in the areas of; Coordinator/team leader, Trainer-of-trainers, digital skills trainers, Curriculum development specialist, assessment and certification specialist, cybersecurity/digital safety specialist, gender and disability inclusion officer, research/data science officer, and monitoring and evaluation. Please do not submit CVs or biodata of individual experts at this stage.

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16, of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025 (Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non- Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications.

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations “Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025”.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours at the address below 08:00 to 17:00 hours from Monday to Friday at the address given below.

Expressions of Interest (One original plus two copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) on or before Wednesday, 18th November, 2026 at 11:00am.

The packages must be clearly marked: “Expression of Interest for Consultancy Services for the Implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP).”

 

Address for submission

National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U)

Palm Courts, Plot 7A Rotary Avenue, 1st Floor

Kampala, Uganda

Email: jacqueline.musimenta@nita.go.ug

 

Any form of canvassing or lobbying for the tender shall lead to automatic disqualification

 

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR

SOLICITUD DE EXPRESIÓN DE INTERÉS

CONTRATACIÓN DE CONSULTOR INDIVIDUAL

 

NOMBRE DE LA CONSULTORÍA: ESPECIALISTA EN GESTIÓN FINANCIERA

UNIDAD DE PRESTACIÓN DE LOS SERVICIOS: UNIDAD TÉCNICA AEROPORTUARIA (UTA) — MOPSV

REFERENCIA STEP: BO-UTA-580787-CS-IND

 

 

El Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial (BM) para cubrir el costo de la Preparación de proyectos (P516619) en relación con el Programa para el Fortalecimiento de la Sostenibilidad Institucional y Financiera del Sector Transporte, a través de la Carta Acuerdo de Cooperación Técnica No Reembolsable Grant No. TF D1775, y tiene la intención de aplicar parte de los fondos a la contratación de servicios de consultoría.

 

El Ministerio de Obras Públicas, Servicios y Vivienda (MOPSV), a través de la Unidad Técnica Aeroportuaria (UTA), invita a consultores elegibles a indicar su interés en proporcionar los Servicios. Los Consultores interesados deben proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para prestar los Servicios.

 

Los Términos de Referencia y los Documentos de Selección para la presentación de postulaciones podrán ser recabados en la página web del SICOES https://www.sicoes.gob.bo/portal/index.php o solicitarse a la siguiente dirección vía correo electrónico: contrataciones.uta@oopp.gob.bo, o en las oficinas de la Unidad Técnica Aeroportuaria del MOPSV, en la dirección indicada al final de este anuncio, a partir del día 11 de noviembre de 2026.

 

Los consultores serán seleccionados mediante el método de Selección Abierta y Competitiva de Consultores Individuales descrito en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión (Séptima Edición, septiembre de 2025). Se llama la atención de los Consultores interesados sobre la Sección III, Regulaciones de Adquisiciones, contempladas en los Párrafos 3.13, 3.15, 3.16, 3.17, 3.20 y 3.21, que establece la política del Banco Mundial sobre "Conflicto de Interés" y "Elegibilidad" para Servicios de Consultoría.

Invitation for Expression of Interest

 

Consulting Services- Firms Selection

 

Geotechnical Studies for a Wind Farm in Botswana

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Geotechnical Studies for a Wind Farm Site

Reference: EOI/MME-PEDU/002/26-27

 

  1. BACKGROUND

 

Botswana plans to harness its renewable energy (RE) resources and accelerate renewable energy development through the implementation of the Integrated Resource Plan (IRP). The Government of Botswana is currently developing renewable energy projects at several pre-selected sites. The Project and Energy Development Unit (PEDU) under the Ministry of Minerals and Energy (the Client) is responsible for the development of these projects. A feasibility consultant has identified a proposed site for a wind farm based on a multi-criteria assessment considering preliminary wind resource data, transmission infrastructure, land use and ownership, and preliminary environmental and social considerations.

 

The geotechnical studies will support the development of a proposed 100 MW wind farm located north of Letlhakane, Botswana. The final coordinates and boundaries of the area to be investigated will be confirmed by the Client prior to commencement of the assignment.

 

  1. SCOPE OF WORK

 

The Client is seeking a qualified and experienced consulting firm to undertake geotechnical investigations to support the pre-development of the proposed 100 MW wind farm.

 

The assignment will include preliminary site-wide geotechnical investigations and, subsequently, location-specific investigations based on the preliminary wind farm layout.

 

The detailed scope, investigation areas, technical requirements and deliverables will be set out in the Terms of Reference provided at the next stage of the selection process.

 

  1. QUALIFICATIONS

 

PEDU invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core Business: Minimum of ten (10) years of experience undertaking geotechnical investigations and related studies.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Digital West Bank & Gaza Project (P174355)

Grant number: (TF0B5236)

Assignment Title: Capacity Building for TRA

Reference No.: GZ-MTIT-548204-CS-CQS

 

The Palestinian Liberation Organization has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) for USD 20 million for the benefit of the Palestinian Authority (PA) to finance the Digital West Bank & Gaza Project (the Project). The Project will seek to produce concrete and tangible results for the Palestinians by enhancing access to high-speed broadband services and increasing access to selected e-services for citizens and businesses. The Project will focus on key points to unleash digital transformation in the Palestinian territories, addressing some of the bilateral challenges that prevent digital transformation from achieving its full potential. It will strengthen the Palestinian territories' digital resilience and the PA's ability to respond to shocks such as COVID-19.

The Project is implemented and overseen by the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MTDE), formerly the Ministry of Telecom and Information Technology (MTIT), to support digital transformation and resilience in the West Bank and Gaza.

The project has the following four components:

  1. Enabling legal and regulatory environment for Digital Economy, mainly institutional development including the development of section Palestinian Telecommunications Regulatory Authority and Trust Service Supervisory Body; legal and regulatory framework; a Quality-of-Service platform; and capacity building.

  2. Implementing Digital Infrastructure Solutions for Emergency Response, Recovery and Resilience which includes the development of an emergency response center.

  3. Fostering User Centered E-Service Delivery, which includes the establishment of a whole government digital transformation strategy, data infrastructure, support for a digital public platform and prioritization, simplification and digitization of services, the launch of e-services, and implementation of an e-Government Procurement (e-GP) System; and

  4. Project Management, which will support the establishment of a Project management unit in MTDE.

     

The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) was established as an independent regulatory body under Decree-Law No. (37) of 2021 Concerning Telecommunications and Information Technology. Its mandate includes overseeing and developing the Palestinian telecommunications market and implementing policies designed by MTDE. The Project supports the establishment and operationalization of TRA, including capacity building to strengthen its effectiveness, credibility and independence.

 

MTDE seeks a qualified consulting or specialized training firm to design and deliver a targeted capacity-building program for TRA staff. The program will strengthen core regulatory skills, institutional processes and evidence-based decision-making, drawing on ITU guidance, ITU Global Symposium for Regulators best practices, and regional and international regulatory experience.

 

The assignment covers the following five training topics, with course content and modalities as detailed in the TOR:

  1. Telecom Licensing, Regulatory Compliance and Enforcement (15 trainees): licensing procedures and conditions; compliance monitoring; risk-based inspections; evidence and case management; proportionate enforcement, sanctions and due process. Expert-led applied workshop with practical exercises.

  2. Telecom Market Analysis and Competition Regulation (7 trainees): market definition and analysis; significant market power; competition remedies; infrastructure sharing, network access and interconnection; and regulatory case studies. Blended training with practical market analysis exercises.

  3. Regulation and Measurement of Telecommunications Quality of Service (QoS) and Quality of Experience (QoE) (7 trainees): regulatory frameworks and standards; network performance indicators; drive testing; measurement, monitoring, data analysis and reporting; and compliance assessment. Specialized training with remote follow-up sessions.

  4. Protection of Telecommunications Consumers and Users' Rights (5 trainees): consumer protection frameworks; provider obligations; complaints and dispute resolution; contracts, pricing and billing transparency; investigations, remedies and consumer protection indicators. Practical workshops.

  5. National Emergency Telecommunications Planning and Telecom Sector Resilience (15 trainees): emergency governance; critical infrastructure risks; business continuity and disaster recovery; incident coordination and reporting; priority communications and service restoration; supply-chain resilience; and tabletop emergency and cyber scenarios. Multi-stakeholder workshop with practical scenarios.

 

Assignment deliverables include training delivery; printed/electronic training materials for each trainee, PMU and TRA; course completion certificates for successful participants; and an evaluation report for each course summarizing outcomes and comparing pre- and post-training test results. Detailed training plans and course outlines will be requested at the subsequent proposal stage and are not required with the expression of interest.

 

Training shall be conducted physically at MTDE labs or the firm's labs, with the course-specific follow-up modalities indicated in the TOR. Arabic is preferred but is not mandatory. Where relevant, professional certification examinations, vouchers, registration and related services may be proposed as optional components with a separate itemized financial offer; TRA may procure all, some or none of these components.

 

Download Full Tor from Here: TRA-Capacity Building ToR.pdf

 

The Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MTDE) now invites eligible consulting firms and specialized training centers ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience.

 

The shortlisting criteria are the firm's core business and years in business, relevant experience, and technical and managerial capability, demonstrated through the following:

  • Specialization in telecommunications regulatory training and capacity building, with demonstrated expertise relevant to the five training topics specified in the TOR.

  • A successful record of similar telecommunications/ICT regulatory training assignments, including completion of at least two training programs on similar topics within the last three (3) years.

  • Experience providing training to telecom/ICT regulatory authorities, ministries or comparable public-sector institutions, preferably in the MENA region.

  • Technical and managerial capacity to organize and deliver the program, and a clear understanding of the assignment and approach to its execution.

     

Expressions of interest should include a firm profile; details of relevant completed assignments, including dates, clients, scope and supporting evidence; and a initial list of proposed trainers and Key Experts, indicating their intended training topics or roles. Trainers and Key Experts will not be evaluated or assigned scores at this stage. No training plan or course outline is required at the expression-of-interest stage.

 

Interested firms must also answer the following questions in their expressions of interest:

  1. What training delivery modality does the firm offer for this assignment: face-to-face, online, or blended? Please specify the proposed modality for each training topic.

  2. Is the firm a local or international company? Please state its country of registration and whether it has a local presence in Palestine.

  3. In which language(s) can the firm deliver the training: Arabic, English, or both? Please specify the available language(s) for each training topic.

     

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant's Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours: Sunday – Thursday (09:00 AM – 01:00 PM) (Local Time GMT +2)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Kyrgyz Republic

Project: Kyrgyz Renewable Energy Development Project (KRED)

Assignment Title: Environmental Specialist (Individual Consultant)

Package #KG/KRED/CS/2026/IC-03

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

The Ministry of Energy of the Kyrgyz Republic, under the World Bank-financed Kyrgyz Renewable Energy Development Project (KRED), invites qualified individual consultants to express their interest in providing consulting services for environmental monitoring and supervision during the rehabilitation of the Bystrovskaya Small Hydropower Plant (SHPP) and the construction of the 110 kV "Nizhniy Tar – Kara-Kuldzha" overhead transmission line.

Minimum Qualification Requirements

Interested individual consultants should demonstrate that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the assignment, including:

  1. Education: A university degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management, Natural Resource Management, or a related field.

  2. Professional Experience: At least five (5) years of professional experience in environmental assessments and/or environmental supervision of infrastructure projects, including monitoring the implementation of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs). Experience in hydropower, energy sector projects, and linear infrastructure (overhead transmission lines and electricity networks) will be an advantage.

  3. International Environmental Standards: Knowledge of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), Environmental and Social Standards (ESS), and/or environmental requirements of other International Financial Institutions (IFIs). Practical experience in environmental supervision of projects financed by the World Bank or other IFIs will be an advantage.

  4. National Legislation: Knowledge of environmental legislation of the Kyrgyz Republic, national environmental assessment and review procedures, and requirements related to protection zones and land acquisition for linear infrastructure projects.

  5. Training and Coordination: Experience in developing and delivering training activities and coordinating with contractors and regulatory authorities will be an advantage.

  6. Language Skills: Fluency in Russian is mandatory. Knowledge of English will be an advantage, while knowledge of Kyrgyz is desirable.

  7. Computer Skills: Proficiency in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Experience with Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and mapping tools (QGIS, Google Earth, etc.) for spatial data analysis, protection zones, and 110 kV transmission line routing will be an advantage.

  8. Fieldwork Availability: Willingness to work predominantly in field conditions (up to 70% of working time), including regular site visits to both Project locations in Kemin, Chuy Region, and Kara-Kuldzha District, Osh Region, as well as extended field missions.

Terms of Reference

The detailed scope of consulting services, responsibilities, qualification requirements, and conditions of the assignment are provided in the Terms of Reference (ToR), available in English and Russian.

Interested consultants are encouraged to review the Terms of Reference before submitting their expressions of interest.

Submission of Expressions of Interest

Qualified individual consultants are invited to submit their Expressions of Interest demonstrating their relevant qualifications and professional experience in accordance with the Terms of Reference.

Expressions of Interest must be submitted in English, electronically, to the following email address:

Email: kred.pmo@gmail.com

Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 16:00 (Bishkek local time, GMT+6).

data.notice_text:
Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)

Country: IGAD Secretariat
Name of project:   Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa        
Project No.:     P178566
Grant No.:       IDA-E0820

Assignment Title: Study to Develop Cross-Border Digital Soil for a Pilot Area in the IGAD Region, Including Digital Soil Property Maps, and Uncertainty Layers 

Reference/Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567697-CS-CQS

1.    The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
2.    The consulting services (“the Services”) includes i) The review of cross border areas in the IGAD region that have existing or planned IGAD Ground Water Information System (GWIS) in place, and identify the most suitable pilot area based on agreed technical, institutional and data-availability criteria. ii) To conduct soil field sampling, laboratory analysis, and quality controlled data compilation one cross border pilot area with a Ground Water Information System in place. iii)To generate updated, harmonized and decision-ready digital soil maps for the selected cross-border pilot area, including key soil properties, soil constraints, land-suitability information and uncertainty estimates. iv)To compile and harmonise existing soil, water, land-use, climate, terrain and remote-sensing datasets relevant to the selected pilot area and ensure compatibility with IGAD’s GeoNode repository, dashboards, DACAS and related decision-support tools. v)To develop a scalable workflow, data standard and implementation approach that can later be extended to other IGAD cross-border clusters. The assignment is expected to take 175 Calendar Days from the date of contract commencement. 
3.    The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://igad.int/consultancies  or can be obtained at the address given below.

4.    The The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  The shortlisting criteria:

i)    The firm should have at least 10 years of experience in conducting soil mapping (soil field sampling, laboratory analysis, and quality controlled data compliation; and generation of harmonised and decision-ready digital soil maps and other tasks in line with the objectives of the assignment)
ii)    Satisfactory completion of three similar assignments in the past 10 years 
iii)    Availability of the below key experts with the required profiles as detailed in the Terms of Reference
 (i) Team Leader: Overall lead of the assignment,(ii) Soil Scientist: Conducts soil characterization, fertility assessment, and land capability evaluation, (iii) Digital Soil Mapping Specialist: Develops digital soil maps using spatial modeling, machine learning, and geostatistics, (iv) GIS and Remote Sensing Specialist: Processes satellite imagery, spatial data, and develops geospatial products, (vi) Agronomist/Crop Production Specialist: Interprets soil information into crop-specific management recommendations. At the proposal stage, the consulting firm must provide a staffing plan with names, roles, and CVs for the core project team as part of the proposal.
5.    The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and revised Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.    Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7.    A Consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant`s Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

8.    Further information can be obtained at the address below during the following office hours 0900 and 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours East African Time (EAT) and public holidays.

Expression of interest shall be sent by e-mail to the address below by 18/11/2026 at 1700hours EAT. to:  procurement@igad.int  with copy to hassan.salah@igad.int  and quote the Assignment title and Contract No (Study to Develop Cross-Border Digital Soil for a Pilot Area in the IGAD Region, Including Digital Soil Property Maps, and Uncertainty Layers, Reference/Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567697-CS-CQS) in the subject row.

The Government of Fiji, through the Ministry of Finance, Strategic Planning, National Development and Statistics, has received financing from the World Bank for the Fiji Tourism Development Program in Vanua Levu or “Na Vualiku” and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will support the Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation (MTCA) in strengthening tourism sector disaster risk management, emergency preparedness, response and recovery, with particular focus on the Northern Division (Vanua Levu and Taveuni).

The assignment will include: (i) assessment of the operational readiness of the Fiji Tourism Risk Management Framework and preparation of an implementation roadmap and supplementary protocols where required; (ii) assessment and strengthening of tourism crisis communications, including training and multi-agency simulation exercises; (iii) identification, assessment and prioritisation of tourism emergency preparedness and response investments in the Northern Division, including concept notes for at least ten prioritised investments; (iv) design and delivery of emergency preparedness and response training for tourism operators, communities, government agencies and emergency responders; and (v) preparation of procurement-ready packages for up to four selected priority investments, including the required environmental and social assessments and instruments, as applicable.

The Services are expected to commence in April 2027 and be implemented over a 12-month period.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Consultancy Firm Services for the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for A Proposed Sanitary Landfill/ Integrated Solid Waste Management Facility on Union Island.

Reference No: SVGUBEC-C-QCBS-10

Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SVG Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC) project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Government of SVG (GoSVG) has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Tourism, Civil Aviation, and Sustainable Development (MoTCASD) responsible for implementing the UBEC project national-level activities and coordinating with relevant ministries.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the preparation of an ESIA package for the proposed landfill / integrated solid waste management intervention. The assignment shall focus on environmental and social due diligence, risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, mitigation planning, and preparation of disclosure-ready instruments. The consulting firm shall use available project information supplied by the Client and shall not be required to prepare a separate technical or economic study. The assignment is expected to take eighteen (18) to twenty (20) weeks from contract commencement, with an expected start in March 2027.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://procurement.gov.vc/eprocure/index.php/current-bids

The MoTCASD now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core business and years in business: the firm shall have at least ten (10) years of experience in environmental and social impact assessment or environmental consulting services.
  2. Relevant experience: the firm shall have completed at least three (3) ESIA/ESMP assignments in the last ten (10) years for sanitary landfills, solid waste management facilities or comparable infrastructure, of which at least one (1) was financed by the World Bank or another multilateral development bank and prepared under the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework or equivalent standards. Experience in Small Island Developing States, the Caribbean, or coastal and disaster-prone settings will be an advantage.
  3. Technical and managerial capability: general organization of the firm; number of permanent professional staff in the relevant disciplines (environmental and social assessment, solid waste, biodiversity, hydrogeology, occupational and community health and safety, and GIS); and demonstrated capacity to carry out inclusive stakeholder consultation and to prepare disclosure-ready documents meeting multilateral development bank requirements.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Expressions of interest should include: (a) a company profile, including year of establishment and core business; (b) a list of similar assignments completed in the last ten (10) years, showing for each the client, location, value, dates, source of financing and the firm’s role; (c) the number and disciplines of permanent professional staff; and (d) for associations, the form of association (joint venture or sub-consultancy) and the role of each member. Expressions of interest should not exceed twenty (20) pages, excluding company registration documents.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI) 

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES) 

 

Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) 

Digital RMI Project 

P171517 

 

Assignment Title:  

Reference No.: MH-DIDA-576425-CS-INDV Digital Unit: Government Technical Support Specialist/s 

(Majuro based position) 

 

The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (the Government) is undertaking a major investment program supported by the World Bank under the Digital RMI Project (Project).  The development objective includes establishing the critical foundations for digital government services and the digital economy. 

 

To support the development of digital government services and a digital economy the Government, with World Bank funding support, has established a Digital Unit reporting into the Office of the Chief Secretary.  

The Project is under implementation and closes in August 2028. The Digital Unit is based in Majuro and currently comprises two Technical Support Specialists, with the Director position under open competitive recruitment. Work currently underway includes the migration of government users to Microsoft 365, an Azure landing zone, consolidation of government onto the rmi.gov.mh domain, a new government web portal, electronic signature and workflow tooling, and the first e-Services and Digital ID releases. 

 

The Director of the Digital Unit is now seeking to recruit a third technical support specialist staff member who will help progress the Digital Unit work program and support the rollout of the Microsoft platform, and applications as approved in the RMI Future State Roadmap Report.  The role involves working closely with relevant Ministry(s) to provide technical support for the implementation of and migration to the Microsoft platform and associated applications. 

 

 A description of the Digital Unit’s functions is set out in the position description in terms of reference, and a copy of the Future State Roadmap Report can be provided on request. 

 

The role is based in Majuro.  This is a full-time position and is for a contracted period from 1 January 2027 to 31 August 2028 (with the possibility of an extension), with a 3-month probationary period.  It is expected that the role will commence on or about 1 January 2027.  The remuneration will reflect the fact that this is a contracted role and not a permanent public sector role. 

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be supplied on request to the Project Officer galbert.robert@rmi.gov.mh.

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include : prepare bankable, climate-resilient, technically sound, environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, and implementation-ready feasibility studies, environmental and social safeguard instruments, detailed engineering designs, cost estimates, and procurement documents for rural water supply and sanitation systems.

The Services comprise: surveys, feasibility studies, assessments, engineering designs, environmental and social safeguard instruments, cost estimates, procurement documents, implementation planning, and capacity-building activities necessary to deliver technically sound, economically viable, environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, climate-resilient, and implementation-ready rural water supply and sanitation systems in the targeted woredas (teru, dubti, afdera, argoba, hadeleela, semurobi) woredas  of afar region.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

(a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business  is in the provision of professional consultancy services related to water supply and sanitation infrastructure development, including planning, feasibility studies, hydrogeological investigations, environmental and social impact assessments, detailed engineering design, preparation of technical specifications, cost estimates, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), and procurement documents. Experience in rural and multi-village water supply systems, climate-resilient infrastructure.

  1. The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini (GoKE) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the International Development Agency (IDA) and grant funding from the Global Public Good (GPG) Facility, which are all under the World Bank. The received financing is for the purposes of implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project (P508960) (the Project), with the involvement of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Energy, as set out in the Loan Agreement, Financing Agreement, Grant Agreement and Project Agreements.

 

  1. The EEC now invites Expressions of Interest (EOI) from interested and eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to provide consulting services for the Review of the 2034 Short-Term Generation Expansion Plan.

 

  1. The Consultant shall undertake, but not necessarily be limited to the following tasks:

 

      1. Review and update the Short-Term Generation Expansion plan -2034
      2. Assessment of baseload options
      3. Assessment of network hosting capacity
      4. Desktop study on potential export market for power generated in Eswatini
      5. Recommendation of a Least Cost Generation Expansion Plan

 

 

  1. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform all the services. The following documents shall also be submitted along with the EOI applications by all the consulting firms including each member of JV firms:
      • Copies of certificates of incorporation/registration of the consulting firms
      • Valid Tax Registration and Clearence Certificates
      • Annual financial records of the firm for the last 5 years
      • Corporate profile of the firm with quality assurance plan, e.g. ISO 9001, information on organizational strength (Organization structure, number of permanent professional staffs and their expertise, qualifications and number of total staff), evidence of availability of licensed power system analysis software, including but not limited to: PSS®E, DIgSILENT Power Factory, ETAP, PSCAD or equivalent software required for execution of the assignment.

 

  1. The qualifications and shortlisting criteria are:
  • At least ten (10) years’ experience in energy-sector planning, power-system studies, electricity-generation planning, energy economics or related advisory services.
  • At least two (2) relevant assignments in electricity-demand forecasting, least-cost generation expansion planning, energy modelling, power-system or grid-integration studies, generation-technology assessment, energy economics
  • Demonstrated experience of at least two (2) relevant assignment in electricity-generation planning.
  • Proven experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in generation expansion planning in Africa.
  • Proven Experience with utility transmission networks.
  1. The purpose of this REOI is to establish a shortlist of not more than eight (8) Prequalified Respondents for the subsequent Request for Proposal and to invite technical and financial proposals from these Respondents. All responses shall be assessed for completeness. The following shall be assessed on a Yes/No basis to determine a PASS or FAIL result; ten (10) years’ experience in energy-sector planning, power-system studies, electricity-generation planning, energy economics or related advisory services; two (2) relevant assignments in electricity-demand forecasting, least-cost generation expansion planning, energy modelling, power-system or grid-integration studies, generation-technology assessment, energy economics; demonstrated experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in electricity-generation planning in Africa.

 

Respondents who have attained a PASS result shall be shortlisted and ranked based on the following weighted aspect:

  • General corporate experience; [15]
  • Specific experience in generation expansion planning and integration studies; [35]
  • Power system planning studies experience; [15]
  • Generation technology assessment and deployment experience; [15]

  1. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

Senior Consultant for VROMI Support to Repair EDMP Procured Equipment

The Emergency Debris Management Project

Assignment Title: Senior Consultant for VROMI Support to Repair EDMP Procured Equipment

Credit/Loan no.: TF-B9747

Reference no.: SX-NRPB-574596-CS-INDV

The Government of Sint Maarten has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Emergency Debris Management Project (EDMP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The objective of the assignment is to engage a Senior Consultant to coordinate, manage and finalize the repair of heavy equipment procured under the Emergency Debris Management Project (EDMP), restoring operational capacity for the solid waste management division of the Ministry of Public Housing, Spatial Planning, Environment and Infrastructure (VROMI). The Consultant will review technical repair scopes, validate supplier quotations, track warranties, review invoices, coordinate shipments and confirm acceptance testing.

  • The assignment will also strengthen VROMI’s capacity for sustainable maintenance and asset management through practical procedures, preventive maintenance schedules, an Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Plan, operational protocols and staff capacity building.
  • The Consultant will deliver the following:
  • Inception report and work plan, including an equipment assessment, prioritized repair coordination plan and stakeholder communication strategy.
  • Coordination of equipment repairs, including an equipment inventory, review of maintenance records and supplier assessments, repair and shipment tracking, warranty monitoring, invoicing, handover and acceptance testing, with quarterly progress reporting.
  • A comprehensive asset management program, including a review of existing procedures and technical capacity, prioritized recommendations, a preventive maintenance schedule and budget linked to the financial framework, an O&M Plan, operational protocols, standard operating procedures and a staff training session.
  • Final equipment repair coordination and asset management report, including financial reconciliation, final recommendations and a handover note for VROMI.
  • Final assignment report covering achievements, lessons learned, challenges and recommendations.

 

The assignment is expected to last six months, including approximately 60 cumulative days in Sint Maarten through periodic missions, with remaining activities performed remotely. Indicative milestones are Week 1 for inception, quarterly progress reports, Week 20 for the final equipment repair coordination and asset management report, and Week 22 for the final assignment report. · Experience preparing O&M manuals, standard operating procedures and maintenance documentation

· Demonstrated experience coordinating multiple actors.

· National experience working with the Government and/or its agencies.

· Demonstrated experience independently conducting activities in a broad context and implementing capacity-building initiatives.

Other skills:

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

IDA CREDIT NO.: IDA-76370

 

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE PREPARATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT (ESIA) AND RESETTLEMENT ACTION PLAN (RAP) FOR RABBAH IRRIGATION SCHEME, MOKWA LGA, NIGER STATE

REFERENCE NO: NG-NIGER STATE SPIN-580030-CS-CQS

PUBLICATION DATE: Friday 6th November, 2026

The Niger State Government, through the Federal Republic of Nigeria, has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for payment of the Consultancy Services for the Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for Rabbah Irrigation Scheme, Niger State.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include conducting an ESIA and preparing a RAP for the rehabilitation of the Rabbah Irrigation Scheme, a 1,830 ha net irrigable area (1,960 ha gross command area) on the River Niger in Rabba community, Mokwa Local Government Area. The rehabilitation works include an 11.4 km protective dyke, a new river intake, delivery sump and rising main, rehabilitation of the main, secondary and tertiary canals with their drainage and hydraulic structures, 55.8 km of access and service roads, a 1,308 kWp solar photovoltaic pumping system and a Water User Association office and shed. The Services include the preparation of the Scoping, Draft and Final ESIA and RAP Reports, including the Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), a Critical Habitat Assessment and Biodiversity Management Plan, a Climate Change Risk Assessment, a Pest Management Plan and Integrated Vector Management Plan, labour influx, SEA/SH and occupational health and safety plans, a grievance redress mechanism, a 100% census and asset inventory of Project Affected Persons, stakeholder consultations, time-based technical support for RAP implementation, and all other deliverables specified in the Terms of Reference (ToRs), in accordance with applicable national regulations and the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToRs) for the assignment is available upon request via: nigerspinprocurement@gmail.com

The Niger State Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

1.      Proven experience as an Environmental and Social Management consulting firm in the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) and Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) for irrigation, water resources, dam rehabilitation, agricultural or similar infrastructure projects.

2.      Demonstrated working knowledge of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), particularly ESS1, ESS5, ESS6 and ESS10, gained through hands-on experience in preparing and implementing environmental and social instruments for World Bank-financed or equivalent donor-funded projects.

3.      A minimum of eight (8) years’ relevant experience in environmental and social assessment and resettlement planning for irrigation, water resources, dam rehabilitation or similar infrastructure projects, including a minimum of five (5) years’ experience in civil works contracts requiring environmental management procedures and mitigation measures.

4.      Successful completion of at least three (3) similar ESIA and RAP assignments for World Bank-financed or equivalent donor-funded projects.

5.      Demonstrated experience in:

  • environmental and social baseline studies, impact assessment and stakeholder engagement, including engagement with farmers, herders and water users;
  • socio-economic surveys, census, asset inventory and valuation, and livelihood restoration planning;
  • Critical Habitat Assessment and biodiversity management under ESS6, climate change risk assessment and hydrological modelling for riverine irrigation systems;
  • occupational health and safety, gender and GBV/SEA/SH risk assessment, and preparation of ESMPs; and
  • work in Nigeria or in a developing country under similar conditions, preferably in savanna agro-ecological zones similar to Mokwa LGA.

 

6.      Availability of adequate organizational and technical capacity, including access to a multidisciplinary team capable of undertaking assignments of similar scope and complexity, and field personnel fluent in Nupe, Hausa or Fulfulde.

7.      Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement and report-writing skills.

Please note: The Qualifications and Experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, Paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Seventh Edition, September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

The consultancy services are expected to be completed within sixteen (16) weeks from the commencement date, during which the Consultant shall undertake the ESIA and RAP assignments concurrently in accordance with the Terms of Reference (ToRs). The Scoping Reports are due four (4) weeks, and the Draft Reports twelve (12) weeks, after contract signing.

The Federal Ministry of Energy, Mining and Industry (FMERI) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Just Transition in Select Coal Regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing daily operational support to the Workforce Transition Unit (LTU) within the Human Resources Department of the Zenica Coal Mine (RMU Zenica). The assignment expects continuous physical presence at the HR Department of RMU Zenica. The initial contract period is twelve (12) months, with the possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance and project implementation schedules.
