AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

RECRUTEMENT D’UNE STRUCTURE D’APPUI A L’ECOSYSTEME(SAE) CHARGEE DE LA PRE-INCUBATION, DE L’INCUBATION ET DE L’ACCELERATION DES STARTUPS

                            Programme « Akili Digital » : Pilote Kinshasa

 

P180496

N° Avis : AMI n° ZR-UGP - PTN-558294-CS-CQS :

N° de l’Accord du financement Crédit IDA : 7602-ZR

N° de la Convention de Crédit AFD      : CCD119801 H

N° de référence du marché PPM : n° ZR-UGP - PTN-558294-CS-CQS :

 

Date : Le 06 novembre 2026

 

Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale d’un montant de 400 millions de dollars américains pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Transformation Numérique de la RDC(PTN) et cofinancé par l'Agence Française de Développement à la hauteur de 100 millions d’euros.

 

Dans le cadre de la Composante 3, et en particulier de la Sous-Composante 3.2, le PTN prévoit la mise en œuvre d’un mécanisme de soutien à l’innovation et à l’entrepreneuriat numérique à travers le programme Akili Digital. Ce programme vise à soutenir le développement du contenu local et à stimuler l’innovation numérique au moyen de concours de plans d’affaires compétitifs ouverts aux startups numériques et aux Structures d’Appui à l’Écosystème (SAE).

Akili Digital est la dénomination du programme. Le dispositif de concours de plans d’affaires constitue une modalité de sa mise en œuvre, appuyée par une plateforme numérique de gestion ; il ne désigne pas un programme distinct.

 

La mise en œuvre de ce mécanisme nécessite un dispositif professionnel d’accompagnement capable d’assurer la pré-incubation, l’incubation et l’accélération des startups lauréates. Pour la phase pilote à Lubumbashi, il est essentiel de s’appuyer sur une SAE expérimentée, capable de fournir un accompagnement technique de haute qualité, un mentorat, un accès à des infrastructures de prototypage, et de faciliter les liens avec le secteur privé.

Le présent recrutement porte ainsi sur une SAE, agissant en qualité de partenaire de pré-incubation, d’incubation et d’accélération pour les startups du programme Akili Digital à Kinshasa, dans le cadre d’un contrat avec l’UGPTN.

 

L’objectif principal de la mission est de fournir un accompagnement de haute qualité aux startups lauréates du programme Akili Digital à Kinshasa, à travers des programmes de pré-incubation (fenêtre A1), d’incubation (fenêtre A2) et d’accélération (fenêtre B1), afin de maximiser leur croissance, leur viabilité et leur impact sur l’écosystème numérique congolais. La SAE contribue ainsi à structurer un pipeline solide de startups, depuis l’idéation jusqu’à la maturité, en cohérence avec les objectifs du PTN.

 

La mission vise à atteindre les objectifs spécifiques suivants :

 

  • Pré-incuber les entrepreneurs en phase d’idéation (fenêtre A1) en les accompagnant dans la validation de leur concept, le développement de prototypes et la préparation de leur passage à l’incubation.
  • Incuber les startups disposant d’un prototype validé (fenêtre A2) en les aidant à développer leur produit, à tester leur modèle d’affaires et à préparer leur mise sur le marché.
  • Accélérer les startups disposant d’une traction initiale (fenêtre B1) en les soutenant dans leur expansion, leur montée en échelle et leur préparation à l’investissement.
  • Fournir un accompagnement technique et business structuré, incluant le mentorat, le coaching, la formation et l’accès à des infrastructures de prototypage.
  • Faciliter le développement de produits et la mise sur le marché des solutions des startups.
  • Renforcer les compétences entrepreneuriales des fondateurs et de leurs équipes.
  • Assurer la conformité des startups avec les exigences de co-financement (pour la fenêtre B1) et les sauvegardes environnementales et sociales (E&S).
  • Faciliter les liens avec le secteur privé en mobilisant des mentors, des partenaires commerciaux et des investisseurs potentiels.
  • Assurer un suivi rigoureux de la performance des startups et produire des rapports réguliers pour les UGP.
  • Promouvoir l’inclusion et veiller à ce qu’au moins 30 % des startups accompagnées soient dirigées ou co-fondées par des femmes.
  • Documenter les leçons apprises et les meilleures pratiques pour le passage à l’échelle du programme.

 

Le démarrage de la mission est prévu au mois de janvier 2027 pour une durée de vingt-quatre (24) mois.

Les termes de référence complets pour le poste ainsi que l’attestation d’intégrité de l’AFD sont disponibles sur le site de mediacongo.net : www.mediacongo.net, sous l’onglet « Offres d’emploi » et sur le site de l’UG PTN : www.ugptn.cd.

 

L’Unité de Gestion de Projet PTN invite dès à présent les firmes de consultants admissibles                    (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

 Les critères d’évaluation de manifestations d’intérêt pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

N°

Critère d'évaluation

Notes par critère

1

Avoir au moins cinq (5) ans d’expérience dans l’accompagnement de startups, la pré-incubation, l’incubation et/ou l’accélération, idéalement dans le secteur du numérique

30 points

2

Avoir accompagné au moins trois (3) cohortes de startups, avec des résultats documentés (levées de fonds, croissance du CA, création d’emplois).

35 points

C

Connaissance approfondie de l’écosystème numérique et entrepreneurial de Kinshasa

25 points

4

Stratégie d'inclusion et de participation féminine

10 points

 

Total

100 points

 

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à cette étape.

 

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, Septième Edition, Septembre 25 (Règlement de passation des marchés), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts. Le candidat devra compléter l’Attestation d’intégrité de l’AFD et la retourner dûment signée accompagnée de sa manifestation d’intérêts.

 

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

 

Un Consultant(firme) sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Basée sur la Qualification des Consultants (CQS) par mise en concurrence ouverte internationale telle que décrite dans le Règlement de passation des marchés susmentionné.

 

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse physique ci-dessous ou à l’adresse électronique recrutement@ugpatn.cd chaque jour ouvrable de 9 heures à 16 heures locales.

 

L’UG PTN se réserve le droit de vérifier l’authenticité des informations fournies par les candidats aux fins de la présente sélection. Les candidats ayant fourni des informations tronquées ne seront pas retenus pour la suite du processus de passation des marchés.

Les Manifestations d’Intérêt, écrites en langue française, doivent être déposées physiquement à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier accompagné d’une version électronique en format Word ou Pdf copiable sur une clé USB ou de préférence, envoyées par courrier électronique en format Pdf copiable à l’adresse mail : recrutement@ugpatn.cd au plus tard le 20 novembre 2026 à 14h00’ heures locales (TU+1) et porter clairement la mention :« AMI n° ZR-UGP - PTN-558294-CS-CQS :Recrutement d’une Structure d’Appui à l’Ecosystème(SAE) chargée  de la Pré-incubation, de l’incubation et de l’accélération des startups : Programme « Akili Digital » : Pilote Kinshasa».

 

 

 

Noel Jean David LITANGA SANGU PAMBA

 

 

                Coordonnateur

Dans le cadre de la Composante 3, et en particulier de la Sous-Composante 3.2, le PTN prévoit la mise en œuvre d’un mécanisme de soutien à l’innovation et à l’entrepreneuriat numérique à travers le programme Akili Digital. Ce programme vise à soutenir le développement du contenu local et à stimuler l’innovation numérique au moyen de concours de plans d’affaires compétitifs ouverts aux startups numériques et aux Structures d’Appui à l’Écosystème (SAE).

Akili Digital est la dénomination du programme. Le dispositif de concours de plans d’affaires constitue une modalité de sa mise en œuvre, appuyée par une plateforme numérique de gestion ; il ne désigne pas un programme distinct.

 

La mise en œuvre de ce mécanisme nécessite un dispositif professionnel d’accompagnement capable d’assurer la pré-incubation, l’incubation et l’accélération des startups lauréates. Pour la phase pilote à Lubumbashi, il est essentiel de s’appuyer sur une SAE expérimentée, capable de fournir un accompagnement technique de haute qualité, un mentorat, un accès à des infrastructures de prototypage, et de faciliter les liens avec le secteur privé.

 

Le présent recrutement porte ainsi sur une SAE, agissant en qualité de partenaire de pré-incubation, d’incubation et d’accélération pour les startups du programme Akili Digital à Lubumbashi, dans le cadre d’un contrat avec l’UGPTN.

L’objectif principal de la mission est de fournir un accompagnement de haute qualité aux startups lauréates du programme Akili Digital à Lubumbashi, à travers des programmes de pré-incubation (fenêtre A1), d’incubation (fenêtre A2) et d’accélération (fenêtre B1), afin de maximiser leur croissance, leur viabilité et leur impact sur l’écosystème numérique congolais. La SAE contribue ainsi à structurer un pipeline solide de startups, depuis l’idéation jusqu’à la maturité, en cohérence avec les objectifs du PTN.

 

La mission vise à atteindre les objectifs spécifiques suivants :

 

  • Pré-incuber les entrepreneurs en phase d’idéation (fenêtre A1) en les accompagnant dans la validation de leur concept, le développement de prototypes et la préparation de leur passage à l’incubation.
  • Incuber les startups disposant d’un prototype validé (fenêtre A2) en les aidant à développer leur produit, à tester leur modèle d’affaires et à préparer leur mise sur le marché.
  • Accélérer les startups disposant d’une traction initiale (fenêtre B1) en les soutenant dans leur expansion, leur montée en échelle et leur préparation à l’investissement.
  • Fournir un accompagnement technique et business structuré, incluant le mentorat, le coaching, la formation et l’accès à des infrastructures de prototypage.
  • Faciliter le développement de produits et la mise sur le marché des solutions des startups.
  • Renforcer les compétences entrepreneuriales des fondateurs et de leurs équipes.
  • Assurer la conformité des startups avec les exigences de co-financement (pour la fenêtre B1) et les sauvegardes environnementales et sociales (E&S).
  • Faciliter les liens avec le secteur privé en mobilisant des mentors, des partenaires commerciaux et des investisseurs potentiels.
  • Assurer un suivi rigoureux de la performance des startups et produire des rapports réguliers pour les UGP.
  • Promouvoir l’inclusion et veiller à ce qu’au moins 30 % des startups accompagnées soient dirigées ou co-fondées par des femmes.
  • Documenter les leçons apprises et les meilleures pratiques pour le passage à l’échelle du programme.

 

Le démarrage de la mission est prévu au mois de janvier 2027 pour une durée de vingt-quatre (24) mois.

Les termes de référence complets pour le poste ainsi que l’attestation d’intégrité de l’AFD sont disponibles sur le site de mediacongo.net : www.mediacongo.net, sous l’onglet « Offres d’emploi » et sur le site de l’UG PTN : www.ugptn.cd.

 

L’Unité de Gestion de Projet PTN invite dès à présent les firmes de consultants admissibles                    (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Multinational

Name of Project: Accelerating Access to Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in the Eastern and Southern Africa Region Project

Grant No.: P506439

Assignment Title: Procurement of consultancy services for Utility Diagnostics, Performance Improvement Action Plans (PIAPs), Digitalization Maturity Assessment and New IBNET Benchmarking under the AFE WASH MPA Regional Support Project

Reference No: 006/AUDA/DITIR/QCBS/2027

Method: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS)

 

  1. Introduction

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Procurement of consultancy services for Utility Diagnostics, Performance Improvement Action Plans (PIAPs), Digitalization Maturity Assessment and New IBNET Benchmarking under the AFE WASH MPA Regional Support Project”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Inception and Utility Prioritization: confirms full alignment of the baseline diagnostic methodology with the AFE WASH MPA PAD (P506439), Component 3 results framework, and World Bank ESF requirements, applies a Utility Prioritization Framework ranking utilities. The consultant will work with a maximum list of 06 proposed utilities by the MPA participating countries, and build a database using, key baseline data on utility characteristics, size and performance, but also considering the characteristics of the enabling environment including criteria related to accountability, transparency, government reform commitment, and climate vulnerability to produce the final utility list and country sequencing for Round 1 (Months 1 to 10) and Round 2 (Months 8 to 20) etc; Task 2: NewIBNET Benchmarking including Digital Maturity: conduct a data audit assessing completeness and reliability of existing performance data against NewIBNET KPI requirements (including but not limiting to - NRW rates, billing and collection efficiency, energy consumption per m³, staffing ratios, O&M and capital expenditure per connection), provide hands-on support for data collection, cleaning, formatting, and platform submission, confirm national adoption of the NewIBNET as a preferred/standradized tool for performance assessment, which will translate into successful enrolment within six months of contract effectiveness etc; Task 3: Utility Diagnostic Baseline Assessments: Operational: NRW loss component analysis separating real losses (leakage, overflows) from apparent losses (meter error, illegal connections, data errors); service continuity by zone; production capacity versus demand; O&M practices and maintenance management systems etc; Task 4:Costed Performance Improvement Action Plans (PIAPs): Costed priority interventions, sequenced in time, assessing impact and feasibility, linked explicitly to the diagnostic root causes they address, and organised by reform dimension, SMART targets for example: reduce NRW from the diagnosed rate to the realistic target / as per resources available to implement the PIAP, by Month X; achieve operational cost recovery of 100% by Month Y; reduce specific energy consumption to the benchmark value by Month Z. These targets should then be calibrated against NewIBNET regional benchmarks etc; Task 5: Capacity Building and Regional Training: Module 1: PIAP Implementation and Utility Turnaround: translating diagnostic findings into managed reform; performance contracting (include successful cases); and turnaround case studies from the AFE region, Module 2:  Leadership and Corporate Governance: board effectiveness; CEO accountability frameworks; performance-based management; customer service culture etc; Task 6:  Knowledge Management and Regional Learning: The Firm shall synthesise all assignment outputs into reusable regional knowledge products and facilitate cross-country learning: minimum five knowledge products in English, French, Portuguese (Regional Utility Performance Report; NewIBNET Participation Guide; PIAP Preparation Methodology Guide; PIAP modelling tool, Utility Digitalisation Primer; Rural Operator Professionalization Framework); at least two regional knowledge-sharing events; a Regional WASH Utility Performance Knowledge Repository compiling all diagnostic reports, PIAPs, RWSSPRs, and benchmarking datasets; and integration of all NewIBNET data and PIAP outputs into AUDA-NEPAD reporting to the World Bank, the Systems Change  Water Scorecard, and AMCOW WASSMO.

 

  1. Level of Effort for Key staff:

 

Key Expert

Indicative Person-Months per Lot

KE1 - Team Leader / Utility Performance Specialist

12-15

KE2 - Water Utility Financial Specialist

8-10

KE3 - Water Engineering & NRW Specialist

8-10

KE4 - Climate Resilience Specialist

4-6

KE5 - Rural Water & Capacity Building Specialist

6-9

Total

40-55

 

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 24 months from contract effectiveness

 

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the following website: https://www.nepad.org/corporate-procurement#tenders

 

  1. Shortlisting criteria:

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. Minimum 10 years providing WASH technical assistance in Sub-Saharan Africa, including utility diagnostic assessments and performance improvement planning.

 

  1. Proven track record preparing costed PIAPs for at least 5 water utilities in Sub-Saharan Africa with measurable operational or financial improvement outcomes.

 

  1. Demonstrated familiarity with NewIBNET or equivalent benchmarking platforms (IBNET, IWA Water Loss Performance Indicators), including hands-on experience facilitating utility enrolment.

 

  1. Experience integrating climate risk screening into utility diagnostics and PIAPs in developing country contexts.

 

  1. Experience developing rural water operator professionalization strategies or sustainable rural O&M models in Sub-Saharan Africa.

 

  1. Experience on World Bank-financed TA assignments, with familiarity with World Bank procurement regulations and ESF requirements.

 

  1. Ability to deploy bilingual (EN/FR) expert teams across multiple countries simultaneously in Eastern and/or Southern Africa.

 

  1. Evidence of at least 2 similar assignments completed in the last 10 years

 

 

  1. Conflict of interest

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025  (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

  1. A firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Goods, Works, or Non-consulting Services for a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that firm), shall be disqualified from providing Consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to, those Goods, Works, or Non-consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

 

  1. A firm that has been engaged by the Borrower to provide Consulting Services for the preparation or implementation of a project (or an affiliate that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Consulting firm), shall be disqualified from subsequently providing Goods, Works, or Non-consulting Services resulting from, or directly related to those Consulting Services. This provision does not apply to the various firms (Consultants, contractors, or suppliers), which together are performing the contractor’s obligations under a turnkey or design and build contract;

 

  1. Neither a Consultant (including personnel and sub-consultants), nor an affiliate (that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that Consultant), shall be hired for any assignment that, by its nature, creates a conflict of interest with another assignment of the Consultant;

 

  1. Consultants (including their experts and other personnel, and sub-consultants), that have a close business or family relationship with a professional staff of the Borrower, or of the project implementing agency, or of a recipient of a part of the Bank’s financing, or any other party representing or acting on behalf of the Borrower, that is directly or indirectly involved in any part of: (i) the preparation of the TOR for the assignment; (iii) the selection process for the contract; or iii. the supervision of the contract, may not be awarded a contract, unless the conflict stemming from this relationship has been resolved in a manner acceptable to the Bank throughout the selection process and the execution of the contract.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office.

The Government of Grenada (GOG) has secured funding through the World Bank (WB) to pursue the Caribbean Efficient and Green-Energy Buildings Project (CEGEB) Project. The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase the share of utility-scale renewable energy generation and private-sector participation in renewable energy development in Grenada.

 

This consultancy supports the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC) in reviewing GRENLEC's retail tariff proposal. While the independent preparation or updating of a Cost-of-Service (CoS) Study is excluded from this scope, the Consultant shall evaluate the proposal against the established CoS framework and supporting regulatory documentation provided by PURC. the Commission seeks to engage the services of a qualified consulting firm to provide independent technical and regulatory advisory support during the review of the utility’s retail tariff proposal, including assistance, where necessary, with stakeholder and public consultation processes undertaken in accordance with the Tariff-Setting Methodology Regulations, 2022.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained on the Government E-Procurement Portal https://in-tendhost.co.uk/gnd/aspx/Home

The Government of Grenada now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.   • Experience working in the Caribbean region or similar island states.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

To obtain the maximum degree of comparison among Expressions of Interests (EOIs) and facilitate the evaluation process, the EOI should be a MAXIMUM of Thirty (30) pages and be submitted in the template provided.

 

Expressions of interest must be submitted via the E-Procurement portal (https://in-tendhost.co.uk/gnd/aspx/Home.), on or before November 20th, 2026, 4pm.

 

Further information can be obtained from donica.modeste@procurement.gov.gd  during office hours 9:00 am to 3:00 pm.

PACIFIC STRENGTHENING CORRESPONDENT BANKING RELATIONSHIPS PROJECT

The CC’s services shall be subject to an annual performance evaluation based on performance indicators specified in the Terms of Reference below. Performance evaluation shall be the basis for the extension or termination of the services. The selected CC is expected to work in his/her home country

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges, and foster collaboration and cooperation in the pursuit of shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.  The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

Participating Countries

The Pacific Island Countries (PICs) participating in the regional project comprise Fiji, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu

Overall Project Objective

The Project development Objective is to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries

Project Length

August 2024 to September 30 2030

 

2. Project Background

The Pacific Island Forum Secretariat (PIFS) is expecting to receive financing from the World Bank (WB) Group’s International Development Association (IDA) for a proposed project to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in Pacific Island Countries (PICs).  The PICs covered by the proposed regional project (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) include diverse island economies facing similar correspondent banking relationship challenges.

PICs range in size and topography – from small island states such as Samoa, with two principal inhabited volcanic islands, to large archipelagos such as the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), with 29 atolls spread over 2 million km2 of ocean. Population sizes vary from 11,300 people in Tuvalu to 930,000 people in Fiji.

The economic landscape of PICs is equally diverse, marked by different growth drivers, poverty rates, and growth trajectories. The average GDP growth across PICs decelerated to 3.5 percent in 2023 after a historically high of 7.9 percent in 2022, in a rebound from the COVID-19 crisis. However, medium-term growth prospects have worsened, with output growth expected to be significantly below the pre-pandemic trend of 4.7 percent between 2014 & 2019. Given low growth and limited employment opportunities in the island economies, labor migration to neighboring countries and the resulting remittances are critical drivers of living standards.

The United States, New Zealand, and Australia account for 94 percent of the Pacific diaspora. Trade and tourism are vital for many PICs, providing revenue and employment opportunities. Remittances, equivalent to more than 40 percent of GDP in some PICs, are a buffer against income shocks and an important source of finance for essential household consumption and human capital investment.

Financial systems in PICs are characterized by low levels of financial access and an uneven development of national payment systems. Both domestically owned and multinational commercial banks dominate the financial sector in all PICs.  In several PICs, much of the population lacks access to basic transaction accounts, limiting households and businesses’ ability to send and receive payments, save, invest, and respond to climatic and economic shocks. The financial market infrastructure is underdeveloped, in part due to limited competition and the lack of economies of scale. The level of national payment system development is uneven across PICs, and regional efforts to improve the efficiency of cross-border payments are limited in scale and scope.

PICs are uniquely vulnerable to the withdrawal of the correspondent banking relationships (CBR) that underpin international trade, tourism, remittances, and humanitarian financial flows. Correspondent banking is an arrangement under which one bank (correspondent) holds deposits owned by other banks (respondents) and provides payment and other services to those respondent banks. CBRs are an essential feature of the global payment system – they enable individuals, businesses, and governments to make and receive cross-border payment services related to remittances, e-commerce, trade, and official sector flows. The cross-border transactions enabled in PICs are in various currencies, primarily the US dollar, Euro, and Australian dollar.

The withdrawal of CBRs, a well-documented global phenomenon affecting many emerging markets and developing economies, has adverse consequences and negative externalities for Pacific Islanders, including seasonal laborers, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and vulnerable populations. Based on publicly available data, the number of active correspondents for Pacific banks has declined significantly since 2011 to levels that put the Pacific financial system overall at risk.

In order to mitigate the issues identified above, the WB will provide funding to the Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) to implement the proposed “Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project”.  The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges and foster collaboration and cooperation in pursuing shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources, and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members' shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance, and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.    The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions, and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

The project will have two components: (1) Temporary correspondent banking services and (2) Enabling environment and regulatory harmonization.  The proposed project will be implemented by a Project Management Unit (PMU) within the PIFS with strategic project oversight provided by a Project Steering Committee (PSC) comprised of representatives of participating Pacific Finance Ministers. While the PMU will be responsible for day-to-day project activities, it will need to ensure close collaboration and coordination with participating Ministries of Finance, which will oversee project activities and approve work plans through the PSC.

Comprising of Secretaries of Finance or other officials from the participating PICs finance ministries and the PIFS Director (Programs and Initiative), the PSC will meet on a quarterly basis and be responsible for the approval of key project activities as needed. The PSC will report to Pacific Finance Ministers annually at the Forum Economic Minister Meeting (FEMM) to ensure that strategic guidance and orientation are provided over the project activities. At the technical level, each participating PIC will be required to nominate a competent   government official as a Country Focal Point (CFP) responsible for project coordination at the national level, who will be designated as the point of contact with the PMU and the WB team.

The competent government official in each PIC will be complemented by a country coordinator (CC) based in-country, recruited through the PMU, and responsible for coordinating service delivery at the individual country level.

The PIFS is now seeking qualified and competent national consultants from each member country to be the country coordinator (CC) for the PMU and based in the respective participating Pacific Island countries (PICs).  The required positions are expected to be selected by the PIFS in accordance with the WB’s ‘Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers’ (Procurement Regulations), fifth edition, September 2023, and as amended over time.

2. Objective of the Position

The main objective of the CC would be to provide on the ground support to the PMU in managing and coordinating the full range of project, country specific activities. The CC will be funded by the project (through the PMU) and report to the PIFS/ PMU Coordinator.  In addition, he/she will work closely with the specific Country Focal Point (CFP), a government official appointed by the MOF of that particular PIC.

3. Scope of Services

The CC will be required to adopt a flexible approach to coordinate and facilitate the required country specific project activities and report on tangible outcomes in terms of project implementation progress. The CC will be required to work in a pro-active manner, and to help ensure effective implementation of activities and delivery of outputs in a timely manner.

The selected CC will undertake the following activities:

  1. Liaising with PICs Ministry of Finance’s CFP and Central Bank on country specific project related activities, including follow up on the Project Steering Committee (PSC) meetings and preparing meeting minutes as required;
  2. Work in close coordination with the CFP in developing the annual country specific activities, budgets to be submitted to the PIFS/PMU;
  3. Follow up closely on all country specific procurement activities to ensure that there are no delays in the selection process;
  4. In coordination with the CFP, identifying problems/impediments promptly as they arise during project implementation and take timely remedial actions;
  5. Monitoring, with assistance of the PMU M&E specialist, the progress of the country specific project activities and its results indicators;
  6. Follow up closely on all country specific financial management activities to ensure that there are no delays in the payment process;
  7. Follow up closely on the country specific activities and report to the CFP and the PMU Project Coordinator;
  8. Work closely with the CFP and review reports/outputs prepared by selected consultants and provide inputs to the CFP as required;
  9. Prepare the required documentation for the payment of outputs prepared by the selected consultants, obtain CFP approval and submit documents to the PMU for payment;
  10. Work closely with the CFP in preparing annual reports on country specific activities to be submitted to the MOF and PIFS; and
  11. Any other activities as requested by the CFP or the PMU Project Coordinator.

 

4. Reporting Obligations

The CC will attend scheduled virtual meetings with the PMU and provide weekly reports on work done

 

5. Institutional Arrangements

This is a part-time work assignment, with the Consultant expected to be based in in their home country. The Consultant will be supported by the PIFS PMU based in Suva, Fiji but will work closely with and report to the country focal person in the first instance. The CC is expected to show flexibility in working arrangements as time inputs will fluctuate based on country requirements. The work will be part-time averaging approximately 12 days per month for the next four years. A contract will initially be signed for two years with a performance-based extension every two years thereafter. Performance evaluation shall be the basis for the extension or termination of the services. Facilities such as office space, intercom telephone facilities, personal computers, printing facilities, Internet access and stationery shall be the responsibility of the Country Coordinator.

 

6. Performance Indicators

The following performance indicators shall be used for performance assessment:

  1. Positive progress and good performance of the entrusted project activities, as per the TOR;
  2. Ensuring that WB processes and procedures are complied with in all activities and in accordance with the POM;
  3. Provide and maintain strategic engagement, networking and collaboration with key stakeholders;
  4. Ensure the utilization and management of project funds are in compliance with the Financing Agreement;
  5. Ensure the collection of all data required to track project progress;
  6. Ensure the project monitoring and reporting timeline is adhered to;
  7. Prepare and compile periodic semi-annual and annual reports on project activities
  8. Compile proposed annual workplan for the following year with budget and procurement plan;
  9. Positive evaluation of performance by the PIFS and the WB team;
  10. Effective management of other experts engaged by the PMU; and
  11. Support in implementing any capacity building agendas related to the Project as required.

 

7. Confidentiality and Conflict of Interest

The CC undertakes to comply with PIF’s and WB’s policies and rules with regard to anti-corruption and prevention of fraudulent practices, conflict of interest and confidentiality. The CC shall maintain confidentiality on all sensitive information obtained during the assignment and shall not publish wholly or in part the findings or such information, without prior written consent by the PIF. Any draft reports and other documents produced by the consultant will be discussed and cleared with the PIF and the WB before their final issue. A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) will be signed between the PIFS and the selected candidate to be attached to the contract.

 

8. Evaluation Requirements

Assignment Title: Preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment and Associated Environmental and Social Instruments for the Proposed Hazardous Waste Treatment and Landfill Facility in Georgia

Reference No.: GFPP /CS/CQS-02

The Government of Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Preparation Grant for Georgia Water Supply, Sanitation, Wastewater, and Hazardous Waste Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and associated environmental and social instruments for the hazardous waste management facilities proposed under the Feasibility Study (FS). These may include pre-treatment facilities (for example, segregation, dewatering and conditioning of oily sludges, contaminated soils and chemical residues); treatment facilities (such as physico-chemical treatment, neutralization and stabilization/solidification, thermal treatment); an engineered hazardous waste landfill; and associated storage, regional waste acceptance and temporary storage facilities, access roads, utilities and transport interfaces, as confirmed through the FS and agreed project scope. The main facility may be located near Marneuli, Kvemo Kartli, Georgia, at the site previously assessed for a non-hazardous waste (municipal) landfill, subject to confirmation. Building on the FS, the 2016 municipal landfill ESIA and available studies, the Consultant will undertake inception and scoping, review and validate existing information, identify data gaps and carry out targeted environmental and social baseline surveys and sampling; assess Georgian environmental assessment, screening, registration and permitting requirements for each relevant facility, alongside applicable World Bank Environmental and Social Standards and EHS Guidelines; describe reasonable alternatives considered in the FS and assess the preferred configuration without repeating technical selection or conceptual design; assess construction, operational, closure and post-closure impacts, including groundwater and soil contamination, emissions, effluents and leachate, hazardous waste handling and transport, worker and community health and safety, credible accidents, emergency preparedness, and climate and natural-hazard risks; undertake stakeholder engagement and disclosure; prepare a detailed, costed Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) and agreed additional instruments (in particular, Stakeholder Engagement Plan and Labor Management Procedures); and support statutory scoping, consultation and regulatory review. The ESIA will be coordinated with the FS and engineering teams and will address regional storage and acceptance facilities to the extent required by their confirmed activities, capacities and applicable regulatory pathways.

The indicative implementation period is approximately 14 weeks from commencement, plus mandatory statutory review and consultation periods, where applicable. The expected start date is [TO BE CONFIRMED]. Estimated level of effort (professional staff-months): [TO BE CONFIRMED]. The schedule will be coordinated with the availability of FS outputs and applicable regulatory procedures.

FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF SOMALIA

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND CIVIL AVIATION

(MoTCA)

Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1

(STAIRS2JOBS) PROJECT

 EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES

PIU Project Coordinator

Country: Federal Government of Somalia

Project ID No: P513127

Project: Somalia infrastructure development for access and jobs, phase 1 (stairs2jobs) project

Consultant Service: MOTCA PIU Project Coordinator 

Individual/Firm: Individual

Duty Station: Mogadishu

Deadline:November 21 2026

Ref: SO-MOTCA-567865-CS-INDV

 

1.  BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

The Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA) is implementing the Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1 (Stairs2Jobs) Project, financed by the World Bank under the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA). The Project Development Objective (PDO) of Phase 1 is to increase access to resilient infrastructure and infrastructure sector jobs, and to improve the capacity of select institutions.

MoTCA is responsible for the overall management, coordination, supervision, and implementation of all project activities under the Ministry. This includes ensuring the timely implementation of civil works; the procurement of goods, works, and services; and compliance with applicable environmental and social requirements. The Ministry oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure that project activities are implemented in accordance with the required technical, quality, environmental, and social standards. It is also responsible for managing project financial activities in coordination with the EAFD, facilitating the timely processing of payments, and preparing periodic work plans, budgets, progress reports, and other required project documentation.

In addition, MoTCA is responsible for implementing the project’s Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), monitoring and evaluating implementation progress and results, addressing implementation challenges, and regularly reporting project performance, progress, and key issues to the World Bank.

To strengthen the effective management, coordination, and implementation of these responsibilities, MoTCA intends to utilise financing under the Stairs2Jobs Project to recruit a Project Coordinator to support the Ministry in the overall coordination and implementation of project activities.

2.  RESPONSIBILITIES

The PIU Project Coordinator for MoTCA will serve as the focal point for coordination and leadership in the effective planning, implementation, and monitoring of all activities under the Stairs2Jobs Project at the MoTCA level. The Project Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing cross-sectoral project activities, ensuring they are implemented in line with approved project objectives, timelines, and budgets. He or she will facilitate coordination and communication among key stakeholders to ensure smooth and efficient project delivery.

All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Ministry’s website at https://motca.gov.so, or upon request via in-person submission or email.

3.  SELECTION CRITERIA

The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience, and skills of the candidate, followed by an interview. The required qualifications, experience, and competencies include:

  • A master’s degree in transport or aviation management, engineering, infrastructure management, public administration, business administration, accounting, economics, or another discipline directly relevant to infrastructure project implementation, institutional coordination, or public-sector programme management, from a recognised university.
  • A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in project management, infrastructure implementation, transport, aviation, or public administration — of which at least four (4) years must be in transportation, aviation, or infrastructure development related roles, preferably within an FCV context and/or on donor-funded projects.
  • Certification in one or more of the following areas will be given preference: Transport Operations or Planning (TPP), Infrastructure Project Management, Consulting Engineering (FIDIC), Air Traffic Control (ATC), Aeronautical Information Management/Services (AIM), Communication, Navigation and Surveillance (CNS), Airport Management, or other relevant technical certifications from recognised institutions.
  • Demonstrated experience working with government ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs), development partners, or multilateral institutions.

4.  REPORTING

The Consultant will report to the Director General of MoTCA and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leaders for the Stairs2Jobs Project.

5.  DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

The MoTCA PIU Project Coordinator shall be contracted for an initial period of one (1) year, renewable subject to a satisfactory performance evaluation by the Ministry, approval by the World Bank, and the availability of project funds.

6.  SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must submit the following:

  • A Curriculum Vitae (CV) including three (3) referees.
  • Copies of certificates of academic qualifications.
  • Copy of the passport or ID
  • A cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing — Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2025) (the “Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

7.  DEADLINE AND ADDRESS FOR SUBMISSION

Expressions of Interest and CVs must be delivered to the address below — by hand, mail, courier, or email — on or before Saturday, 21 November 2026 at 16:00 hours.

Interested applicants may obtain further information, including the detailed Terms of Reference, from MoTCA in person or by email at the address given below during office hours, from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Saturday to Thursday.

ADDRESS FOR SUBMISSION

Acting PIU Coordinator, Stairs2Jobs Project

Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA)

Physical address: Shangaani District Corso Somalia Street

Email: to: stairs2jobs.procurement@motca.gov.so

Cc: dg@motca.gov.so

Office hours: 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m., Saturday to Thursday.

data.notice_text:
Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh

Ministry of Social Welfare

Department of Social Services

Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience,

Inclusion, and Targeting (SSPIRIT) Project

21/1 & 21/2 Bir Uttam A.N.M. Nuruzzaman Sarak,

Shyamoli Square (9th Floor), Shyamoli, Dhaka-1207.

   Memo No.41.01.0000.126.07.007.2026-387                                                   Date: 28 October 2026

 

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

 

The World Bank is supporting the Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh to better serve the poorest and most vulnerable populations by expanding coverage and strengthening delivery of the national social protection system for the poor through an IDA Credit of USD 200 million for the “Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience, Inclusion and Targeting (SSPIRIT)” project. Key features of the initiative include, i) establishment and roll out of a Dynamic Social Registry (DSR), which will act as a central platform to improve the accuracy and efficiency of identifying and supporting beneficiaries; ii) strengthening Institutional Capacity for service delivery; iii) enhancing benefits adequacy of allowance programs; iv) strengthening skills development and complementary services; and v) providing tailored livelihood support to vulnerable group.

 

DSS intends to utilize a part of this credit to hire a Procurement Specialist as an individual national consultant to ensure effective management of the Project.   

 

  1. Procurement Specialist (Package SD-01): 1 Position

 

Qualifications & Experience

  1. At least bachelor’s in engineering, or Masters in procurement/MBA/Commerce or other relevant fields;
  2. Professional certifications/degree in Procurement from any recognized institution will be given preference;
  3. At least ten (10) years of general experience out of which seven (7) years of experience in procurement in government/semi-government institutions, or with international donors, implementing development projects; or having had other responsibilities with a substantial procurement content especially in procurement of services and goods (i.e. preparation of bidding documents and requests for proposals; use of internationally accepted contract documents; understanding of principles underlying procurement practices; analytical capability in identifying and resolving procurement issues; etc.);
  4. At least 02 (Two) years’ experience in managing procurement under projects funded by multilateral organizations such as ADB/AIIB/IsDB/JICA and particularly World Bank;
  5. Hands-on experience in managing all steps in the procurement process, including procurement planning, preparation of bidding/contract documents, bid/proposal evaluation, contract award and implementation monitoring of procurement of goods, works and consultant services;
  6. Understanding of Bangladesh Government’s procurement Rule/Act;
  7. Analytical capability in identifying and resolving procurement issues;
  8. Strong coordination and communications skills in presenting, discussing and resolving difficult issues;
  9. Ability to work efficiently and effectively in a multidisciplinary team;
  10. Excellent computer skills;
  11. Excellent English writing and speaking ability;
  12. During the term of the contract the consultant shall not be associated with any other Government agency, consulting firm or private business entities;
  13. Individuals who are currently working as procurement consultants on another World Bank-financed project may also compete in this selection process, but if they are selected, they will be required before signing the proposed contract to provide documentary evidence of having satisfactorily complied with their existing contract’s requirements with respect to early termination of the contract by the consultant, including advance notice period, to avoid disruption in implementation of that project.

 

  • SSPIRIT, DSS now invites eligible applicant(s) to indicate their interest in providing the services mentioned above. The Applicants are invited for providing information in detail including their qualifications to perform the service (complete CV along with a description of the similar assignment, experience in similar position and conditions, general qualification etc.)

(i) Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest, and

data.notice_text:
Request for Expression of Interest

(Consulting Services- Individual Consultant Selection)

Urban Development Bureau, Urban Productive Safety Net and Job Project (UPSNJP)

Grant Number- D732-ET

Oromia Urban Development Bureau invite qualified eligible individuals of the following positions for Regional Urban Productive Safety Net and Job Project PCU, which is financed by World Bank and Government of Ethiopia.

Position # 1: Procurement Specialist for Regional HUB

Required number: 1

Ref # ET-OROMIA-UDHB-573623-CS-INDV for Regional HUB

  Specific roles and responsibilities

  1. Managing the procurement management of the Project for procurement of goods, works and non-consulting in accordance with agreed procurement procedures for the project.
  2. Providing technical support and guidance to other implementing agencies in all aspects of procurement of works, goods and services.
  3. Monitoring procurement in IAs at cities to ascertain compliance with the World Bank and GoE procurement regulations.
  4. Preparing and Updating the UPSNJP Procurement Plan and regularly updating and uploading the documents and information in Systematic Tracking and Exchange in procurement (STEP).
  5. Coordinating/conducting the preparation of Terms of Reference, Request for Expression of Interest, Shortlisting, Invitation of Bid, preparation of a comprehensive and complete Bidding documents for Works, Goods, and non-consulting services. 
  6. Ensure that proper maintenance of files and Procurement Register Books are up-to-date in STEP as well as in hard copy.
  7. Present monthly technical reports and perform any other duties assigned by Project Coordinator.

    Required qualifications and Experience

  • MSc/MA/BSc/BA from a reputable and recognized university in Commerce, Business Administration, Economics, accounting, management or any other related discipline
  • Training in procurement or a professional qualification in procurement.
  • At least 6/8 years’ experience in procurement in a large private/ public sector organization or Projects for Masters and Bachelor degree respectively.
  • At least 2/3 years procurement experience in GOE/IDA funded Projects thorough understanding of World Bank’s procurement regulations, Federal and regional government procurement procedures.
  • Excellent writing and communication skills both in Amharic and English
  • Experience and knowledge on the Systematic Tracking and Exchange in procurement (STEP) is an added advantage.

Position #2: Livelihood Specialist for Regional HUB

Required number: 1

Ref # ET-OROMIA-UDHB-573642-CS-INDV

Specific roles and responsibilities

  • Provide expert technical advice and input to local governments and city project teams on best-practice urban livelihoods approaches and social protection strategies.
  • Develop regional and city-level Livelihood Development Plans, outlining target groups, activities, timelines, resources, and expected outcomes.
  • Coordinate with city project officers, community organizations, and other stakeholders to ensure activities are well-planned, sequenced, and responsive to local needs.
  • Design and implement service linkages (financial literacy, access to finance, market/value chains for input and output sourcing, access to workspaces, etc.) for sustainable livelihood development.
  • Track, document, and report on partnerships, service linkages, and market integration outcomes, providing evidence and lessons to inform adaptive management and continuous improvement.
  • Prepare timely and high-quality progress reports, review reports, mission reports, and project completion reports as required by the project.
  • Carry out any other assignments related to livelihoods and jobs as delegated by the Regional Project Coordination Hub or Project Coordinator.

  Qualification and Experience Requirements

    • Minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree in Economics, Urban Planning, Business Administration, Management, Sociology, Development Studies, or a closely related discipline.
    • At least 8 years (Master’s) or 10 years (Bachelor’s) of progressively responsible experience in urban livelihoods development, enterprise development, or related areas.
    • Demonstrated experience in establishing partnerships and service linkages with private sector actors, NGOs, financial service providers, and government-supported initiatives.
    • Experience supporting market linkages, business formalization, and promoting sustainable exit strategies for project beneficiaries.
    • A minimum of 5 years’ experience working with local governments, urban development agencies, municipal structures, or urban communities.
    • Demonstrated experience in World Bank or other donor-funded project environments is a strong advantage.
    •  Written and verbal communication skills in English and Amharic; knowledge of local languages is an asset.
    • Advanced report writing, data analysis, and presentation skills.

Duration of Assignment: The assignment will be a one-year contract, with possible extension upon satisfactory performance of the consultant for both positions.

Remunerations: As per the revised Ministry of Finance channel one salary scale for both positions.

 

How to apply:

Applicants should enclose their expression of interest including CV, letter of application, Copy of Educational document and Work Experience and other supportive documents to the address HR Administration Building Directorate, 2nd floor of building in person or by e-mail: duressad1976@gmail.com or urgessaregasa234@gmail.com for ten (10) working days starting from this announcement during office hours.

Oromia National Regional State, Urban Development Bureau, HR Administration and Capacity Building Directorate, 3rd floor of building.

Finfine Oromia Bureau Compound, Around Sarbet (Near to Pushkin Square) on the way to Kera left Side

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

Country: Moldova

Name of Project: Moldova Rural Connectivity Project

Project ID: P180153

 

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Construction Supervision of the Design & Build Contract for the Rehabilitation of road G33: R12 – Mîndîc – Zguria – Mrculeti – R13 and G35: R14 – epilova – Vanina – Cinarii Vechi – G33 (Corridor 5)

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MRCP/CS/C5/01

 

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank (the “Bank” or the “WB”) in the form of a loan/credit toward the cost of the Moldova Rural Connectivity Project. The S.A. “Administraia Naional a Drumurilor” (“NRA” or JSC “National Road Administration”), an implementing agency (the “Client”), intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan/credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is issued.

 

The selected Consultant is expected to provide professional assistance to the Client in administration of the WB funded Contract with due diligence and by carrying out the duties of the Engineer as defined in the conditions of the Works Contract.

 

The duties of the Consultant for the supervision of the execution of design and works under Corridor 5, as per the “FIDIC Conditions of Contract for Plant & Design-Build (2nd Edition, 2017; Reprinted 2022 with amendments)” published by the Federation Internationale Des Ingenieurs – Conseils (FIDIC).

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained following a formal request to the Client to procurement.wb@andsa.md.

 

The Assignment is expected to start in May 2027 and has an estimated overall duration of 42 months, which includes 30 months of works supervision and 12 months covering Defects Notification Period the Performance Certificates issue and other closing activities, Final Account and Contract close-out.

 

The estimated minimum number of person-months required for the assignment is 211 person-months. This includes 67 person-months for Key Staff.

The Client’s estimation of the necessary input for Non-Key Staff/Technical Support Staff is 134 person-months and 10 person-months for short-term experts.

 

The NRA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Consulting Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Consultant will be a firm or a group of firms (JVCA[1]) with previous project experience related to Construction Supervision Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. Core business/structure and years of experience in business:
  • at least 10 years of experience in consulting services in the road sector.
  • Demonstrated satisfactory technical and administrative capacity. The number of permanent staff of the consultant must be at least 10 for each of the last 5 years starting 1st of January 2021 at the deadline for submission of proposals. The average annual turnover of the consultant must be at least EUR 500,000 (Five Hundred Thousand) equivalent for each of the last 3 years starting 1st of January 2022 until the deadline for submission of proposals.

data.title: Consultoría por los Servicio de supervisión técnica del proyecto de perforación de pozos geotérmicos en campo geotérmico Chinameca
data.project_name: El Salvador Geothermal Energy for Sustainable and Inclusive Development
data.notice_text:
INVITACIÓN A PRESENTAR EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS
(SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA-SELECCIÓN DE FIRMAS)


País: El Salvador
Proyecto: “Energía Geotérmica para el Desarrollo Sostenible e Inclusivo”
Préstamo No.: 9788-SV
Título Asignado: Servicios de Supervisión Técnica del contrato identificado como “Servicios de perforación y de suministros de materiales, accesorios, tuberías y servicios complementarios para la perforación de 8 pozos geotérmicos en el campo geotérmico Chinameca”.


Referencia No.: SV-LAGEO-534014-CS-QCBS


La Comisión Ejecutiva Hidroeléctrica del Río Lempa (CEL) ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para el proyecto “Energía Geotérmica para el Desarrollo Sostenible e Inclusivo” y se propone utilizar una parte de los fondos para la contratación de los servicios de consultoría mencionados en la referencia.


Los servicios de consultoría (“los servicios”) comprenden la supervisión técnica, operativa, de seguridad industrial y ambiental, así como la administración del contrato mencionado en el encabezamiento. Las funciones de la firma consultora se alinearán estrictamente con el rol de “El Ingeniero”, descripto en el contrato estipulado entre LaGeo y el contratista de perforación, bajo las condiciones del Libro Rojo de FIDIC (Edición 2017, reimpresa en 2022). El alcance de las obras a ser supervisadas es la perforación y completamiento de ocho (8) pozos geotérmicos profundos, de los cuales cinco (5) son con fines de producción de fluido bifásico agua/vapor y tres (3) para reinyección de agua geotérmica separada, bajo la modalidad de un Servicio Integrado de Perforación.


Los Términos de Referencia de esta asignación estarán disponibles en la página web de LaGeo (http://www.lageo.com.sv), o podrán ser solicitados directamente al Contratante a través de la dirección de contacto indicada al final de la presente solicitud.


La empresa ejecutora LAGEO S.A. de C.V., invita a firmas consultoras elegibles (¨Los Consultores”) a expresar su interés en prestar los servicios solicitados. En la Expresión de Interés, las firmas interesadas deberán proporcionar información que demuestre que cuentan con las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia pertinente para ejecutar los servicios.


Los criterios para la conformación de la lista corta son los siguientes:

  • Experiencia en la supervisión técnica y operativa de proyectos de perforación profunda (1,500-3,000 metros de profundidad) en campos geotérmicos o de petróleo y gas.
  • Experiencia en la supervisión de obras bajo contratos FIDIC, actuando en el rol de "El Ingeniero".
  • Experiencia en la supervisión de planes de gestión ambiental, social y de salud y seguridad ocupacional, bajo estándares de organismos multilaterales de crédito u otros internacionales equivalentes.

La experiencia deberá registrarse en el formulario EXP-2 Experiencia específica de la firma, que acompaña a esta solicitud de expresión de interés.


Se valorará positivamente:

  • Haber supervisado pozos geotérmicos.
  • Experiencia en la región centroamericana.
  • Contar con sistemas de gestión de calidad, ambiental, y salud y seguridad ocupacional certificados (ej. ISO 9001, 14001, 45001 o equivalentes), y;
  • Experiencia en la supervisión o aplicación del Marco Social y Ambiental del Banco Mundial.

La expresión de interés de los Consultores es requerida bajo el párrafo 7.16 (conformación de la lista corta) de las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, edición septiembre 2023 (en adelante las Regulaciones). data.title: Recruitment of an Individual Consultant to Develop the Adaptive Social Protection (ASP) Sub-Window Manual and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)
data.project_name: The Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills, and Equity Project
data.notice_text:
Country:        The Republic of the Gambia

Project Name: The Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills and Equity Project

Project Number: P179233                    

Reference No.:       GM-CPCU - MOFEA-573311-CS-INDV

Selection Method: Individual Consultant Selection

Assignment Tittle:     Request for Expressions of Interest - Recruitment of an Individual Consultant to Develop the Adaptive Social Protection (ASP) Sub-Window Manual and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

Project Background

 The Government of The Gambia has secured Additional Financing (AF) under the Resilience, Inclusion, Skills, and Equity (RISE) Project (P179233), supported by the International Development Association (IDA) and the Global Shield Financing Facility (GSFF), to strengthen the country’s capacity to respond to climate and disaster-related shocks.

The AF introduces a new Subcomponent 3.4: Strengthening Disaster Risk Financing (DRF) and Adaptive Social Protection (ASP), which aims to integrate prearranged disaster risk financing mechanisms with shock-responsive social protection systems. This includes the establishment and capitalization of an Adaptive Social Protection (ASP) Sub-Window under the Social Protection Fund (SPF).

The ASP Sub-Window will serve as a dedicated, rules-based financing mechanism to enable timely and predictable delivery of emergency cash transfers to poor and vulnerable households affected by shocks such as droughts, floods, and food price crises.

Objectives of the assignment

The main objective of this consultancy is to develop a comprehensive, rules-based ASP Sub-Window Operational Manual and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) that will guide the governance, management, and utilization of funds for shock-responsive social protection interventions.

 

Scope of Services:

The consultant will develop the ASP Sub-Window Operational Manual addressing the following elements:

  1. Institutional and Governance Framework
  2. Define explicit time benchmarks for each step in the response chain (trigger confirmation, activation decision, beneficiary list finalization, payment instruction, first transfer received), calibrated to the project target of 60% of beneficiaries receiving their first transfer within 60 days of trigger activation. Reference the 2-week on-time Nafa payment standard as the operational baseline.
  3. Position the ASP Sub-Window clearly within the national risk-layering framework
  4. Financial and Investment Framework
  5. Activation protocols (“triggers”)
  6. Create a placeholder section that will outline when exactly an emergency response via the ASP Sub-Window will be activated. The consultant should create an outline detailing the type of information required per subsection. This section will then be filled separately.

 

Qualifications & Experience of the Consultant:

The individual consultant should have:

  • A Master’s degree in economics, public policy, finance, or related field.
  • At least 10 years of demonstrated experience in the design or management of disaster response funds and adaptive social protection systems.
  • Proven experience working in developing countries. Experience working in West Africa –ideally The Gambia – is an advantage.
  • Knowledge of the design of sovereign risk transfer instruments is an advantage.
  • Knowledge of the rules and regulations guiding the management of national funds in The Gambia is an advantage.
  • Knowledge of the financial management rules and regulations of the World Bank guiding supported projects is an advantage.
  • Excellent command of the English language
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and experience interacting with senior government officials.
  • Capacity to work independently with minimal supervision and to deliver work within agreed deadlines.

Submission of Expressions of Interest:

The Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs (MoFEA), through the Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills and Equity Project, now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2025(“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant firm will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultants (IC) set out in the Guidelines for Recruitment of Consultants.

Further information and the full TOR can be obtained from the email addresses below during office hours from 08:30 to 16:00 GMT Mondays to Thursdays and from 0830 to 12:30 GMT on Fridays.

Expressions of interest should be delivered by electronic mail on or before 23rd November 2026 at 12h30 GMT

Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills and Equity Project, RISE

Royal Insurance Building

2nd Floor, Kotu Bertil Harding Highway

The Gambia

Consulting Services for the Development, Deployment, Rollout and Post-Deployment Support for a Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS)

REFERENCE No.:     LR-MOGCSP-546313-CS-CQS

The Government of the Republic of Liberia through the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Liberia Women Empowerment Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the Consulting Services for the Development, Deployment, Rollout and Post-Deployment Support of a Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS) at the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MGCSP)

 

Objective of the Assignment  

The objective of the consultancy is to develop and operationalize an integrated Gender-Based Management Information System (GB MIS) for the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MGCSP) that will enhance the Ministry’s institutional capacity to systematically collect, capture, store, manage, analyze, visualize, and report gender-related data and information. The consultancy will cover the design, development, testing, deployment, rollout, user training, documentation, and post-deployment support of the GB MIS, ensuring that the system is scalable, secure, interoperable, user-friendly, and aligned with the Ministry’s gender data and information management requirements.

The system is expected to improve the availability, quality, accessibility, timeliness, and use of sex- and gender-disaggregated data to support evidence-based policy and program planning, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, coordination, and decision-making at national and sub-national levels

The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (“the Client”) now invites eligible Consultants to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) in providing the Services. Interested firms must provide their detailed profile demonstrating that they meet the following shortlisting criteria:

  • Core business of the firm/JV/Consortium that is relevant to the assignment  
  • At least 7 years of general experience in design, development, deployment, and support of Management Information Systems (MIS), digital platforms, or integrated ICT systems.
  • At least 5 years of specific experience implementing MIS or digital systems for government institutions, donor-funded projects, or development partner-supported programs. 
  • Have a proven record of successful completion of at least 3 similar MIS or digital system assignments within the last 5–7 years, of comparable scope and complexity.
  • Have experience implementing at least 2 assignments for government institutions, donor-funded, or development partner-financed programs, preferably in the social, gender, GBV, or related sectors. Experience in West Africa is an advantage.
  • Demonstrated experience in delivering end-to-end digital solutions, including system design, development, integration, deployment, training, documentation, and postdeployment support.
  • Demonstrated experience in system integration, interoperability, data management, and scalable solutions for decentralized or multi-location operations.
  • Evidence of capacity for knowledge transfer, user training, technical support, and preparation of system and operational documentation.
  • Evidence of technical and managerial capability to complete the assignment (Provide only the structure of the firm, general qualifications, and number of key staff. Do not provide CVs of staff as Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.)  

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the fact that the selection of Firm/Consortium will be done in accordance with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (“Procurement Regulations”) dated July 2016, revised in November 2017 and August 2018, and updated in November 2020, September 2023, February 2025, and September 2025

The completed expression of interest documents in writing, three (3) copies, must be delivered to the Procurement Unit or by email to the address below to be received on or before November 23, 2026, at 1500 hours GMT. Renewable Energy Generation and Access INcrease Project (REGAIN)

Grant No.: E331-MH
REGAIN Project
Reference No. MH-MEC-563965-CS-CQS

November 23, 2026


The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has received financing from the International
Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a grant (hereinafter called “the Grant”), in the
amount of US$60 million, toward the cost of the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase (REGAIN)
Project (P181250), approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030.
The Marshalls Energy Company (MEC), as Employer and implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of
the proceeds of the Grant to eligible payments under a contract for consulting services to prepare and support an
implementation plan for renewable energy, energy efficiency and e-mobility under the Energy Act, 2025 and the
National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions, under Sub-Component 3.1
(Sector Development Assistance) of the REGAIN Project. The assignment shall be carried out in close
coordination with the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA) and shall cover all MEC-served
systems, including Majuro, Ebeye and the outer islands.
The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise proposing activities to be undertaken in the short, medium,
and long term and undertaking them to strengthen the capacity of key energy sector stakeholders by focusing on
regulation, target setting, monitoring tools, dissemination of progress, feedback, and course correction to
promote security, safety, reliability, and sustainability of energy supply (excluding petroleum) in RMI as per the
provisions of the EA 2025 and aligned with the National Energy Authority Act, 2025. Services include, among
others:
• Diagnostic review of the Electricity Sector (in particular RE, EE and E-Mobility) of the Marshall Islands;
• Strategic review of the applicable RMI’s electricity sector-related international and national commitments
and targets;
• Propose a strategy for addressing the identified gaps;
• Assessing the Institutional structure and the manpower requirements of the Energy sector;
• Monitoring, Database and Reporting Framework for RE;
• Electricity tariff review and recommendations, building on MEC’s existing tariff methodology and
extending it to Ebeye; and
• Addressing the recommendations by preparing, revising, or aligning the policies, regulations, codes,
guidelines, and other instruments required to give effect to the relevant provisions of the Energy Act, 2025
and the National Energy Authority Act, 2025, excluding petroleum-sector provisions.
The assignment is structured as a lump-sum contract with an estimated duration of 9 months, with an expected
start date in January 2027. The selected firm will nominate a multidisciplinary team, including the Key Experts
described in the attached TOR, and will report to MEC, coordinating closely with NEA, the World Bank, and
other relevant stakeholders.
The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.
MEC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.
Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and
relevant experience to perform the Services.
The shortlisting criteria, as set out in Section 10 of the attached TOR, are:
1. Experience preparing energy-sector legal, policy and regulatory frameworks, or implementation plans
for energy legislation, including regulations, codes and licensing (35 points)

system utilities, preferably with high renewable energy penetration (25 points)
