REPUBLIC OF MOLDOVA

GEF/WB  Project: Restoring ecosystems for marine pollution prevention” (ReMaP) (P505546)

Assignment Title: Senior International Advisor for Forestry Sector Reform in Moldova

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MD-NOIEP-577223-CS-INDV

Moldova “Restoring Ecosystems for Marine Pollution Prevention” (REMAP) Project, financed by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and supported by the World Bank, is implemented through the National Office for the Implementation of Environmental Projects (NOIEP) under the Ministry of Environment (MoE). REMAP is a flagship national initiative promoting Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to restore ecosystems and reduce land-based pollution in the Dniester River Basin. The project aligns with Moldova’s priorities under the EU approximation agenda, the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and the Paris Agreement, demonstrating that healthy, community-supported ecosystems underpin climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods.

REMAP supports ecosystem restoration and sustainable watershed management to reduce land-based nutrient pollution entering the Dniester River and ultimately the Black Sea. Its Project Development Objective is to increase the area under sustainable landscape management practices in targeted areas within the Dniester River Basin in Moldova. Institutional strengthening and improved forest governance, including implementation of the Forest Code No. 69/2024, are central to achieving this objective.

The Senior International Advisor shall serve as the Minister of Environment's principal international strategic and technical advisor on forestry sector reform. The Advisor shall provide independent, high-level guidance on transition implementation, governance modernization, EU accession alignment, and resource mobilization, while bringing relevant international experience to bear on Moldova's specific circumstances and priorities. All reform decisions and implementation authority remain with the competent national authorities.

The minimum qualifications and experience for the requested position are:

Education:

  • Advanced university degree in public administration, public policy, economics, environmental policy, law, organizational development, or related discipline. Qualifications or substantive professional experience in forestry, natural resource management, or environmental governance are a strong advantage.

Essential Requirements:

  • At least 15 years of relevant experience in high-level advisory roles, institutional reform, public-sector restructuring, state-owned enterprise transformation, or environmental governance, including demonstrated experience advising ministers or senior government officials.
  • Proven strategic advisory capacity: the ability to provide frank, forward-looking counsel to senior decision-makers on politically sensitive reform processes, not merely technical analysis.
  • Hands-on implementation experience in at least one substantial institutional or sector reform following formal political, legislative, or governmental decisions, including organizational integration, transition management, and stabilization. Experience limited to assessments or reform design is insufficient.
  • Experience in financial mobilization, including engagement with international donors, development banks, or climate finance mechanisms.
  • Strong understanding of EU accession processes and environmental acquis, particularly as they relate to forestry, land use, or natural resource management.
  • Excellent analytical, drafting, communication, and facilitation skills; fluency in English.

Desirable:

  • Reform experience in Baltic, Balkan, Eastern European, or post-Soviet EU candidate country contexts.
  • Experience with anti-corruption frameworks, digital governance, or transparency systems in natural resource sectors.
  • Knowledge of carbon markets, ecosystem service payments, or climate finance instruments.
  • Familiarity with World Bank or EU-financed operations.
  • Proficiency in Romanian and/or Russian is a significant advantage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1 – Regional Project Manager 1)

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant No. TF0C5794

Assignment Title: Regional Project Manager 1

Reference No. LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is implementing projects financed by the World Bank, including: Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (UIHERP) and Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program (LEARN) Program and plans to prepare and implement new operations in cooperation with the World Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Operation(s)).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan). The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of the Consultant's assignment is to manage and coordinate the implementation of NUS reform initiatives within the designated geographical area, ensure effective adaptation of national programs to the regional context, and maintain close cooperation with local education authorities.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time November 24, 2026.  

TERMS OF REFERENCE

 

for consulting services (individual consultant)

 

Regional Project Manager 1

 

Contract No. LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

URTF Grant No. TF0C5794

 

 BACKGROUND

 

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is implementing projects financed by the World Bank, including: Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (UIHERP) and Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program (LEARN) Program and plans to prepare and implement new operations in cooperation with the World Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Operation(s)).

LEARN

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675,9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is funded by a US$235 mln credit provided by Bank resources, supported by credit enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT NUMBER 9721-UA). An additional US$150 mln is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (LOAN NUMBER 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT NUMBER 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, the Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for the Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development was signed in the amount of US$286 mln (LOAN NUMBER K019-UA).

 

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0C5794).

On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

For this program, “strategic communication and public engagement” refer to three critical aspects of ensuring the effective implementation of education policies and public trust in reforms:

i. Transparency and trust, including timely and clear communication about key initiatives, accessible information for stakeholders, and proactive crisis communication strategies to address concerns and misinformation.

ii. Awareness and outreach, especially the development of targeted campaigns, public information materials, and digital engagement strategies to ensure broad understanding and support for educational transformations among educators, parents, students, and policymakers.

iii. Capacity building in communication, ensuring that education institutions, regional authorities, and key stakeholders are equipped with the necessary tools, guidelines, and skills to effectively communicate and engage with the public regarding policy changes, funding mechanisms, and international support programs.

Effective communication is a key instrument for building trust in education reforms, shaping public perception, and ensuring stakeholder engagement. The Operation of the World Bank is inlined with the Strategic Action Plan and Communications vision of the Ministry.

 OBJECTIVE

 

The objective of this assignment is to manage and coordinate the implementation of NUS reform initiatives within the designated geographical area, ensure effective adaptation of national programs to the regional context, and maintain close cooperation with local education authorities.

 SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Manages the implementation of NUS reform initiatives in the designated geographical area.
  • Coordinates with local education authorities and stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of the reform.
  • Monitors progress and implementation challenges of the reform at the regional level.
  • Provides feedback on regional adaptation needs and implementation challenges to NIO management.
  • Supports capacity-building activities of regional education institutions.
  • Maintains regular communication with regional stakeholders.

REPORTING

The Regional Managers Coordinator reports to the LEARN Project Coordinator / Co-Coordinator and works under the supervision of the Head of the New Ukrainian School (NUS) Implementation Office. In carrying out their duties, the Consultant works closely with the Deputy Heads of the NUS Implementation Office and the Heads of the relevant functional units to ensure coordinated planning, management, and implementation of communication activities across the NUS reform portfolio.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports describing the tasks performed, key results achieved, and challenges identified..

 RESOURCES PROVIDED

MoES provides the Consultant with the information necessary to perform his/her assignment in a timely manner. At the same time, the Consultant independently arranges his/her own workplace, including the equipment necessary to perform his/her functions (e.g., PC, communication means and office equipment).

 QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • At least 2 years of experience in managing education projects and administering/implementing them
  • At least 1 year of experience in cooperation with national and local authorities
  • At least 2 years of experience in the education sector, preferably in school education
  • Experience in cooperation with international financial or donor organizations
  • High level of English proficiency (upper intermediate or above)
  • Fluency in Ukrainian

Desirable skills and qualifications:

  • Experience in managing education projects
  • Knowledge of the specifics of the regional education system
  • Understanding of project management methodologies
  • Knowledge of the principles and objectives of the NUS reform
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail
  • Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills
  • Ability to work under conditions of high uncertainty
  • Crisis management experience

 

 DURATION AND PLACE OF WORK

The Consultant shall provide services until 31 August 2028, with the possibility of extending the contract term until the completion of the LEARN Operation.

The Consultant is expected to work on a full-time basis.

Services are planned to be provided in Kyiv, Ukraine. Business trips of the Consultant to other regions of Ukraine may be required to support the implementation of the Operation.

The Consultant may be expected to provide services remotely; however, at the Client's request, he/she shall arrive and/or provide services at the Client's premises as soon as possible.

Contract terms and working arrangements are subject to negotiation.

APPLICATION PACKAGE

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua, Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org and maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua  indicating the email subject: " LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1: Selection of Regional Project Manager 1: [NAME]".

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time November 24, 2026.

If the Consultant fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the Consultant's application.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Project: Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II)

Assignment Title: Consultancy service for Detail Design for Adigafelema irrigation scheme from groundwater sources [40 Ha]

Credit No.: IDA- 7519-ET

Procurement Reference No.: ET-DR-RPCU-571065-CS-QCBS

  1. The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank (IDA) and IFAD toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the detailed design of the Adigafelema irrigation scheme from groundwater sources [40 Ha] in Aseliso Woreda.
  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the following:

The objective of the assignment is to prepare a bankable, climate-resilient, environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, and implementation-ready irrigation scheme in accordance with national standards, the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and IFAD SECAP. Specifically, the Consultant shall:

  • Verify existing groundwater investigations (hydrogeology, boreholes, pumping tests, water quality) and assess long-term sustainability of abstraction; no new production well design is envisaged unless instructed;
  • Undertake baseline, socioeconomic, gender and social inclusion, soil and land suitability, agronomic and agricultural economics studies, and a climate-risk assessment;
  • Carry out topographic and geotechnical surveys and the feasibility study, including technical, economic and financial analysis of alternatives;
  • Prepare the ESIA and applicable ESF instruments (ESMP, SEP, LMP, IPMP, GBV/SEA/SH risk assessment);
  • Prepare detailed designs of the solar-pumped, pipe-supported surface irrigation system and drainage, drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities, cost estimates, tender documents and construction readiness package; and
  • Develop the operation and maintenance framework and Water Users Association arrangements, and build the capacity of stakeholders.

The Consultant shall carry out all investigations, surveys, analyses, assessments, stakeholder consultations, designs, cost estimates and tender document preparation to achieve the objectives above, in accordance with generally accepted professional standards, whether or not a specific activity is cited in the Terms of Reference. The estimated level of effort is 25.25 key-expert staff-months. The assignment duration is three (3) calendar months (twelve weeks) from the contract commencement date, and the assignment is expected to start on February 25th, 2027.

The Dire Dawa Administration Agriculture, Water, Mines and Energy Bureau, LLRP-II Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address given below.

3. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in irrigation and water resources engineering consultancy services; provide the company profile, registration certificate, and number of years in business;
  • Relevant experience: proven experience during the last ten (10) years in feasibility studies, detailed design and ESIA of irrigation and drainage schemes (preferably groundwater-based and/or solar-powered schemes) and preparation of tender documents; experience on World Bank- or IFAD-financed projects is an advantage. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, irrigated area, contract value, duration and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates;
  • Technical and managerial capability of the firm: managerial and organizational structure, survey and field equipment, design software (e.g. for hydraulic and pipe network design), quality assurance systems and capacity to mobilize field teams. COUNTRY:                                       Federal Republic of Somalia

NAME OF PROJECT:                    Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)  

PROJECT ID:                                    P176181         

Assignment Title:                          Consulting Firm to Undertake the Independent Valuation of Assets for the Somali National Fiber Infrastructure Company (SONFIC) Special Purpose Vehicle

Reference No.:                                SO-MOCT-FGS-580867-CS-CQS

Place of assignment:                   Mogadishu, Somalia

Submission Date:                         November 25, 2026, 2.00pm (local time, Mogadishu, Somalia)

The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP), and the Ministry of Communications and Technology intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) are required to be undertaken by an external consulting firm supporting the client, the Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS, through the EA-RDIP Project Implementation Unit (PIU), to carry out the “Consulting Firm to Undertake the Independent Valuation of Assets for the Somali National Fiber Infrastructure Company (SONFIC) Special Purpose Vehicle”. Under Component 1 of EA-RDIP, the Government is establishing a national wholesale, open-access fiber backbone through the Somali National Fiber Infrastructure Company (SONFIC), a Special Purpose Vehicle formed in September 2026 by the Government and five licensed telecommunications operators (the “Founding Operators”). Existing operator Inter-City fiber and related assets are to be contributed to SONFIC in return for shares, on the basis of an independent valuation. The Firm will act as Independent Valuer and will: (i) establish a verified inventory of the assets proposed for contribution by each Founding Operator, including technical audit, ownership, title and encumbrance checks; (ii) determine which assets are eligible; (iii) determine the fair value of each contribution under the International Valuation Standards (IVS) and IFRS 13, using cost, market and income approaches; (iv) convert accepted values into Class A share allocations and value the options for any excess contribution; and (v) hand over the asset register, valuation model and working papers to MoCT/PIU and train staff. The results must be auditable and suitable to support the SONFIC Board and shareholder resolutions authorizing each allotment. The consultant firm will undertake all the specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The assignment is expected to be completed within approximately three (3) months (thirteen (13) weeks) from contract effectiveness.

Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: https://moct.gov.so/en/jobs/  or it can be provided upon submission of application in person or by e-mail. The e-mail address is provided below.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.).  The short-listing criteria are as follows:

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm and at least eight (8) years of relevant organizational experience in asset valuation, financial advisory or transaction advisory services, with evidence of the company registration certificate, business license or operational permit, and a company profile indicating services offered and years in operation.
  2. The firm should demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) comparable valuation assignments for telecommunications, fiber optic or other network/linear infrastructure, including at least one (1) involving contributions in kind, Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) or joint venture formation, or the determination of shareholding among multiple contributors. Demonstrated application of the International Valuation Standards (IVS) and IFRS fair-value principles, and experience in physical verification of assets, including in difficult-access environments, is required. For each assignment, firms should indicate the client, contract value, duration, scope of services and the firm’s role.
  3. Demonstrate experience of relevant services implemented in Somalia, or in Africa, fragile/conflict-affected or comparable environments similar to that of Somalia; experience with public-sector clients and World Bank-financed assignments will be an advantage; and
  4. The technical and managerial organization of the firm, including documented quality-assurance systems and the capacity to manage and protect commercially sensitive data. (Provide only the structure of the firm’s organization.) Do not provide CVs of staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In particular, the Consultant shall be independent of SONFIC, the Founding Operators and their shareholders, and shall disclose any past or present relationship with them in its Expression of Interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint venture and/ or a Sub consultancy. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Interested Consultant may obtain further information in a written communication to the address below during office hours from 9.00am to 4.00pm Mogadishu time (Excluding public holidays).

Expressions of interest (EOI) should be submitted electronically (by e-mail) to the address below on, or before, 2:00 PM (Mogadishu, Somalia Local Time) on November 25, 2026.

Terms of Reference

Consulting Services for the Expertise of Projects under the Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project (TRIP)

 

TRIP-CQS-EX-01

 

  1. Background

The Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Program (TRIP) aims to promote Armenia’s tourism potential through targeted infrastructure investments and soft interventions in several regions of the country. The Program will support seven out of the twenty identified tourism clusters: Areni, Yeghegis, Jermuk, Dvin, Gyumri, Dilijan, and Goris, focusing on wine, wellness, adventure, cultural, educational, and ecotourism across the regions of Ararat, Vayots Dzor, Shirak, Aragatsotn, Tavush, and Syunik.

The Program will contribute to improving access to tourism clusters and developing infrastructure at tourist destinations. It also aims to make more effective use of Armenia’s natural resources and human capital by enhancing the business and professional skills of residents in neighboring communities, with a view to maximizing the potential for job creation. In addition, the Program is aligned with the World Bank’s approach to attracting private investment in these tourism clusters.

The objective of the Program is to improve access to climate-resilient infrastructure and increase tourism’s contribution to the local economy in the clusters supported by the Program.

 

The consulting firm will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications Selection (CQS) method, in accordance with the World Bank’s Guidelines for the Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers.

A one-time contract will be concluded with the Consultant, under which the Consultant will be tasked with reviewing the designs of three subprojects.

 

  1. Objectives

The Consultant shall review the design documentation for the following subprojects:

 

  1. “Improvement of the Dvin Archaeological Site and Adjacent Area and Development of Tourism Infrastructure”;
  2. “Partial Renovation of Dashtadem Fortress, Establishment of a Museum, and Improvement of the Area Adjacent to the Monument”;
  3. “Reconstruction of the Drinking Pavilion in the City of Jermuk, Republic of Armenia.”
  1. Scope of Services of the Consultant
  • Conduct an appraisal of the submitted designs, including verification of architectural, structural, engineering, and technological solutions and calculations, as well as construction work quantities and cost estimates, to ensure compliance with the requirements of applicable regulatory documents and standards.
  • Cooperate with the Client’s specialists during the appraisal of each assigned design project and provide the necessary information and clarifications regarding applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Carry out the appraisal activities in accordance with the schedule agreed upon with the Client.
  • In the event of new circumstances or requirements, review any revisions made to the design documentation and, where necessary, make corresponding amendments to the appraisal report.
  1. Consultant’s Reporting Obligations
  • As a report on the services performed, the Consultant shall submit an appraisal report for each design project reviewed.
  • The deadline for submitting the appraisal report for each project shall be agreed upon by the Client and the Consultant, taking into account the complexity and scope of the work, but shall not exceed 15 working days. The agreed deadline shall be specified in the terms of reference for the respective project and endorsed by both the Client and the Consultant.
  • The Organization shall submit to the Client an expert examination report prepared in accordance with the requirements established by the legislation of the Republic of Armenia, in Armenian, in two (2) hard copies and one (1) electronic scanned copy.

P509405 was signed on 30th of July 2025.  The Government of Montenegro aims to modernize payment systems through the improvement of the legal and regulatory framework and the modernization of financial infrastructure.  This Project will assist authorities in supporting the modernization of the payment’s infrastructure. The proposed Project builds directly on the existing engagement and supports authorities with necessary investment activities.   The overall Project have three components:

(i)        Providing technical assistance for setting up a new payment system and developing the broader payments ecosystem.

(ii)       Supporting the implementation and operation of the new payment system.

(iii)      Project Management.

The Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) is preparing for future participation in the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and, ultimately, in the Euro system, in line with Montenegro’s broader strategic objective of European Union (EU) accession. This process requires the continued alignment of CBCG’s institutional, operational, legal and technical frameworks with relevant EU standards and practices applicable to central banking and financial market infrastructures.

The Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) is the Project Implementing Entity and will have overall responsibility for project implementation and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for the experienced and qualified Consultancy firm is to ensure the CBCG to development of a clear TARGET Services Accession Strategy and a comprehensive but proportionate implementation roadmap for Montenegro’s participation in relevant TARGET Services. The assessment shall be tailored to Montenegro’s monetary and institutional circumstances and to the practical needs of the CBCG and banking community. The Consultant shall focus on analysis and recommendations at a level sufficient to support strategic decisions and define subsequent implementation work. Detailed system specifications, extensive institution-by-institution audits, drafting of complete legislative instruments, vendor selection, live testing and migration execution are outside the scope unless separately agreed.

The Consultant (firm/company) shall perform the required activities in cooperation with CBCG and relevant stakeholders. The ten areas correspond to the required substantive outputs described in ToR.  Findings may be consolidated into coordinated reports rather than duplicated across separate studies. The level of analysis shall be sufficient to identify decisions, implementation prerequisites and indicative costs; detailed implementation design remains a subsequent project stage.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT, HIGHWAYS AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS

Project: Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE).

Project ID: P511605.

Credit No: 7985-LK.

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Detailed Design and Construction Supervision for Arugambay Tourism Cluster development.

PP ref no: LK-REVIVE-PMU-573674-CS-QCBS.

1. The Government of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE) Project. The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development (MoTHUD), serving as the Executing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the review and validation of conceptual master plans and feasibility studies; site surveys and engineering investigations; preparation of implementable, climate-resilient detailed designs, Good for Construction drawings, design calculations, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates and World Bank-compliant bidding documents; intermittent technical support during works procurement; full-time construction supervision and contract administration; and support during the Defects Liability Period for investments at the Arugambay Tourism Cluster development including beachfront redevelopment, a lagoon ecological restoration, road improvement, tourism or public-realm development and refer to Annexure A of TOR.

3. The total duration of the assignment is expected to be approximately forty six (46) months: Phase A – Detailed Design, Bidding Documents and intermittent procurement support, ten (10) months, including four (4) months for detailed design and up to six (6) months for procurement support; Phase B – Construction Supervision and Contract Administration, twenty four (24) months; and Phase C – Defects Liability Period Support, twelve (12) months.

4. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.transport.gov.lk/ (Media > Procurement > TORs).

5. The Chairman of the Ministry Consultants Procurement Committee, on behalf of the REVIVE Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required firm-level qualifications, relevant experience and institutional capacity to perform the assignment.

 The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

(a) Legal Status, Core Business and Institutional Experience: The Consultant shall have been legally registered and in operation for at least fifteen (15) years and shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of institutional experience in detailed engineering design of multidisciplinary infrastructure, tourism or public-realm development construction supervision with contract administration. The Consultant shall submit supporting documents, including Certificate of Incorporation/ Registration, Company Profile and nature of business and evidence of relevant institutional experience.

(b) Comparable and Relevant Assignment Experience: The Consultant shall have successfully completed at least three (3) comparable consultancy assignments involving detailed engineering design and/or construction supervision with contract administration of similar nature, scope, scale, and complexity within the last ten (10) years. At least one assignment shall have included both detailed design and construction supervision with contract administration, and at least one shall have involved multidisciplinary infrastructure, tourism-related infrastructure, or public-realm development. The same assignment may satisfy both requirements. The Consultant shall provide relevant assignment details, including name, Client, location, commencement and completion dates, scope, contract value (USD equivalent), level of effort (person-months), and supporting evidence of successful completion, such as contracts, completion certificates, or client references.

(c) Management Capacity: The Consultant shall demonstrate adequate organizational, management, and technical capacity to undertake the assignment, including multidisciplinary engineering investigations, detailed design, procurement support, construction supervision, and contract administration. The Consultant shall provide relevant information on its organizational structure, technical resources, and management capacity to demonstrate its ability to perform the required services.

(d) Technical Capacity: The Consultant shall demonstrate the availability of adequate qualified and experienced professional resources and the capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary specialists required for the assignment. The Consultant shall provide information on its professional staff resources, including relevant specializations and experience. Individual Key Experts and their qualifications will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

(e) Additional Relevant Experience: Experience in World Bank or other multilateral development bank-financed assignments, coastal or environmentally sensitive settings, and in Sri Lanka, South Asia, or comparable island environments with similar physical, climatic, and institutional conditions will be considered an advantage during shortlisting.

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In accordance with Paragraph 3.17 - Consultants previously involved in the preparation of conceptual plans, feasibility studies, or related studies for the assignment shall disclose such involvement in their Expressions of Interest. To avoid any unfair competitive advantage, the Client shall make available to all shortlisted Consultants, together with the RFP, all relevant information that may provide a competitive advantage to any previously engaged Consultant.

8. A Consultant will be selected by following Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations: “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025)”.

9. Interested Consultant may obtain further information from Senior Procurement Consultant, REVIVE Project at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 15:00 hours (+94 112 - 869521) Facsimile: +94 112 861 860, E-mail: proc.revive@gmail.com only on working days.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

REPUBLIC OF TAJIKISTAN

TAJIKISTAN DIGITAL FOUNDATIONS PROJECT

Date: November 9, 2026

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Advanced Digital Skills Trainings for 1,000 individuals

Reference No.: PIC-TDFP-CS-3

State Institution "Projects Implementation Center for Tajikistan Digital Foundations" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan is implementing Tajikistan Digital Foundation Project (thereafter referred to as Project) co-financed by the World Bank and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC). The total cost of the project is US$46.2 million, of which the IDA grant is $30M, SDC Trust fund is $14.8M and GoTJ share is $1.4M. and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the Advanced Digital Skills Trainings for 1,000 individuals

 

The consultant will have to perform the following tasks:

Tasks shall include, but not be limited to, the following: Program Design and Preparation

  1. Develop a time-bound implementation plan which includes target numbers of trainees to be trained, and description of monitoring mechanisms of the training program execution and quality of training offered
  2. Develop modular digital skills training programs or use off the shelf courses on AI, Cloud, Network, System Administration and Cybersecurity aligned with labor market relevance in Tajikistan and addressing language requirements, inclusivity considerations, infrastructure constraints, and applicability of skills.
  3. Develop of complementary business soft skills training modules, that will be delivered in Russian and Tajik to enhance participants’ readiness for employment and further skills development.
  4. Ensure blended and online delivery modalities through the Platform for Educational Needs, describing delivery options, sequencing, and implementation considerations to support regional equity of access and sustainability beyond the project period.
  5. Develop an inclusive outreach and participant selection framework, including eligibility criteria and targeting approaches, to support the participation of youth, NEET populations, women, persons with disabilities, and beneficiaries in line with the inclusion targets defined in the Objective section.
  6. Develop and adapt training curricula and learning materials in Russian, English, and/or Tajik, leveraging and contextualizing existing resources available in Tajikistan and identifying gaps where supplementary materials may be required.
  7. Develop and implement employer engagement mechanisms to facilitate internships and job matching for the course beneficiaries.
  8. The Consultant shall track employment outcomes for at least six (6) months following graduation.
  9. Collaborate with other training centers to achieve the objectives of this assignment.
  10. Develop an implementation plan with milestones, deliverables, and performance indicators.
  11. Coordinate with the PIC EOP and relevant stakeholders to ensure alignment with Component 2 objectives.
  12. Transfer full documentation, training materials (free of copyrights) to PIC EOP upon contract completion.

 

Duration

The total duration of the contract is 24 months.

PROJECT ID: P180337, IDA CREDIT NO. 73380-ZM

ZM-MOT-580359-CS-QCBS

INDICATIVE ASSIGNMENT DURATION

March 2027 – June 2030, Subject to Contract Effectiveness, Financing Availability and The Project Closing Date.

Background

The Government of the Republic of Zambia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Green, Resilient and Transformational Tourism Development Project (GREAT-TDP), which is being implemented by the Ministry of Tourism (MoT) through a Project Implementation Unit (PIU). The Project seeks to enhance the sustainability, resilience, and competitiveness of Zambia's tourism sector while promoting inclusive economic opportunities and conservation outcomes in tourism destinations.

The GREAT-TDP comprises three components:

Component 1:      Strengthening Tourism Competitiveness and Destination Management;

Component 2:       Improving Access to Resilient Infrastructure; and

Component 3:      Project Administration and Management.

Under Component 1, Subcomponent 1.3, Expanding Economic Opportunities through MSMEs and Community-Based Tourism Support, the Project provides financial and technical support to tourism-related Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), Community-Based Enterprises (CBEs), Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), and Tourism Private Sector Associations (TPSAs) through a Matching Grants and Technical Assistance Program. The Program is designed to strengthen business capacity, improve competitiveness, support sustainable tourism development, and expand economic opportunities for participating beneficiaries.

Consulting Services

The Ministry of Tourism intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing for consulting services ("the Services"), which include the engagement of a Grant Management Company (GMC) to support the implementation and administration of the Matching Grants and Technical Assistance Program under Component 1 of the GREAT-TDP.

The GMC will be responsible for the overall management and administration of the Program, including outreach and communications, beneficiary engagement, application intake and evaluation, grant administration, coordination and delivery of technical assistance activities, monitoring and verification of results, operation of the Management Information System (MIS), reporting, and other related functions as described in the Terms of Reference (TOR). The GMC will support the Ministry of Tourism in ensuring that the Program is implemented efficiently, transparently, and in accordance with the Project's objectives, procedures, and applicable requirements

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at https://greattdp.gov.zm/tenders  or https://www.mot.gov.zm/?page_id=3201  or by writing at the email address given below;

 

 

The project coordinator:

Green, Resilient and Transformational Tourism Development Project

Ministry of Tourism

Kwacha House Annex

Cairo Road

Lusaka Zambia

Email: procurementgreattdp@mot.gov.zm

Copying:  greattdpprojectcoordinator@mot.gov.zm  

The Ministry of Tourism (MoT) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Service as required in the TOR. The submission should include a cover letter summarizing the relevant experience and indicating its relevance to the assignment at hand. The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  • Comparable program experience. At least 10 years of relevant organizational experience managing grant, matching-grant, or enterprise-support programs. During the 10 years preceding the EOI submission deadline, the firm must have managed at least 2 programs comparable to this assignment in scope, operational complexity, funding value, and number and type of beneficiaries.
  • Technical assistance delivery. Practical experience designing and delivering TA to MSMEs for business development or investment implementation, directly or through specialists managed by the firm. Tourism-sector experience is an advantage.
  • Organizational and managerial capacity. Experience mobilizing multidisciplinary teams and managing geographically dispersed operations. An existing office in Zambia is not required at EOI stage, but the firm must demonstrate capacity to mobilize an effective in-country operation.
  • Systems and controls. Capability to operate grant management informational system (MIS) and maintain audit trails, fiduciary and integrity controls, and environmental and social screening and monitoring procedures.
  • Donor financed and regional experience. Experience in World Bank or other development partner financed programs in the context of developing economies, especially in southern Africa.

Conflict of interest.

The attention of interested consultancy is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’ July 2016 revised 7th Edition 2025 [Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services], setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Joint venture or sub consultancy

Consultants may associate with other consultants in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications. The nature of association, whether it is a joint venture or a sub consultancy, should clearly be stated. In case of joint venture, the Consultant leading the joint venture should be mentioned.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN

CONNECTIVITY AND TRANSPORT SECTOR IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

Project ID: P509487

Assignment Title: Fit-gap analysis in the field of sustainable development, ESG reporting (SASB, IFRS 1/2), development of a decarbonization program, industrial safety, independent reporting certification, and obtaining an ESG rating

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-CTSI-1004-CS-QCBS-UTY-PM-05

The Republic of Uzbekistan has applied for financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) of the World Bank Group toward the cost of the Connectivity and Transport Sector Improvement Project (CTSIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the enhancement of the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices of JSC “O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari” and its Group entities, comprising a Double Materiality Assessment (DMA); assessment of sustainability-related financial risks and opportunities, including climate-related physical and transition risks and opportunities; an integrated ESG diagnostic covering governance, strategy, risk management, data and internal controls, and readiness for IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 reporting; targeted implementation of both ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems at three common operational sites, together with capacity transfer and tools for subsequent Group rollout; a Scope 1, Scope 2 and material Scope 3 GHG emissions inventory and an air pollutant emissions assessment for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 reporting years, and development of decarbonization and air pollutant emissions reduction programs; and preparation of a 2025 SASB-aligned Sustainability Report and a 2026 IFRS S1/S2-aligned Sustainability Report, together with strengthening of internal sustainability reporting readiness. The Services also include support for one initial engagement cycle with one ESG rating agency selected and contracted by the Client. The Client shall pay the agency’s fees; the Consultant shall not guarantee a particular rating outcome.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

JSC “O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari” (the “Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

1. At least 5 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving the preparation and/or assurance of sustainability reports under SASB, IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards and/or GRI Standards for companies in transport, infrastructure, utilities, energy, extractives, manufacturing or other asset-intensive sectors. The demonstrated experience shall include direct preparation of sustainability reports.

2. At least 4 comparable ESG diagnostic assignments completed during the last 5 years for companies in the above sectors. The experience shall cover governance, management systems, data, internal controls and disclosure processes, including at least two assignments involving IFRS S1/S2 readiness, implementation or reporting.

3. At least 3 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving climate-risk and opportunity assessments, scenario analysis and assessment of potential financial effects. At least 1 assignment shall involve infrastructure, industrial operations or other long-lived physical assets.

4. At least 5 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving Scope 1, Scope 2 and material Scope 3 GHG inventories under the GHG Protocol and/or ISO 14064-1, including decarbonization measures, target pathways or transition-planning inputs.

5. At least 2 comparable double materiality assessment completed during the last 5 years using ESRS requirements and EFRAG guidance.

6. At least 3 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving ISO 14001- and/or ISO 45001-aligned management systems. The combined experience shall cover both standards and include practical implementation, procedures and controls, training, internal audits, management review and corrective actions.

Experience providing ESG, sustainability, governance, climate or corporate transformation advice to state-owned enterprises, sovereign holding companies or public-sector entities will be considered a strong advantage. Railway-sector experience shall not be mandatory unless expressly specified for a particular role.

(Note: Consultants shall clearly describe relevant assignments, indicating the client, country, duration, scope of services, financing source, and role of the firm.)

The same assignment may satisfy more than one experience criterion where its scope, outputs and the relevant entity’s or expert’s role are clearly evidenced. Evidence may include completion certificates, acceptance acts, client references or equivalent contractual documentation. Anonymized evidence may be provided where confidentiality restrictions apply.

Relevant experience of joint venture members shall be assessed against their assigned roles. Specialized ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 experience may be demonstrated by a named sub-consultant where permitted by the procurement documents and supported by a substantive role and committed resources. Experience of an affiliated or network firm shall not be attributed automatically to the bidder; that entity’s formal participation, assigned responsibilities and committed resources shall be identified.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain 5 to 8 firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, as set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and as further detailed in the Request for Proposals (RFP).

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by November 30, 2026 12.00 o’clock (midday by Tashkent time). Late expressions of interest will be rejected.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Consulting Services for the Reengineering and Standardization of INEFOP's Main Processes and Procedures

CONSULTING SERVICES – QUALITY AND COST-BASED SELECTION (QCBS)

2.2.14./C-2.2.14/COMP.2/CS/INEFOP-2026

The Government of Angola, through the Ministry of Public Administration, Labor and Social Security (MAPTSS), via the National Institute of Employment and Vocational Training (INEFOP) and with the support of the World Bank, received funding of US$250 million for the implementation of the Angola Youth Employment and Opportunities Project (AYEOP/JOVEM+, P505158), approved by the World Bank Board of Directors on March 20, 2025, and intends to apply part of this funding to the contracting of consultancy services for the reengineering and standardization of INEFOP's main processes and procedures.

This consultancy aims to hire a specialized company or consortium to diagnose, redesign, standardize, and validate 18 mission, management, and support processes, based on quality management standards. These include processes for financial management, asset management, human resources management, customer service and service center management, information technology (IT), communication, and document management and archiving, as well as capacity building and an institutional adoption plan.

The consultancy is expected to be completed within nine (9) months from the start date of services, which is considered to be the time required to complete these tasks. The terms of reference can be obtained at the email address indicated below.

The Employment and Opportunities Project for Young People in Angola (AYEOP/JOVEM+) hereby invite eligible companies ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services, submitting their expressions of interest, certificates/diplomas and other supporting documents deemed necessary for the application.

The consultant must possess the following qualifications: a. A minimum of 5 years of experience and three completed projects of a comparable nature. The experience must demonstrate, collectively, process reengineering, institutional modernization, procedures, and quality management, with at least two projects in public institutions or service delivery networks of comparable size. At least one project must include the application of quality management benchmarks, and at least one must cover employment, vocational training, social services, or public services directed at citizens. The experience of the consortium members will be related to the proposed distribution of responsibilities. Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

 

The World Bank is supporting the Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh to better serve the poorest and most vulnerable populations by expanding coverage and strengthening delivery of the national social protection system for the poor through an IDA Credit of USD 200 million for the “Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience, Inclusion and Targeting (SSPIRIT)” project. Key features of the initiative include, i) establishment and roll out of a Dynamic Social Registry (DSR), which will act as a central platform to improve the accuracy and efficiency of identifying and supporting beneficiaries; ii) strengthening Institutional Capacity for service delivery; iii) enhancing benefits adequacy of allowance programs; iv) strengthening skills development and complementary services; and v) providing tailored livelihood support to vulnerable group.

 

DSS intends to utilize a part of this credit to hire a Safeguard Specialist as an individual national consultant to ensure effective management of the Project.

Qualifications & Experience

  1. At least a Master’s Degree from a reputed university in Environmental Management, Natural Resource Management, Sociology, or other Social Sciences;
  2. At least Seven (07) years of relevant operational ES experience and proven track record in working on projects covering a broad range of environmental and social management and development issues.
  3. Experience with World Bank projects would be preferred.
  4. Ability to think strategically and conduct dialogue on environmental and social development policies and priorities, while maintaining a strong sense of realism with regard to context, conditions and competing demands for resources;
  5. Experience of working with field level and local Government officials and local NGOs is highly desirable;
  6. Excellent spoken and written Bengali and English skills.

data.project_name: Regional Electricity Market Interconnectivity and Trade
data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

COUNTRY: Central Asia region (Republic of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Republic of Uzbekistan, Republic of Tajikistan)

NAME OF PROJECT: Central Asia Regional Electricity Market Interconnectivity and Trade Project (P509488)

                                                             Grant No.: D0247          

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to Design, Implement, and Maintain Central Asia Pilot Short-Term Electricity Market

Reference No. UZ-CDC ENERGIA-CS1-QCBS

The CDC "Energia" intends to procure consultancy services  ("the Services") including the Design, Implement, and Maintain Central Asia Pilot Short-Term Electricity Market, financed under the World Bank’s Regional Electricity Market Interconnectivity and Trade (REMIT) Project.

Objective

The objective of this assignment is to prepare the necessary legal agreements and documents to govern the operation of the Central Asian pilot market, develop and implement a trading platform for running the Central Asian pilot market and a settlement solution, implement the market, and provide pilot market operation as a service for a period of 24 months after system is operationalized, with an option for subsequent yearly extension of service if requested by the Client.

The consultancy will cover a pilot market for all Central Asia participating countries. Provision needs to be made by the consultant for future market products, and expansion in participating countries and market participants.

 

The expected commencement date for the assignment is May 2027. The duration of the assignment shall be 18 months for implementation (Phase 1) from the date of contract signature, plus 24 months of services for Central Asia .pilot market live operation (Phase 2), with an optional yearly extension of service thereafter.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link: https://udc.uz/request-for-expressions-of-interestconsulting-services-firms-selection/.

The Coordination Dispatch Center "Energia" (CDC "Energia") now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core Business (Areas of Expertise). The Consultant must demonstrate extensive and in-depth experience in power market design and advisory, power exchange, market operation, electricity trading and settlement platform provision.
  • Years in Business – The Firm must be minimum 5 years of business related to the assignment.
  • Experience in Similar Assignments. The Consultant must demonstrate experience in the fields of (i) design of day-ahead or short-term markets, including market rules, price formation and clearing algorithm, and cross-border capacity allocation ; (ii) delivery and go-live of trading and settlement platforms (iii) operation of a market as a service. For each project performed, the Consultant shall provide the name and contact address of the client (office and e-mail address and telephone number), date(s) of execution, name(s) of lead and associate firms, contract amount, and financing sources.
  • Technical and Managerial Capability. The Consultant must demonstrate competencies in:
    • Electricity market concepts and industry trends
    • Power system economics
    • Power market operations
    • System operations of interconnected power systems

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Further, the experience of a parent company, subsidiary company, group of companies, or associates of the firm shall not be considered in the evaluation.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The intended contract type with the selected Consultant for the 2 phases: Phase 1- lump-sum and Phase 2- time-based.

Further information can be obtained from CDC "Energia" at the address below.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by courier, or by e-mail) on or before November 30, 2026, at 15:00 hours – Tashkent time.

Expressions of Interest should be clearly marked: "EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR PROVISION OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO DESIGN, IMPLEMENT, AND MAINTAIN CENTRAL ASIA PILOT SHORT-TERM ELECTRICITY MARKET, REF. NO: UZ-CDC ENERGIA-CS1-QCBS".

Expressions of interest must be prepared in English and, if submitted electronically, should be sent in PDF format to the e-mail address mentioned below.

Note: CDC "Energia" is holding an online conference for potential Consultants before the EoI submission deadline. Consultants can use it to seek clarifications on the assignment. Details are below:

  • November 16, 2026, at 17:00 Tashkent time

Potential Consultants are welcome to participate. Consultants may request the link to the above session at the e-mail address below.

data.notice_text:
Government of Odisha

Department of Water Resources

 

 

Invitation for Expressions of Interest [EOI]

E-Procurement Notice

(Consulting Services – Firms Selection)

 

 

INDIA – Second Dam Rehabilitation and Improvement Project – Additional Financing (DRIP 2-AF)

Project ID: P170873

 

Consultancy Services for Construction Supervision and Quality Assurance of Works, including Detail Engineering Designs and Construction Drawings for the Construction of Additional Spillway of Hirakud Dam on Left of Gandhi Hillock including Drop Structure, End Structure and Spill Channel, Burla, Odisha, India.

 

STEP/Procurement Plan Reference Number: IN-ODISHA WRD-568132-CS-QCBS

 

  1. The Water Resources Department, Government of Orissa (hereinafter called the “Client”) through the Government of India (hereinafter called “Borrower”), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Consultancy Services for “Construction, Supervision and Quality Assurance of Works, including Review of Engineering Designs and Drawings for the Construction of Additional Spillway of Hirakud Dam on Left of Gandhi Hillock including Drop Structure, End Structure and Spill Channel, Burla, Odisha, India”, under the Dam Rehabilitation and Improvement Project-Additional Financing (DRIP 2-AF) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

  1. The Project Management Consulting Services (“the Services”) include:

 

  1. Carrying out the detailed design and preparation of Construction Drawings for various components of civil works and co-ordinate for obtaining approval of the Central Water Commission (CWC) of the Government of India.

 

  1. Reviewing and coordinating with regard to Hydro-mechanical works and associated electrical works for designs and drawings prepared by the Contractors and obtain approval from the CWC.

 

  1. Supervise and Monitor all Civil, Hydro Mechanical (HM) and Electrical Works (EW) and ensure quality control on behalf of Client including assistance in measurements, bill verification, and Contract management and administration.

 

  1. Supervise and monitor the environmental, social, health and safety (ESHS) of the project in accordance with the applicable project ESIA, ESMP, ESMF, SEF, ESCP and RAP, site-specific Stakeholder Engagement Plan, applicable World Bank Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), applicable Indian laws and regulations, and the conditions stipulated in the Environmental Clearance, Forest Clearance and other statutory approvals.

 

  1. Assist the Client in implementing and tracking the applicable ESCP commitments and other environmental and social obligations, including supervision of the Contractor’s Environmental and Social Management Plan, monitoring of non-compliances and corrective actions, and reporting of environmental and social compliance through Monthly and Quarterly Progress Reports.

 

  1. The likely duration of the assignment is 36 months.

 

  1. The tentative Terms of Reference (TOR) of the assignment can be downloaded from: - https://dowr.odisha.gov.in/en/projects-%26-schemes/projects/externally-aided-project/DRIP

 

  1. The Office of the Chief Engineer and Basin Manager, Mahanadi Basin, Burla, Odisha, India under the Water Resources Department, Government of Orissa, an implementing agency under the Second Dam Rehabilitation and Improvement Project – Additional Financing (DRIP 2-AF),now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

  1. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. General experience of the Consulting Firm: Minimum of fifteen years of experience prior to deadline for submission of EOI in providing Engineering Consulting services for Design, Construction Supervision and Quality Assurance for Large Dams including Hydro-mechanical and associated works to Government/Semi Government, Multilateral /Bilateral/ Private projects. The documentary evidence related to the legal status, nature of core business of firm, completed consulting assignments over the period shall be provided.
  2. Specific Experience of Consulting Firm relevant to the consulting assignment: The consulting firms should have experience of providing engineering consulting services including detailed design, preparation of construction drawings, construction supervision, and quality assurance service, including ensuring implementation of mitigation measures for identified Environment, Social, Health, Safety risks and adverse impacts; demonstrated through successfully completion of the consulting assignments as specified below during seven years prior to deadlines for submission of EOI as described below. Consultants are advised to submit comprehensive details of all relevant qualifying consulting assignments executed by them.
  1. Minimum one consulting assignment for dam spillway with minimum 5000 cumec as design discharge capacity for a commissioned and operating project including concrete dam and associated energy dissipation arrangements.
  2. Minimum one consulting assignment for an artificial channel/canal with minimum 200 cumec discharge capacity and outfall structures. The artificial channel / canal are defined as an artificially constructed, commissioned and operational hydraulic section of minimum 500-meter length.

Documentary Evidence: Firms should provide details of relevant assignments, including name and location of assignment, client, contract value, duration, scope of services, and the firm’s specific role and responsibilities. Key experts shall not be evaluated at shortlisting stage

 

  1. The consulting firms should have financial capabilities as specified below:
  1. The firm should have Minimum Average Annual Turnover of INR Fifty crores Or US $5.26 Million in preceding seven financial years. Documentary Evidence: The firm shall submit audited profit and loss statements duly certified by Charted Accountant for the same.
  2. The firm should have Minimum Average Annual Gross Income of INR Twelve crores Or US $1.26 Million in preceding seven financial years, received by providing similar engineering consulting services for construction of large dams and spillways. Documentary Evidence: The firm shall submit supporting certified statements of receipts for such assignments from Charted Accountant for the same.
  3. The firm should have Positive Net Worth of Minimum INR Twenty crores Or us $2.11 Million during preceding seven financial years.  Documentary Evidence: The firm shall submit audited balance sheets along with related financial statements certified by the Chartered Accountant.
  1. Technical and Managerial Capabilities: The consulting firm shall demonstrate its technical and managerial capabilities for the assignment and provide all relevant details including its organizational structure, availability of professional experts commensurate with key personnel requirement under assignment indicating number of key experts on their payroll available for the assignment. The firms having number of key experts as regular employees will be given higher weightage.

NOTE: Names/details of key experts are not required. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

  1. Interested consulting firms may download the Request for Expressions of Interest (REOI) document and the detailed indicative Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment, free of cost, from e-procurement system https://tendersodisha.gov.in/nicgep/app.The Consultants would be responsible for ensuring that any addenda available on the website is also downloaded and incorporated prior to the submission of Expressions of Interest (EOIs).

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and paragraph 3.32 “Fraud & Corruption” of the Regulations.

 

  1. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy.
