Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication

 

Terms of Reference

 

for

 

Project Manager

 

Micro Small Medium Enterprises (MSME) and Related Technical Assistance
World Bank / NRPB SPEAR Project – Sint Maarten

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Background and context

Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) constitute approximately 95% of all businesses in Sint Maarten and form the backbone of employment, entrepreneurship, and economic resilience. Recognizing their central role, the Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication (MinTEATT), through the Department of Economy, Transport and Telecommunication (ETT), is undertaking a comprehensive update of four (4) interrelated MSME-related policies, and the MSME institutional strengthening support programs. These two projects are being implemented under The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project, funded by the Government of the Netherlands through the Sint Maarten Reconstruction, Recovery, and Resilience Trust Fund (TF) administered through the World Bank and implemented through the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB)[1].   The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project is a strategic initiative led by the Government of Sint Maarten and the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB), with support from the Sint Maarten Trust Fund. It aims to enhance the operational effectiveness of recovery efforts and build long-term institutional resilience. The Trust Fund is governed by a tripartite Steering Committee composed of representatives from Sint Maarten, the Netherlands, and the World Bank, which allocates resources to short-, medium-and long-term recovery and capacity-building initiatives.  SPEAR has the following objectives:

  • Enhance the operational capacity and effectiveness of the National Recovery Program Bureau, and
  • Strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the Government of Sint Maarten to ensure sustainability of investments.

Scope of Work

This task falls within the second component of SPEAR.

  1. A Policy Consultant or firm is engaged to lead the development of four (4) policy documents: These policies form the foundation of Sint Maarten’s MSME business environment. Updating these policies is essential to reflect the current realities, economic conditions, and evolving dynamics of the local business climate—while also anticipating future needs. At the heart of these policy updates is the goal of fostering a supportive, enabling environment in which entrepreneurs and businesses can thrive and operate efficiently. These revisions aim to strike a thoughtful balance between encouraging economic activity and safeguarding the quality of life, ensuring that Sint Maarten remains a safe, vibrant, and sustainable place to live, work, and do business. The policies are:
  1. The National MSME Policy
  2. The Investment and Diversification Policy
  3. The Residential Economic Policy (REP)
  4. The Beach and Vending Policy

The policy revisions are intended to align and update these policies to reflect current day realities on Island. The update is expected to be informed by data-driven strategies including the proposed World Bank Enterprise Survey[2]. Such data along with the revised policy documents are essential to sustaining progress and achieving inclusive economic growth in the vital Medium Micro and Small Enterprise (MSME) sector in Sint Maarten.  Therefore, the updates, will be critical to ensure alignment between these operational aspects, policy development, MinTEATT priorities, and overall GoSXM priorities.

  1. In parallel to the policy revisions, MinTEATT has requested technical assistance from the ongoing Enterprise Support Project (ESP), funded by the same Trust Fund, to support the execution of the operational aspects of MSME programs. This assistance focuses on institutional strengthening of MSME related institutions including the Sint Maarten Entrepreneurship Development Center (SEDC) and the Chamber of Commerce (COCI). The MSME support areas are:  

 

  1. Governance and Oversight Framework: The objective is to strengthen the Ministry’s oversight and governance of MSME support
  2. Monitoring and Evaluation’ (M&E) framework: Development of an M&E framework for MSME support programs.
  3. Standard Operating procedures (SOPs): Establish SOPs for MSME support programs in key aspects to include basic business training, one-on-one business advisory, and business coaching.
  4. Funding mechanisms for MSME support programs.

Terms of reference for these activities are being developed.

Role of the Project Manager

The Project Manager will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the SPEAR Project policy development and the ESP MSME institutional strengthening support programs components. This responsibility includes coordinating with the Policy Consultant and other Consultants hired through ESP, managing project workflow, coordinating with Min TEATT/ETT, facilitating stakeholder engagement and ensuring compliance with all project requirements.   The Project Manager will also be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day execution of the project process; maintaining project timelines; ensuring compliance with Government of Sint Maarten requirements; and facilitating the successful delivery of all project outputs. In this role, the project manager shall organize and supervise the identification, formulation, approval, implementation and completion of all activities under the component and liaise with the Project Implementation Unit at the Ministry of Finance (SPEAR) and National Recovery Program Bureau (ESP). Functional responsibilities for the role include:

  1. Project Management and Coordination
  2. Communication with Relevant Stakeholders
  3. Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation
  4. Oversight and Quality Management

Under the supervision of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Finance for overall project coordination and administrative oversight, and of the Ministry of TEATT, through ETT, for policy direction and substantive technical oversight, the Project Manager is expected to perform the following tasks. ETT will guide the policy content, review and validate project outputs, and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s priorities, with final policy approval remaining with the competent authorities:

Project Management and Coordination

  • Oversee the execution of the policy development update process and the development of MSME Support Programs ensuring that activities, deliverables and timelines across both workstreams progress in line with approved plans
  • Coordinate with Policy Consultants to monitor the project’s progress, address challenges, and ensure alignment with project objectives and timelines.
  • Facilitate and participate in regular project meetings with MinTEATT/ETT, NRPB, Ministry of Finance, the Policy Consultant and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Work directly with project counterparts and relevant stakeholders to ensure deliverables fall within the applicable scope and budget. This will involve coordinating with departments within the Government as well as external counterparts, including NRPB, to ensure all aspects of each project are compatible and to clarify specific requirements of each project.
  • Ensure project milestones are achieved on-time and that deliverables meet the required quality standards.
  • Identify and manage project risks, developing mitigation strategies as needed.
  • Manage the project budget, track expenditures and ensure allocated resources are used in accordance with approved plans.
  • Participate as a member of the bid evaluation team during the contracting process.
  • Support the selection of new project staff or consultants as needed.
  • Support the revision process of operational project documents (e.g., project operations manual, procurement plan, and environmental and social management plan), as needed. Participate and/or lead technical meetings with agency counterparts and project participant
  • Regularly supervise and report on project execution progress and budget performance
  • Assist with the preparation of progress reports and actionable information as required by Government to support its reporting commitments to the Council of Ministers, the Trust Fund Steering Committee and the World Bank, as needed.
  • Any other task related to this function that will contribute to the objectives of the project

Communication with Relevant Stakeholders

  • Facilitate communication among government counterparts, NRPB/WB and private sector stakeholders
  • Provide contributions to press releases related to project activities, as needed
  • Consolidate and track feedback and recommendations from stakeholders and develop response matrices with the Policy Consultant.
  • Ensure timely reporting, briefing notes, and updates to the Ministry of Finance and other governing bodies as required.

Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation

  • Monitor Policy Consultant’s deliverables and work quality, ensuring it adheres to the TOR, timelines and quality standards.
  • Prepare and submit progress reports to relevant stakeholders where applicable (MinTEATT/ ETT, Ministry of Finance World Bank)
  • Submit necessary reports on delays and mitigation strategies/ corrective actions to relevant stakeholders (MinTEATT/ETT, Ministry of Finance, World Bank).
  • With the applicable PIUs (MoF, NRPB) provide inputs to address any complaints submitted through the projects’ Grievance Redress Mechanism (https://nrpbsxm.org/complaints-procedure)
  • Prepare and provide input on SPEAR and Institutional strengthening project required reports.

Consultant Oversight and Quality Management

  • Review Policy Consultant’s inception reports, providing feedback and ensuring alignment with project objectives and MinTEATT/ETT priorities.
  • Review all Annotated Policy Outlines (MSME policy, REP, Investment & Diversification Policy, Beach & Vending Policy), coordinating feedback from MinTEATT and ensuring coherence across the four policies.
  • Review all annotated outlines for the MSME institutional strengthening program support documents to assess quality, identify gaps and ensure that they meet technical and operational standards
  • Conduct quality checks of all policy documents ensuring alignment with Governing Program and National Development Plans (and other applicable documents).
  • Facilitate review and approval processes for all consultant deliverables, coordinating feedback from the  Department Head of ETT, Secretary General, Minister TEATT and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure deliverables submitted are timely and are of professional standard, and incorporate stakeholders input where necessary.
  • Work with the Policy Consultant to assess stakeholder feedback, address identified gaps and incorporate feedback agreed upon by TEATT into the final documents and capacity-building materials. Document the reasons for not incorporating substantive stakeholder comments
  • Verify that consultants’ invoices are supported by appropriate reports, deliverables documentation and evidence of work completed.  

Any other tasks related to the function that will ensure successful completion of the SPEAR Project policy development and the Institutional Strengthening components

 

  • Final Project Completion Report- Documentation of the project including activities, results achieved, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations for implementation and future work.
  • Transition report- Handover documentation including all relevant information for smooth transition and continued implementation.
  • Budget execution reports, stakeholder coordination logs
  • Policy Documents (4),
  • MSME Institutional Strengthening documents (3),

Contract Arrangements and Reporting

The contract duration will be twelve (12) months, from contract signing, with the possibility to extend until June 2028. The successful candidate is expected to reside in Sint Maarten/Saint Martin to support the effective organization and execution of the work and ensure continuous engagement with public sector agencies and local stakeholders.

The Project Manager will report to the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Finance for project administration, financial management and compliance and work in close collaboration with the Department of Economic Transportation and Telecommunication (ETT) for substantive technical oversight, policy direction and review of deliverables

Qualifications and Experience

Minimum Requirements

  • At least a bachelor’s degree in public policy, economics, business administration, project management, or another relevant field.
  • At least 5 years of experience in project management, preferably in the public sector or development projects.
  • Demonstrated skills in results-based project planning, monitoring, and management.
  • Experience coordinating multi-stakeholder processes and facilitating consultation workshops.
  • Prior experience working in Sint Maarten or the Caribbean region.

 

Preferred Requirements

  • A master’s degree in a relevant field is a plus.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
  • Experience with MSME development, private sector development, or economic policy projects is a plus.
  • Proficiency in Dutch (spoken and written) is a plus.

 

General Competencies

  • Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities simultaneously.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to anticipate challenges and develop effective solutions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including report writing, presentation, and facilitation abilities.
  • Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, with demonstrated ability to build relationships and coordinate across diverse groups.
  • Computer literate with high proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project) and project management software.

 

[1]   Which is supporting implementation of the Enterprise Support Project (ESP), funded by the Sint Maarten Recovery and Resilience Trust Fund. ESP’s objective is to support the recovery of and increase resilience of existing and new micro, small, and medium sized enterprises in Sint Maarten.

 

[2]   The Enterprise Survey (ES) is a nationally representative firm-level survey with top managers and owners of businesses in over 160 economies (to reach 180 in upcoming years) that measures businesses’ major constraints, performance (including job creation), and characteristics including innovation and technology, market linkages, access to finance, infrastructure, and more. ES’s comprehensive data and analytical reports enable easy comparisons across economies and time.

Mr. Shervin Frederick,  Email address:  Shervin.Frederick@sintmaartengov.org     AND

Mrs. Avril Isaac,            Email address:  Avril.Isaac@sintmaartengov.org

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Syrian Arab Republic

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516)

Grant No.: E6410-SY

Assignment Title: Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component (Sub-Component 2.2)

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SY-MOF-547078-CS-INDV

The Ministry of Finance of the Syrian Arab Republic (the “Employer”) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the services of a Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component (Sub-Component 2.2), who will provide high-level strategic leadership and policy direction to the Government of Syria in the design, sequencing, and oversight of the public procurement reform program under the Project, with a view to establishing a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with international best practices.

The Technical Lead will lead and coordinate implementation of the procurement reform activities under Sub-Component 2.2 - the new public procurement legal and regulatory framework (replacing the Uniform System of Contracts Law No. 51 (2004)), standard bidding documents, the Single Procurement Portal (SPP), an independent procurement complaints and review system, and the national procurement professionalization and capacity-development program, advising the Ministry of Finance and relevant stakeholders, coordinating with government entities, development partners and the World Bank Task Team, overseeing implementation progress and risk management, and leading the results framework for procurement reform, including key performance indicators and milestones. The assignment will be for an initial period of one (1) year, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance and project requirements (the contract may be extended to cover the full duration of the Project).

The Technical Lead will work under the overall guidance of the Project Coordinator and the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit (PFMRCU) within the Ministry of Finance, and will closely coordinate with relevant government entities, the Syria External Assistance Fiduciary Section (SEAFS) and the World Bank Task Team.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Ministry of Finance (through the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit - PFMRCU) now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms' staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

  1. postgraduate qualifications in procurement, law, public administration, engineering, economics, or a related field, and at least ten (10) years of relevant professional management-focused experience;
  2. proven successful experience in leading and managing technical assistance projects financed by international donors;
  3. experience in public procurement, including demonstrated experience in procurement reform, development of legal and regulatory frameworks, and institutional strengthening (highly desirable);
  4. advanced leadership skills in organizational change and development, with the ability to introduce critical reforms in complex organizational and contextual structures, including in Fragile and Conflict-affected Situations (FCS);
  5. proven experience in coordinating, cooperating and negotiating with high-level government officials, donor partners and multiple local stakeholders; and
  6. fluency in Arabic and English.

 

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers [insert correct title and date of applicable Regulations edition as per the financing agreement] (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the following email address: syriapfmprocurement@gmail.com by 5PM on 30 November 2026 Damascus time.

 

Attn: Project Coordinator

Ministry of Finance

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project

Joul Jammal Street, P.O. Box 13136

Damascus, Syrian Arab Republic

E-mail: syriapfmprocurement@gmail.com

 

 

=======================================================================

 

Terms of Reference (TOR)

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516)

Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component

 

Project Background

  1. Syria is making progress in its transition towards stabilization, recovery, and reintegration, while continuing to face major challenges after 14 years of conflict. More than one year after the December 2024 political transition, the new Syrian government under the leadership of President Al-Sharaa has maintained overall political stability. Modest economic growth is projected for 2025 and 2026, and Syria has benefitted from the lifting of major economic sanctions and renewed participation in international financial systems and investment discussions. At the same time, the security situation remains fragile, with occasional outbreaks of violence, and the country faces massive development challenges and continued humanitarian needs. Continued international engagement and financing will be critical to support Syria in its post-conflict transition. 
  2. Sound management of public funds and transparency about their use are prerequisites for the Syrian state to gain the trust of its citizens and the international community as it seeks to mobilize resources and deliver services to the population. Fourteen years of conflict and economic mismanagement have weakened the capacity and legitimacy of Syria’s state institutions. A disciplined and transparent approach to public financial management (PFM) will be a critical foundation for Syria’s path to recovery and development. The Ministry of Finance has identified support for PFM reforms as a priority, highlighting the immediate need to update the relevant legal framework, rebuild human capital for core government functions, advance digitalization, and establish accountability and transparency. Sound management of public funds will also be needed to mobilize external assistance for the country’s massive reconstruction needs, with expectations from the international community of adequate oversight of reconstruction investments, payroll, and the flow of funds to provide these resource flows.
  3. The Syrian Arab Republic has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing for services of a Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component. The project components/sub-components are shown in Table 1. Full details are available in the Project Appraisal Document (PAD).

Table 1: Summary of project components/sub-components

 

  1. Within this context, Component 2 of the Project focuses on improving the efficiency and effectiveness of essential PFM and procurement functions. A key sub-component (Sub-component 2.2) is dedicated to public procurement reform, which aims to establish a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with good international practices. This includes the development of a new procurement legal framework, introduction of standard bidding documents, establishment of a Single Procurement Portal (SPP), strengthening of complaint handling mechanisms, and development of procurement professionalization programs.
  2. The current procurement system, governed by the Uniform System of Contracts Law No. 51 (2004), presents several structural gaps and limitations, including weaknesses in competition, transparency, complaints review, and the absence of modern e-procurement systems.

 

Objective of the Assignment

  1. The objective of this assignment is to provide high-level strategic leadership and policy direction to the Government of Syria in the design, sequencing, and oversight of the public procurement reform program under the Project, with a view to establishing a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with international best practices.

The Technical Lead will guide the reform agenda at the institutional and policy level, ensure coherence across reform pillars, and support sustainable capacity development and ownership by government institutions.

Tasks and Responsibilities

  1. The Technical Lead for Public Procurement Reform Component will be responsible for leading and coordinating the implementation of the public procurement reform activities under the Project and providing advisory support to the Ministry of Finance and relevant stakeholders.

In particular, the Lead will undertake the following tasks:

  1. Strategic Leadership and Reform Direction:
  • Provide overall vision, leadership, and strategic direction for the public procurement reform program, ensuring alignment with national priorities and international good practices.
  • Define and guide the sequencing and prioritization of reform initiatives, taking into account institutional readiness and the FCV context.
  • Advise senior government leadership on policy options, reform trade-offs, and implementation risks.

 

  1. Procurement Legal and Regulatory Reform:
  • Lead the strategic design and oversight of the new public procurement legal and regulatory framework, ensuring coherence, applicability, and sustainability.
  • Oversee the work of technical teams responsible for drafting legislation and regulations and ensure quality assurance and policy consistency.
  • Facilitate high-level consultations and consensus-building among key stakeholders to support adoption of the reform framework.

 

  1. Digital Transformation and System Modernization
  • Provide strategic guidance on the development and implementation of the Single Procurement Portal (SPP) as a cornerstone for transparency and efficiency.
  • Ensure that digital solutions are aligned with broader public financial management systems and government digital strategies.
  • Oversee high-level design decisions to ensure sustainability, interoperability, and scalability of systems.

 

  1. Complaint Handling and Oversight Mechanisms:
  • Lead the strategic design of an independent and credible procurement complaints and review system.
  • Ensure that oversight mechanisms are aligned with principles of fairness, transparency, and due process, and are institutionally sustainable.

 

  1. Capacity Development and Professionalization Strategy
  • Provide strategic guidance on the development of a national procurement professionalization framework, including certification pathways and institutional arrangements.
  • Oversee the design of capacity development programs to ensure long-term institutional strengthening, rather than short-term training delivery.
  • Promote a culture of professionalism and ethical standards in the procurement function across government.

 

  1. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination
  • Act as a key interlocutor with senior government officials, development partners, and other stakeholders on procurement reform matters.
  • Ensure effective coordination across ministries, agencies, and donor-supported initiatives to avoid fragmentation and duplication.
  • Support the Government in articulating and communicating the reform agenda to build broad-based ownership.

 

  1.  Implementation Oversight and Risk Management
  • Provide strategic oversight of implementation progress, ensuring that reform activities remain aligned with objectives and timelines.
  • Identify key implementation risks and bottlenecks and advise on mitigation measures at the policy and institutional levels.
  • Guide pilot initiatives and scale-up decisions from a strategic perspective.

 

  1. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Results Orientation
  • Lead the development of a results framework for procurement reform, including key performance indicators and milestones.
  • Oversee monitoring and evaluation processes to ensure evidence-based decision-making and adaptive management.
  • Provide high-level reporting and strategic insights to inform the Government and the World Bank on reform progress.

 

Deliverables

  1. The overall deliverable is the successful and timely implementation of the project activities as contained in Sub-Component 2.2 under the project.  The Technical lead will also be expected to achieve smooth, effective, and efficient disbursement of the budget allocated for Sub-Component 2.2. Specific delivery includes work programs, budgets, procurement plan and periodic progress and delivered as they fall due.

 

Duration of the Assignment

  1. The assignment will be for an initial period of one (1) year, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance and project requirements. The contract may be extended to cover the full duration of the Project.

 

 

Institutional Arrangements

  1. The Technical Lead will work under the overall guidance of the Project Coordinator and the PFM Reform Coordinating Unit (PFMRCU) within the Ministry of Finance and will closely coordinate with relevant government entities, the Syria External Assistance Fiduciary Section (SEAFS), and the World Bank Task Team.

 

Qualification and Experience Requirements

  • The suitable candidate for appointment must hold postgraduate qualifications in procurement, law, public administration, engineering, economics, or a related field, and at least ten (10) years of relevant professional managementfocused experience.

 

  • Proven successful experience in leading and managing Technical Assistance projects financed by international donors.

 

  • Experience in public procurement, including demonstrated experience in procurement reform, development of legal and regulatory frameworks, and institutional strengthening is highly desirable.

 

  • Candidate must possess excellent interpersonal skills, strong oral and written communication skills, problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, with the ability to succeed in evolving Fragile, Conflict, and Violence (FCV) environment. be proficient in the use of the computer.
  • Advance leadership skills in organizational change and development with the ability to introduce critical reforms in complex organizational/contextual structures.
  • Proven experience in coordinating, cooperating and negotiating with high level Government officials, donor partners and multitude of local stakeholders.
  • Excellent Knowledge in International management Standard for Quality management System, Health & Safety Management System, Environmental Management System, Business Continuity Management System, Information Security Management System.
  • Fluent in Arabic and English.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE PREPARATION AND IMPLEMENTATION SUPERVISION OF A RESETTLEMENT ACTION PLAN FOR THE BANSARA IRRIGATION SCHEME, CROSS RIVER STATE

    1. Background & Assignment Description

The Cross River State Government of Nigeria has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The assignment ensures that all land acquisition, physical displacement, and economic disruption caused by the irrigation infrastructure are identified, mitigated, and compensated in strict alignment with both Nigerian statutory laws and the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Standard 5 (ESS5) on Involuntary Resettlement.

Key Operational Objectives

     2. Ensure Full Compensation and Livelihood Restoration

      3. Establish Governance, Transparency, and Digital Tracking

The State Project Implementation Unit (SPIU) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-2.6--4-R – Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

GPE TF0D0613

 

Assignment Title: Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

No. LEARN-2.6--4-R

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest. The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 01, 2026.

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

Contract No. LEARN-2.6-CC-4-R

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project

GPE TF0D0613

I. Background

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln  provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675.9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, a Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (Loan No. K019-UA) in the amount of $286 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

II. Objective

The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources.

III. Scope of services

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Analyze the current system of budgetary and strategic planning within the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES), including the application of the program-based budgeting approach;
  • Analyze the alignment of budget programs with strategic objectives and national policy priorities in the education and science sector;
  • Develop recommendations for aligning strategic documents (strategies, operational plans) with MoES budget programs;
  • Ensure integration of strategic objectives and priorities into the budget process (including preparation of budget requests, budget program passports, and reporting);
  • Contribute to the improvement of the structure of budget programs, performance indicators, and effectiveness metrics;
  • Support medium-term budget planning in line with strategic documents;
  • Provide methodological support on the application of the program-based budgeting approach within MoES;
  • Coordinate with the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine on budget planning and alignment of budget programs;
  • Provide methodological and analytical support for public expenditure reviews in relevant MoES sectors;
  • Develop proposals for implementing recommendations from expenditure reviews and ensure their incorporation into future budget planning cycles;
  • Support the implementation of results-based management approaches in the budget process;
  • Assess the effectiveness of MoES budget programs;
  • Prepare analytical materials on the efficiency of public expenditure and achievement of results.

Expected Deliverables:

  • Regular reports on the progress of aligning budgetary and strategic planning;
  • Analytical notes on the effectiveness of budget programs and their alignment with strategic objectives;
  • Proposals for improving the MoES budget process:

consulting and practical support to the Ministry of Education and Science in implementing results-oriented management approaches;

conducting analysis and assessment of the efficiency and effectiveness of budget programs of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine;

  • Analyze the implementation of previously provided recommendations and their impact on MoES budget indicators in the medium term, including collection and systematization of recommendations provided by the Accounting Chamber, the State Audit Service, and expenditure reviews conducted during the previous three years, as well as assessment of their implementation status.

 

IV. Reporting

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Project Co-Coordinator and work in coordination with the Deputy Ministers of Education and Science of Ukraine, relevant MoES directorates, and project managers involved in the implementation of Project activities. On operational matters, the Consultant shall cooperate with the Head of the World Bank Operations Management Team.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports to Project coordinator / Project Co-coordinator in hard copy. The reports shall include a description of services provided during the reporting period.

 

V. Provided resources

 

MoES shall provide the Consultant with the information necessary to carry out his/her assignment in a timely manner. MoES may provide the Consultant with a workplace, including necessary equipment to carry out his/her functions (e.g. PC, communications and office equipment).

 

VI.  Qualification requirements

 

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

 

  • Master’s degree or higher in finance, economics, accounting, or taxation;
  • At least 5 years of professional experience in public financial management or related areas;
  • Experience in strategic planning and alignment of budget programmes with sectoral policies.
  • Fluency in Ukrainian;
  • Proficiency in English at a minimum level of B1.

 

Desirable skills and qualifications:

  • Experience in effective communication among different government authorities;
  • Experience working with reforms or policies in the education and/or science sector;
  • Skills in using analytical tools and basic data visualization tools;
  • Experience in drafting regulatory/legal acts;

 

VII.  Period and location of employment

The Consultant shall provide his/her services until October 30, 2027. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine during the Project financing period.

The Consultant is expected to provide services under this Agreement on an ongoing basis throughout its term at a level of engagement equivalent to full-time employment, to the extent necessary to properly perform the tasks specified in the Terms of Reference.

The Consultant shall provide services primarily in Kyiv, Ukraine, and may take business trips to other regions of Ukraine to support implementation of the Project.

The Consultant is expected to be able to provide services remotely, but at the MOES request must arrive and/or provide services at the MOES premises as soon as possible.

VIII. Application package

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org, maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua indicating the email subject: «LEARN-2.6-CC-4-R: Selection of the Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert 2 (Budget Planning): [NAME]».

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 01, 2026.

If the candidate fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the candidate’s application.
